t: bun test --coverage emits DA records (DA:<line>,0) for comment-only and blank lines
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What is the problem?
When a source file is loaded but a function is never executed, bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov emits DA:<line>,0 records for lines that are comment-only or blank, not just executable lines.
LCOV DA records are meant for executable lines. Stamping comment/blank lines makes those lines appear as "uncovered code" in downstream tools — for example, codecov reports them as uncoverable, producing a false-red when several such all-zero coverage chunks are merged (union) into a combined report.
Minimal reproduction
mod.ts:
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  // this is a comment line that is never executed

  return a + b;
}
load-only.test.ts:
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
import * as mod from "./mod.ts";
test("imports the module but never calls add", () => {
  expect(typeof mod.add).toBe("function");
});
Run:
bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov --coverage-dir=cov load-only.test.ts

cov/lcov.info contains:
SF:mod.ts
FNF:1
FNH:0
DA:1,0
DA:2,0   <- comment line
DA:3,0   <- blank line
LF:3
LH:0
end_of_record

Line 2 (a comment) and line 3 (a blank line) receive DA records, while the actual executable return (line 4) does not.
What should happen instead?
Comment-only and blank lines should not receive DA records — they are not executable. Only executable lines should appear in DA / LF / LH.
Related
Possibly related to #12095 (lcov results differ from CLI).

t: new tls.TLSSocket(socket, { isServer: true }) never asks for a client certificate unless ca is also set, even with requestCert: true
b:
Relationship to #33924
I filed #33924 earlier and it was correctly closed as not planned. That report's central claim - that Bun should auto-close the connection when an untrusted client certificate is presented to a bare new tls.TLSSocket({ isServer: true }) - was wrong. robobun checked this against real Node.js and showed Node doesn't auto-close there either; that auto-reject logic lives specifically in tls.createServer()'s connection listener, not in the TLSSocket constructor. I independently confirmed this by reading Node's actual current source (lib/internal/tls/wrap.js, onServerSocketSecure, wired only by tlsConnectionListener) and tracing it back to a 2013 commit, so that part of the discussion is settled and I'm not reopening it.
While verifying that, I found a separate, narrower bug in the same code area that robobun's investigation didn't touch, because their test always included a ca option. This report is about that bug specifically. It has nothing to do with auto-closing connections.
What steps will reproduce the bug?
new tls.TLSSocket(socket, options) accepts requestCert as a documented option. From Node's own docs (doc/api/tls.md, current main, under new tls.TLSSocket(socket[, options])):

requestCert: Whether to authenticate the remote peer by requesting a certificate. Clients always request a server certificate. Servers (isServer is true) may set requestCert to true to request a client certificate.

Nothing in that sentence, or anywhere else in the option's documentation, conditions it on a ca option also being present. Bun's own TLSOptions.requestCert doc says the same thing, independently, for Bun's own Bun.listen/upgradeTLS surface (packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts:4018-4023):

If set to true, the server requests a client certificate.
Default is false.

On Bun, a standalone new tls.TLSSocket(rawSocket, { isServer: true, requestCert: true, key, cert }) with no ca option never requests a certificate at all. The client can present one, but the server's getPeerCertificate() comes back empty, as if requestCert had never been set.
I traced this to src/js/node/tls.ts. The TLSSocket constructor never reads options.requestCert into this._requestCert for a bare isServer: true socket - only tls.createServer()'s own Server() constructor does that (at src/js/node/tls.ts:1382-1385). So this._requestCert stays undefined for this path regardless of what's passed to the constructor, and [buntls] (src/js/node/tls.ts:1187-1209) hands requestCert: undefined to

t: TranspilerJob lives inside the VM allocation, so a pool-thread transpile racing worker.terminate() reads freed memory
b:
What
A TranspilerJob that is still on the work pool when its owning worker VM is terminated reads freed memory, because the job itself is stored inside the VirtualMachine allocation.

RuntimeTranspilerStore.store is a HiveArrayFallback<TranspilerJob, 64> (src/jsc/RuntimeTranspilerStore.rs:394) embedded by value in VirtualMachine.transpiler_store; the first 64 slots are an inline array inside the VM allocation (heap-fallback boxes are used only beyond that).
TranspilerJob::run() executes on the work-pool thread and dereferences (*self.vm) throughout (generation check, a ptr::read of the whole Transpiler, bun_watcher, macro_mode, ...).
WebWorker::shutdown() frees the VM allocation. For an inline-slot job that is self itself, so every self.* access afterwards is a use-after-free, including the schedule-time vm_handle that the checked enqueue in dispatch_to_main_thread reads.

Reachable via a worker that performs a dynamic import() (the module-load path schedules the transpile on the pool) and is terminate()d while the job is in flight.
Why the checked-enqueue pattern cannot close this one
#32071 routes cross-thread completions through a live-VM registry so producers never touch a freed VM. That works when the producer's own state lives outside the VM allocation. Here the job storage is inside the allocation, so the handle the check needs is itself freed; the registry gate in dispatch_to_main_thread (added in #32071) narrows the window for heap-fallback slots and makes a garbage generation overwhelmingly likely to fail the match, but it is not a guarantee, and run()'s body reads happen before the gate either way. This is pre-existing behavior; #32071 strictly narrows exposure for this producer.
Possible fixes (structural)

Move the job storage out of the VM allocation, e.g. Box the HiveArrayFallback (or the whole RuntimeTranspilerStore) and give it its own lifetime, freed only after the pool quiesces. The schedule-time vm_handle then lives in memory that survives VM teardown, and run()'s (*vm) reads can be gated on the registry check.
Or have WebWorker::shutdown() wait for in-flight transpiler jobs (a per-VM in-flight counter joined before dealloc(VirtualMachine)).

Same limitation shape as #33313 (a pre-existing cross-thread access that the registry approach narrows but cannot fully close without structural change). Spotted in review of #32071.

b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.6 (also reproduced on 1.3.14)
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (WSL2)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
@typescript/typescript6 is the package Microsoft ships so that tooling needing the TypeScript 6.0 programmatic API (e.g. typescript-eslint) keeps working while tsc is upgraded to the native TypeScript 7 compiler — see the official TypeScript 7.0 announcement. It is meant to be installed under the name typescript via an npm alias. Internally it re-exports the real TS6 through a dependency @typescript/old whose spec is npm:typescript@^6.
Minimal repro:
// package.json
{
  "name": "alias-of-alias-repro",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "npm:@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2"
  }
}
bun install
bun -e "const ts=require('typescript'); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.Extension)"
What is the expected behavior?
require('typescript') returns the working TS6 API, as it does with npm:
$ npm install && node -e "const ts=require('typescript'); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.Extension)"
6.0.3 object

What do you see instead?
Under bun the module is empty:
$ bun install && bun -e "const ts=require('typescript'); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.Extension)"
undefined undefined

Root cause
@typescript/typescript6 depends on @typescript/old = npm:typescript@^6 (the real TypeScript 6). bun resolves that dependency to @typescript/typescript6@6.0.2 itself instead of the real typescript@6: @typescript/typescript6 is already hoisted under the name typescript, its version 6.0.2 satisfies ^6, and bun reuses it despite the package name being different (@typescript/typescript6 ≠ typescript).
Visible directly in bun.lock:
"@typescript/old": ["@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2", "", { "dependencies": { "@typescript/old": "npm:typescript@^6" }, "bin": { "tsc6": "bin/tsc6" } }, "sha512-…"],

and on disk node_modules/@typescript/old/package.json has "name": "@typescript/typescript6" (should be typescript). So @typescript/typescript6 ends up require()-ing itself through @typescript/old, yielding an empty module and a broken TS API. npm resolves @typescript/old to the real typescript@6 and works correctly.
Additional information
Impact: this blocks the officially-recommended TypeScript 7 coexistence path (@typescript/typescript6) for every bun project — typescript-eslint (and anything using the programmatic TS API) crashes at load under bun once tsc is on TS7. The same package set installs and works correctly with npm.

t: install: integrity verification keeps only the first digest of the strongest algorithm (ssri any-match)
b:
When a package's integrity string carries more than one digest of the same algorithm (legal SSRI, e.g. sha512-A sha512-B), bun install verifies the tarball against the first one only. npm's ssri picks the strongest algorithm and then accepts a match on any digest of that algorithm (W3C SRI §3.3.4), so a tarball matching B passes npm and hard-fails Bun, and the outcome depends on entry order, which the spec makes irrelevant.
#33072 changed Integrity::parse to split a multi-entry SSRI string and keep the strongest algorithm. Before that, a multi-entry string decayed to Tag::UNKNOWN and verification was skipped, so #33072 is a strict improvement; it just over-tightens on this one shape. The deviation is noted in that PR's description.
Why it isn't a one-liner
Integrity is a fixed 65-byte value (tag: u8 + [u8; 64]) that lives on disk:

src/install/npm.rs PackageVersion.integrity (binary manifest cache)
src/install/lockfile/Package/Meta.rs Meta.integrity (lockfile)

All parse sites (npm.rs, bun.lock.rs, migration.rs, pnpm.rs, yarn.rs) call Integrity::parse on the raw string and store the single result; the raw string is discarded. By the time verification runs (extract_tarball.rs / TarballStream.rs via integrity::Streaming), only that single digest is available, so holding a bounded set in Streaming::init alone doesn't reach; the extra digests are already gone.
Scope of a fix
Carry every digest of the strongest algorithm through to verify time. Roughly:

widen what the manifest cache stores (variable-size, or a small fixed cap) and bump CacheVersion::CURRENT
Meta.integrity can stay single-digest for bun.lock (we write the digest that matched), but the migration/package-lock/pnpm/yarn parse paths need the full set until the tarball is verified
Streaming/verify_by_tag compare against each
test: two sha512- entries where the tarball matches the second

npm publishes exactly one digest per algorithm, so the trigger is rare (hand-edited lockfiles, third-party registries, or migrated lockfiles that already carry the shape), but the failure mode is a hard integrity error on a tarball npm accepts.
Originated from the src/install/integrity.rs review thread on #33072.

t: Proposal for Qwen 4: Context-Reset Multi-Agent Evaluation & Learn-From-Mistakes Pipeline
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Current LLM evaluation and training pipelines suffer from context-dependent scoring illusions and static knowledge limitations. Models evaluated in shared-context multi-turn chats exhibit sycophancy, attention drift, and groupthink, leading to inflated benchmark scores that don’t reflect real-world robustness. Additionally, pretraining on internet-scraped data teaches what is but not what was wrong and how it was fixed. This results in models that are statistically competent but lack dynamic self-correction capabilities, causing failures in agentic/tool-use scenarios (e.g., Claude Opus 4.7 Adaptive scoring only 49 on Tool Use despite high overall benchmarks).
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Implement a Context-Reset Multi-Agent Evaluation Pipeline combined with a Learn-From-Mistakes Training Data Integration:
Evaluation: Replace single-agent or shared-context multi-agent benchmarks with isolated agents that reset context per turn. Aggregate results via consensus/outlier detection to measure true robustness over context-dependent performance.
Training: Curate a high-signal dataset of production errors + verified fixes (not just raw web text). Use asymptotic error reduction signals from later training stages to distill the model’s true capability ceiling into the next version. Prioritize this error-fix data over generic internet scrapes for alignment and reasoning fine-tuning.
This shifts the paradigm from brute-force parameter scaling to intelligent, self-correcting iteration — mirroring expert cybersecurity practices where sandboxed testing and vulnerability remediation logs drive security more effectively than raw code volume.
What alternatives have you considered?
Larger parameter counts / more internet data: Already proven inefficient; Qwen3.7 Max outperforms larger models like Claude Opus 4.7 via smarter architecture, not scale.
Shared-context multi-agent evaluation: Prone to groupthink and bias propagation; fails to isolate individual agent reasoning.
RLHF-only alignment: Optimizes for safety/compliance over functionality; leads to tool-use paralysis (e.g., Opus 4.7 Adaptive).
Static benchmark leaderboards: Measure test-taking ability, not real-world adaptability; no feedback loop to training.
None of these address the core issue: models need to learn from their own verified mistakes in an isolated, context-independent manner to achieve genuine robustness.
Note This is for upcom

t: fetch()/WebSocket: passing a URL object as the whole `proxy` option is silently ignored — the request goes DIRECT with no error
b:
What version of Bun is running?
Current main. Long-standing.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
const origin = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response("FROM_ORIGIN") });
const prox   = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response("FROM_PROXY") });
const target = `http://127.0.0.1:${origin.port}/`;
console.log(await (await fetch(target, { proxy: `http://127.0.0.1:${prox.port}` })).text());   // string
console.log(await (await fetch(target, { proxy: prox.url })).text());                          // URL object
Note Bun.serve().url is itself a URL — proxy: server.url is about the most natural spelling.
What is the expected behavior?
Both lines print FROM_PROXY, or the second one throws.
What do you see instead?
FROM_PROXY
FROM_ORIGIN

The URL object fails the is_string() check on the top-level proxy value, falls into the {url, headers} object branch (src/runtime/webcore/fetch.rs, 'extract_proxy), has no .url own property (URL exposes .href), and is silently ignored — the request goes direct, un-proxied, with no error and no signal. That's a silent proxy bypass: swap a working proxy string for the equivalent URL and every request quietly egresses outside the corporate/scanning/anonymizing proxy while returning 200s.
new WebSocket(url, { proxy: new URL(p) }) has the identical shape and identical silent bypass in src/jsc/bindings/webcore/JSWebSocket.cpp (isString() → object branch → no url prop → no proxy).
Additional information
This is deliberately not folded into the proxy: { url: URL } fix (#29103) because a naive "route url-less objects through the URL parser" fix would break a separate, intentional, issue-numbered contract: a plain object without a url property must be ignored, per #25413 and its explicit tests (test/js/bun/http/proxy.test.ts, "proxy object without url is ignored"). A correct fix must distinguish "a real URL instance" from "an object without url" (e.g. a jsDynamicCast-style instance check), route the former through the existing href_from_js path, and leave the #25413 contract intact — in both fetch and WebSocket. Given the security-relevant failure mode (silent bypass), failing loud may also be preferable to failing open here.

t: patchedDependencies silently not applied on CI installs with a warm global cache (Expo EAS builders)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
We didn't record the exact bun version on the builder when we hit this (April 2026), and the builders are Expo's EAS managed workers so we don't control the image. Locally we're on 1.3.12 now. Filing anyway because the failure mode is silent and nasty to catch.
What platform is your computer?
The failure happens on Linux x64 (Expo EAS Build workers). We never reproduced it on our macs (macOS arm64), same commit, same lockfile.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
We don't have a minimal repro, it seems to depend on the state of the machine. This is what we observed:

package.json has a patchedDependencies entry, in our case "expo-audio@55.0.13": "patches/expo-audio@55.0.13.patch". The patch file exists and the version key matches the installed version.
bun install runs on a CI machine where bun's global cache is warm (EAS restores it between builds).
Install finishes with no error or warning, but node_modules/expo-audio is pristine. The patch content is just not there.

What is the expected behavior?
The patch gets applied, or the install fails loudly.
What do you see instead?
Silent no-op. We only caught it because our patch adds enum entries on the Android side, and inspecting the dex of the built APK showed them missing. The patch file was there, the version key matched, install was green.
Additional information
The same commit installs correctly patched on our macs. That's what makes us think it's the cache-restore path (package hardlinked/copied from the global cache without the patch being re-applied on top) and not the patch itself.
Our workaround is a postinstall script that checks every patch and re-applies whatever bun skipped. On the affected builders it logs the re-apply, so the tree really is unpatched right after bun install. The core of it:
for (const key of Object.keys(pkg.patchedDependencies)) {
	const name = key.slice(0, key.lastIndexOf("@"))
	const patchPath = pkg.patchedDependencies[key]
	const applyArgs = `--directory="node_modules/${name}" "${patchPath}"`

	try {
		// --check succeeding means the patch is NOT applied yet
		execSync(`git apply --check ${applyArgs}`, { stdio: "pipe" })
		console.log(`applying ${patchPath} (bun skipped it)`)
		execSync(`git apply ${applyArgs}`, { stdio: "inherit" })
	} catch {
		// already applied (reverse --check passes) or the patch doesn't match
		execSync(`git apply --reverse --check ${applyArgs}`, { stdio: "pipe" })
	}
}

fs.realpathSync converts backslash to slash on Linux, throws ENOENT for existing paths
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af — also reproduced on canary 1.4.0-canary.1+d37f52067
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
// repro-backslash.js
const fs = require("fs");
const dir = "/tmp/back\\slash";  // one literal backslash in the name
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
console.log("existsSync:  ", fs.existsSync(dir));
console.log("lstatSync:   ", fs.lstatSync(dir).isDirectory());
console.log("realpathSync:", fs.realpathSync(dir));
$ bun repro-backslash.js
existsSync:   true
lstatSync:    true
ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/tmp/back\slash'
fs.realpathSync.native fails identically. Node v22 prints /tmp/back\slash
as expected.
What is the expected behavior?
On POSIX, \ is an ordinary filename character. realpathSync should resolve
the path exactly as existsSync/lstatSync already do (both return true for
this directory in the same process).
What actually happened?
strace shows realpath rewrites the backslash to a forward slash before
touching the filesystem, then opens the wrong path:
$ strace -f -e trace=%file bun repro-backslash.js 2>&1 | grep '/tmp/back'
mkdir("/tmp/back\\slash", 0777)            = -1 EEXIST (File exists)
newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/back\\slash", {st_mode=S_IFDIR|0755, ...}, 0) = 0
access("/tmp/back\\slash", F_OK)           = 0
statx(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/back\\slash", ...)   = 0
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/back/slash", O_RDONLY|O_PATH) = -1 ENOENT
Every other fs call passes the backslash through byte-perfect; only realpath's
resolver applies the (Windows-only) \ → / normalization. Two smaller
inaccuracies in the resulting error object: syscall is reported as "lstat"
(the failing syscall is openat), and path is the original input, which
makes the error look impossible next to a successful lstatSync of the same
string.
path.normalize / path.resolve / path.join are all correct (backslash
preserved), so the stray normalization is specific to the realpath
implementation.
Real-world impact
Claude Code (a Bun single-file executable) realpath-validates its working
directory at startup, so it cannot launch in any directory whose absolute
path contains a backslash:
$ mkdir 'a\b' && cd 'a\b' && claude
Error: Can't access working directory /home/user/a\b: Path "/home/user/a\b" does not exist

t: Segfault (null deref, address 0x0) in JSC::MarkedBlock::Handle::sweep during TCPSocket upgradeTLS — Bun v1.4.0, running inside Claude Code
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0 (commit 63bb0ca)
What platform is your computer?
WSL2 Ubuntu, Windows 11, x86_64. Running as the embedded Bun runtime inside Claude Code (standalone executable), versions 2.1.198 through 2.1.201 — the crash reproduced across all of these.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
I don't have a minimal JS reproduction — this happens inside Claude Code's bundled standalone executable, so I can't isolate the exact call site in user-land code. However, it reproduced 10+ times over a single session, with no obvious user action correlating to each crash (not tied to any specific command; one instance coincided with claude --resume <session-id>, but the other 9 occurred during ordinary use with no --resume).
I captured one crash live via script to preserve the Bun crash reporter output, which produced this crash report URL:
https://bun.report/1.4.0/B_163bb0camgggkEuhogDs5n/1Egz9r6C6ons6Cui880E8jt80EojkysE8l3xsE4lmpgDk38stDu9zw6Co65qtD_uwwn6Bms3/5Bi3vh2E2uih2E6h0h5Ewpuq7E45i8lD_A2AA
Crash summary
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x0

The decoded stack trace shows the fault occurring inside JSLock.cpp:55 (RefPtr<JSC::VM>::refIfNotNull dereferencing a null VM*), reached via:
JSC::LocalAllocator::allocateSlowCase
  → JSC::MarkedBlock::Handle::sweep
    → (GC sweep triggered during allocation of a new JSTLSSocket cell,
       via JSCellInlines.h / JSC::allocateCell)
    → concurrently, a TCP socket's Rust-side Handlers object is being
      dropped (bun_runtime::socket::Handlers::drop → Bun__JSValue__unprotect)
      as part of TCPSocketPrototype__upgradeTLS
  → RefPtr<JSC::VM>::RefPtr → refIfNotNull → JSLock.cpp:55  [CRASH: null deref]

This looks like a race/use-after-free between the JSC garbage collector's mark-and-sweep pass and the Rust-side socket Handlers::drop cleanup that happens as part of upgrading a plain TCP socket to TLS (socket.upgradeTLS()). The GC sweep, triggered while allocating a new JSTLSSocket object for the upgraded connection, appears to encounter a socket handler object whose backing VM* has already been invalidated/freed by the concurrent Rust drop, leading to a null pointer dereference.
Possibly related
This may be related to (or share a root cause with) #24357 "SegFault running Claude Code", which shows a very similar crash shape:
JSC::LocalAllocator::allocateSlowCase
  → JSC::LocalAllocator::tryAllocateWithoutCollecting
    → JSC::LocalAllocator::tryAllocateIn

t: VirtualMachine::event_loop_handle is read from producer threads without synchronization (wakeup path)
b:
What
VirtualMachine::event_loop_handle is a plain, non-atomic Option<*mut PlatformEventLoop> (src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs:181) that is read from non-JS threads on the cross-thread enqueue path, while the JS thread may concurrently rewrite it.
Read path (POSIX):
EventLoop::enqueue_task_concurrent(&self, task)   // called from producer threads
  -> self.wakeup()                                 // src/jsc/event_loop.rs:1003
     -> self.vm_ref().platform_loop_opt()          // src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs:1144
        -> self.event_loop_handle.map(|h| unsafe { &mut *h })   // plain, non-atomic read

Write path (JS thread): ensure_waker() (event_loop.rs) and the spawnSync prepare/cleanup swap (__bun_spawn_sync_vm_set_event_loop_handle).
So a producer thread (HTTP client, work pool, waiter thread) can read the field while the JS thread writes it. platform_loop_opt()'s own SAFETY comment states "only the owning JS thread reborrows mutably", which that path does not satisfy; it also hands out &mut PlatformEventLoop from &self, so two producer threads can form aliasing &mut to the same loop.
Impact
Low / practically benign on supported targets, which is why this is filed rather than fixed inline:

Option<*mut T> is niche-optimized to a single machine word, so the read cannot tear.
uws::Loop::wakeup() is a thread-safe eventfd/pipe write.
Windows does not go through platform_loop_opt() in wakeup().

It is still formally UB (unsynchronized read/write of a non-atomic field, plus aliasing &mut), and it is the last non-atomic field on a path that was otherwise made atomic (is_shutting_down → AtomicBool, event_loop → AtomicPtr<EventLoop>).
Suggested fix
Make event_loop_handle an AtomicPtr<PlatformEventLoop> (null = None): Release-store in ensure_waker / __bun_spawn_sync_vm_set_event_loop_handle, Acquire-load in the accessor. Split the accessor in two so the cross-thread wakeup() path takes a shared Option<&PlatformEventLoop> (it needs no &mut), leaving the existing &mut accessor for the JS-thread-only tick/run/update_counts call sites.
Credit: spotted in review of #32071, where the neighbouring event_loop/is_shutting_down fields were made atomic for exactly this reason.

t: ws npm package's maxPayload not working as expected under Bun, but does under Node
Detect unsettled top-level await and exit like Node (exit 13 + warning)
b:
Split out from #14951, which was closed for its CPU-spin half (fixed by #32014: condition-gated drive loops now ref the event loop and park instead of busy-spinning).
The other half remains: when a module's top-level await never settles and nothing else refs the event loop, Node prints a warning and exits 13:
$ node -e 'await new Promise(() => {})'
Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await at [eval]:1
await new Promise(() => {})
^
$ echo $?
13
Bun's wait_for_promise refs the loop for the duration of the wait, so it waits for any pending unref'd timer and otherwise parks indefinitely rather than exiting. Verified against Node 26.3/26.4.
Implementing this means detecting "the module promise is pending and nothing other than this driver refs the loop", emitting the warning at the awaiting source location, and exiting 13. Two tests in test/js/web/timers/timers-unref-idle-loop.test.ts carry TODOs pointing here and assert today's divergent behavior (exit 0, no warning); they should be flipped as part of the fix.
Related: #31501 (closed as a duplicate of #14951).

t: event loop: never re-enter from inside a dispatch callback (de-block expect().resolves and HTMLRewriter.transform, then assert)
b:
Invariant
The event loop must never be re-entered from inside a poll-dispatch callback.
waitForPromise ("run the event loop until this promise settles") is legitimate only where a synchronous outer context is inherent — the module pipeline and top-level drivers, which run when no dispatch is in flight:

entry-point module-graph evaluation (bun file.ts): ES-module evaluation is async by spec, so the synchronous entry must pump until it settles
macro loading/evaluation inside the transpiler
the REPL / CLI drivers

Every other caller is a synchronous API signature sitting on an asynchronous operation, reachable from inside I/O completion callbacks. Re-entering the loop there is what makes bugs like the one root-caused in #32233 possible: a nested epoll_wait/kevent overwrites the shared ready_polls batch mid-iteration, and any not-yet-dispatched one-shot entries (subprocess pipe readers, process watchers) are lost forever — the owner hangs.
#32233 contained a correct, minimal, well-tested fix that made the dispatcher tolerate re-entry. It was closed deliberately (see the closing comment: #32233 (comment)) because tolerating the state entrenches it: the right end-state is that the state cannot occur, and CI screams if someone reintroduces it.
What #32233 established (all of this carries over)

Plain concurrent Bun.$ never hangs by itself: 0/20 (Linux) and 0/8 (macOS) on unfixed builds. The loss requires a waitForPromise caller in a continuation of an I/O completion.
The nested-tick stack was captured live (gdb, loop->data.tick_depth == 2), with HTMLRewriter.transform (async handler) as a pure-runtime trigger: 20/20 hangs unfixed → 0/20 with the (closed) dispatcher fix.
require() is not a trigger: an ordinary graph never pumps the loop, and a top-level-await graph is refused with ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE.
Three deterministic regression tests exist in that PR's branch (test/js/bun/spawn/pipe-reader-nested-tick.test.ts): two trigger via bun:test matchers, one via HTMLRewriter; victims cover both Bun.$ and Bun.spawn pipes.

t: Bun.Terminal: spawned child's controlling terminal is not the PTY (no setsid/TIOCSCTTY) — ^C never signals, /dev/tty points at the parent's tty
b:
What is the problem?
Bun.spawn({ terminal }) connects the child's stdio to the new PTY, but it doesn't make that PTY the child's controlling terminal (no setsid() + TIOCSCTTY on the slave, the way forkpty(3)/node-pty do). Two consequences:

The PTY's line discipline has no foreground process group to signal, so writing ^C (0x03) into the terminal never delivers a SIGINT — you can't interrupt anything you spawn on a Bun.Terminal.
/dev/tty inside the child still resolves to the parent's terminal (or nothing), so programs that talk to their controlling tty directly (password prompts, less, tput) reach the wrong one.

Repro (run from a terminal):
const term = new Bun.Terminal({ cols: 80, rows: 24, data: (_t, d) => process.stdout.write(d) });

const proc = Bun.spawn(["sh", "-c", 'ps -o pid,pgid,sess,tty,command -p "$$"; sleep 500; echo SURVIVED'], {
  terminal: term,
});

setTimeout(() => term.write("\x03"), 500); // ^C into the PTY (slave has ISIG on)

console.log(await Promise.race([
  proc.exited,
  new Promise((r) => setTimeout(() => r("child still alive 3s after ^C"), 3000)),
]));
Output on my machine (parent is on ttys029):
  PID  PGID   SESS TTY      COMMAND
45278 45277      0 ttys029  sh -c ps -o pid,pgid,sess,tty,command -p "$$"; sleep 500; ...
^C
child still alive 3s after ^C

The child's TTY is the parent's terminal, not the new PTY, and the ^C is just echoed.
What did you expect?
The same as forkpty(): the child starts a new session with the PTY slave as its controlling terminal, so

term.write("\x03") → SIGINT to the PTY's foreground process group (the sleep dies, proc.exited resolves ~130), and
open("/dev/tty") in the child gives the PTY.

Without this, anything shell- or terminal-emulator-shaped built on Bun.Terminal has to reimplement the line discipline's signal generation in userspace (watch for 0x03/0x1c/0x1a in the input stream, check term.localFlags & ISIG, signal the process tree manually), which is what I'm doing today.
Ran into this building an interactive shell on Bun Shell + Bun.Terminal; related to #33234.
Bun v1.3.14, macOS arm64.

t: `Bun.Archive`: support per-entry file modes when creating archives
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun.Archive hardcodes 0644 for every entry when creating an archive (Archive.rs: entry_ref.set_perm(0o644)). There is no way to mark a file as executable.
This makes it unusable for building npm tarballs that ship precompiled binaries (esbuild-style platform packages): the binary must carry 0755 inside the tarball, since npm only chmods files listed in the manifest's bin field. Today we have to keep node-tar as a dependency just because it preserves file modes.
Note extraction already preserves modes — creation is the only gap.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A way to set the mode per entry, e.g.:
new Bun.Archive({
  "bin/mytool": { data: bytes, mode: 0o755 },
  "README.md": "hello",
});
What alternatives have you considered?

node-tar (works, but defeats the point of a native API)
chmod after extraction — doesn't help; consumers are npm clients extracting the tarball, not our code

t: [vscode] bun.runtime path with spaces fails on Windows (spawn ENOENT)
b:
Problem
On Windows, if the bun.runtime setting points to a path containing spaces (e.g. C:\Program Files\bun\bun.exe), the extension fails to launch the debugger or run tests:
Failed to start debugger. Program could not be started.
spawn C:\Program is ENOENT

The root cause: the extension passes the raw path string through a shell-interpolated command string. On Windows, unquoted paths with spaces are split at the first space by the OS, so C:\Program Files\bun\bun.exe is interpreted as executable C:\Program with argument Files\bun\bun.exe.
Steps to Reproduce

Install Bun to C:\Program Files\bun\ on Windows (any path with a space works).
Set "bun.runtime": "C:\Program Files\bun\bun.exe" in VS Code settings.
Open a file and run a test via Test Explorer, or press F5 to debug.
Observe the spawn ENOENT failure.

Expected Behaviour
Use child_process.spawn(bunPath, args, { shell: false }) — passing the executable and arguments as separate values — so no shell tokenisation occurs:
// Wrong (shell splits on space):
child_process.exec(`${bunPath} test ...`);

// Right (no shell, no splitting):
child_process.spawn(bunPath, ['test', ...args], { shell: false });
Environment

OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200
Bun installed to path-with-spaces
VS Code: 1.89+
Extension: oven.bun-vscode latest

t: [vscode] Extension does not support multi-root workspaces: bun.runtime and test settings apply globally, not per folder
b:
Problem
In a VS Code multi-root workspace (.code-workspace) with multiple packages, the Bun extension applies bun.runtime, bun.test.filePattern, and bun.test.timeout settings globally. There is no way to set different Bun versions or test patterns per workspace folder.
This matters in monorepos where:

One package uses Bun 1.x, another still uses a pinned older version.
One package has tests matching **/*.spec.ts, another uses **/*.test.ts.
One package needs a longer test timeout due to database setup.

Steps to Reproduce

Create a .code-workspace with two folders:
{
  "folders": [
    { "path": "packages/api" },
    { "path": "packages/frontend" }
  ]
}

In packages/api/.vscode/settings.json:
{ "bun.test.filePattern": "**/*.spec.ts", "bun.test.timeout": 10000 }

In packages/frontend/.vscode/settings.json:
{ "bun.test.filePattern": "**/*.test.tsx" }

Open the multi-root workspace. Both folders use the same (workspace-global) bun.test.filePattern — folder-level overrides are ignored.

Expected Behaviour
The extension should use vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('bun', document.uri) (URI-scoped) when reading settings that affect individual files, so VS Code's built-in folder-override resolution applies.
Proposed Fix
Audit every `vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('bun').get(...)" call in the extension and change them to URI-scoped lookups where the setting is per-file or per-folder in nature.
Environment

OS: Windows 11 / macOS
VS Code: 1.89+, multi-root workspace
Extension: oven.bun-vscode latest

t: node-postgres: parameter values bleed between concurrent queries on a shared pg.Pool (22P02 / 08P01) under Bun

What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14 (oven/bun:1.3.14-slim, linux/x64)
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (AWS Fargate, oven/bun:1.3.14-slim). Connects to PostgreSQL 16 (AWS RDS).
Dependencies

pg@8.21.0 (pg-pool@3.14.0, pg-protocol@1.14.0, pg-types@2.2.0)

What steps will reproduce the bug?
In one long-running process, a single shared pg.Pool is used concurrently by multiple independent async tasks, each following the standard checkout pattern:
const client = await pool.connect();
try {
  return await client.query(text, params); // parameterized, $1..$n
} finally {
  client.release();
}
Concretely: an SQS-consumer loop and a background job worker (pg-boss) both issue parameterized queries through the same pg.Pool at overlapping times. Each call checks out what should be a distinct pooled client.
Intermittently, under real concurrency, a parameter value from one in-flight query becomes bound to a different concurrent query running on a different pooled client. It surfaces as either:

22P02 invalid input syntax for type <T>: "<a string value that belongs to a different, concurrently-running query>", or
08P01 wire-protocol / "invalid message format" errors.

Application-level logging immediately before each client.query() proves the correct parameters were passed; Postgres' WHERE: unnamed portal parameter $N = '...' shows a value that originated in a different query executing at the same moment.

⚠️ I do not yet have a reduced minimal reproduction — it is timing/load-dependent and only manifests under genuine concurrency in a long-running process. The identical code does not exhibit this on Node.js.

How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?
Intermittent — appears when two independent queries on the shared pool overlap in time. Rare per-query, but reliably recurring in a busy long-running process. Requires genuine concurrency on a shared pg.Pool.
What is the expected behavior?
Each pool.connect() yields an isolated client; concurrent queries on distinct pooled clients must not share wire/parameter state. Parameters passed to client.query(text, params) must bind to that query only — matching Node.js behavior with identical code.
What do you see instead?
Parameters from one query bind to a concurrently-executing query on another pooled client (22P02 with a foreign value, or 08P01).

t: Add --ts-version flag for init
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, bun init always defaults to installing a generic or older TypeScript version (like TS 5.x). When developers want to seed a new project using newer versions like TypeScript 6 or the latest TypeScript 7, they have to manually update the dependency after initialization. This adds repetitive boilerplate steps for anyone wanting to test or adopt newer TS features immediately.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I propose adding a --ts-version (or --typescript) flag to the bun init command.
Proposed Usage:
# Initialize a project with a specific TypeScript version
bun init --ts-version 6
bun init --ts-version 7.0.0-rc

# Or using tags
bun init --ts-version latest
bun init --ts-version rc
How it helps:
This would allow developers to customize their development stack directly from the initialization step, aligning with Bun's core philosophy of being a fast, all-in-one, frictionless toolkit.
What alternatives have you considered?

structuredClone(Object.prototype) throws a DataCloneError instead of returning an empty object
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0-canary and current main (0f9331d)
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (reproduces everywhere)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
console.log(structuredClone(Object.prototype));
What is the expected behavior?
It returns {}.
%Object.prototype% is an immutable prototype exotic object, and the exotic-object rejection step in StructuredSerializeInternal carves it out explicitly:

Otherwise, if value is an exotic object and value is not the %Object.prototype% intrinsic object associated with any Realm, then throw a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
Note: %Object.prototype% is an immutable prototype exotic object; that is why it is excluded from this step. It will be handled in the default case, and end up being deserialized as an empty object.

Node 26.3.0 returns {}:
$ node -e 'console.log(structuredClone(Object.prototype))'
{}

What do you see instead?
$ bun -e 'console.log(structuredClone(Object.prototype))'
DataCloneError: The object can not be cloned.

Additional information
Noticed while writing the structured clone fuzz target in #32979. It is not part of that test because it would be red on main, so filing it separately. Admittedly obscure, but it is a spec deviation with an explicit note in the standard explaining the carve-out.

t: Temporal: buddhist calendar's year field returns the ISO year instead of BE
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0-canary.1+df92f8fd6 (also reproduces on a debug build of current main, revision 0f9331d)
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Temporal is currently behind the BUN_JSC_useTemporal=1 JSC option.
BUN_JSC_useTemporal=1 bun -e '
const d = Temporal.PlainDate.from("1870-08-19").withCalendar("buddhist");
console.log(d.year, d.eraYear, d.era);
const e = Temporal.PlainDate.from({ year: 2515, month: 2, day: 1, calendar: "buddhist" });
console.log(e.toString(), e.daysInMonth);
'
What is the expected behavior?
2413 2413 be
1972-02-01[u-ca=buddhist] 29

The Thai Buddhist Era is the ISO year plus 543, so ISO 1870 is BE 2413, and the buddhist calendar has a single era, so year and eraYear must agree. In the other direction, { year: 2515, calendar: "buddhist" } is BE 2515 = ISO 1972, a leap year, so February has 29 days.
This is what Node v26.3.0 prints, and @js-temporal/polyfill 0.5.1 agrees on year (2413) and on the from round-trip (1972-02-01[u-ca=buddhist], daysInMonth 29).
What do you see instead?
1870 2413 be
2515-02-01[u-ca=buddhist] 28

Two problems, both sides of the same mapping:

The year getter returns the ISO year (1870) while eraYear correctly returns 2413. These disagreeing on a single-era calendar is internally inconsistent, and it means Temporal.PlainDate.from({ year: d.year, month: d.month, day: d.day, calendar: d.calendarId }) does not round-trip.
Temporal.PlainDate.from({ year, ... calendar: "buddhist" }) interprets the year field as an ISO year instead of a buddhist year, so BE 2515 resolves to ISO 2515 (not a leap year, hence daysInMonth 28).

Additional information
This is the cause of the test/intl402/Temporal/*/basic-buddhist.js and */with/mutually-exclusive-fields-buddhist.js test262 failures.
Found while measuring the test262 Temporal suite and a 20,500-operation deterministic output diff against Node for #15853.

b:
What
Expose the existing reactFastRefresh option on new Bun.Transpiler(), matching the
Bun.build() API. The parser transform already exists and is already wired through the
bundler — the Bun.Transpiler path just never reads the option and hardcodes the feature
to false. This is a ~3-line threading change in src/runtime/api/JSTranspiler.rs plus a
type definition.
(Filing fresh against the current Rust tree. This supersedes my older #30295 and the
pre-rewrite PR #28312, both of which targeted Zig files that no longer exist.)
Why
Unbundled ESM dev servers transpile individual .tsx files on the fly for HMR (the same
pattern Vite uses): serve source modules one at a time, and on change re-transpile just that
file (~0.1ms) instead of running a full Bun.build(). React Fast Refresh needs
$RefreshReg$ / $RefreshSig$ registration calls injected, which the parser already does
when features.react_fast_refresh is set — but there's currently no way to ask
Bun.Transpiler for it, so per-file HMR consumers are forced into a full Bun.build() per
keystroke.
Current state on main
Bun.build() exposes reactFastRefresh (it's on BuildConfig in packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts),
and the bundler threads it correctly:
// src/bundler/ParseTask.rs:2469-2470
opts.features.react_fast_refresh =
    topts.react_fast_refresh && loader.is_jsx() && !source.path.is_node_module();
But the Transpiler API never parses the option and hardcodes the feature off:
// src/runtime/api/JSTranspiler.rs:1096
transpiler.options.react_fast_refresh = false;
The from_js options parser (JSTranspiler.rs, ~lines 162–650) reads loader, target,
tsconfig, macro, autoImportJSX, allowBunRuntime, minify, sourcemap, exports,
logLevel, … but has no reactFastRefresh branch. And TranspilerOptions in
packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts (lines 2391–2508) has no such field.
Proposed change
Three spots, all mirroring how autoImportJSX is already handled:


Parse it — in from_js, right after the autoImportJSX block (JSTranspiler.rs:389-391):
if let Some(flag) = object.get_boolean_loose(global, "reactFastRefresh")? {
    self.runtime.react_fast_refresh = flag;
}


Thread it — replace the hardcode at JSTranspiler.rs:1096, mirroring
auto_import_jsx at line 1093 and gating on a JSX loader like ParseTask.rs:2469:
transpiler.options.react_fast_refresh =
    config.runtime.react_fast_refresh && transpiler.options.loader.is_jsx();

ParseTask doesn't apply here sinc

t: node:crypto: generateKeyPair("rsa-pss") silently accepts conflicting deprecated hash / hashAlgorithm aliases
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0 (reproduces on current main)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Node's crypto.generateKeyPair/generateKeyPairSync accept a deprecated hash option as an alias for hashAlgorithm (and mgf1Hash for mgf1HashAlgorithm). Node rejects a request that sets both to different values. Bun silently accepts it.
import crypto from "crypto";
for (const [name, options] of [
  ["hash vs hashAlgorithm", { modulusLength: 512, saltLength: 16, hash: "sha256", hashAlgorithm: "sha1" }],
  ["mgf1Hash vs mgf1HashAlgorithm", { modulusLength: 512, saltLength: 16, mgf1Hash: "sha256", mgf1HashAlgorithm: "sha1" }],
]) {
  try { crypto.generateKeyPair("rsa-pss", options, () => {}); console.log(name, "=> NO SYNC THROW"); }
  catch (e) { console.log(name, "=>", e.code); }
}
What is the expected behavior?
$ node repro.mjs
hash vs hashAlgorithm => ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE
mgf1Hash vs mgf1HashAlgorithm => ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE

What do you see instead?
$ bun repro.mjs
hash vs hashAlgorithm => NO SYNC THROW
mgf1Hash vs mgf1HashAlgorithm => NO SYNC THROW

The conflict is silently ignored (one of the two values wins) and the key generation proceeds.
Additional information
The conflict checks in RsaKeyPairJobCtx::fromJS (src/jsc/bindings/node/crypto/CryptoGenRsaKeyPair.cpp) are dead. The function declares four view variables (hashView, hashAlgorithmView, mgf1HashView, mgf1HashAlgorithmView), but:

the options.hashAlgorithm branch writes to hashString/hashView (not hashAlgorithmString/hashAlgorithmView), and
the options.mgf1HashAlgorithm branch writes to mgf1HashView (not mgf1HashAlgorithmView),

so hashAlgorithmView and mgf1HashAlgorithmView are never assigned. The two conflict checks are if (!hashAlgorithmView->isNull() && hashAlgorithmView != hashView) and the mgf1 equivalent, which can therefore never fire. The subsequent hashAlgorithmView->isNull() ? hashView : hashAlgorithmView selection also means whichever of the two branches ran last wins.
Two things a fix should also cover:

Node's upstream test/parallel/test-crypto-keygen.js, which Bun vendors, contains assert.throws(..., { code: 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE' }) assertions for exactly these two cases, and that file currently passes on Bun even though the reproduction above shows no exception is thrown. I could not determine what satisfies those assertions; whatever it is deserves a look, because an upstream test that is green while the behavior it asserts is absent is worth understanding on its own.
Bun's asse

bun update <package> ignores catalog and creates a spurious root dependency at latest
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
In a workspace monorepo, define a named catalog in the root package.json and consume it from workspace packages via catalog:<name>. The catalog package is not present in the root dependencies/devDependencies — it only exists in catalogs.
Root package.json:
{
  "name": "stitch",
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*", "connectors/*"],
  "catalogs": {
    "ai": {
      "ai": "6.0.116",
      "@ai-sdk/provider": "3.0.10"
    }
  }
}
A workspace package (e.g. packages/server/package.json):
{
  "dependencies": {
    "ai": "catalog:ai"
  }
}
Then run an update for the named catalog package:
bun update ai
# or to preview without writing:
bun update ai --dry-run
What is the expected behavior?
bun update ai should update the version of ai inside the catalog definition (catalogs.ai.ai) in the root package.json, respecting the existing semver constraint (or the latest satisfying version), and the workspace packages should continue to reference it via catalog:ai. The catalog should remain the single source of truth.
This mirrors how bun update -i --recursive is documented/expected to behave for catalogs.
What do you see instead?
bun update ai ignores the catalog entirely and instead creates a brand-new top-level dependency in the root package.json at the latest version, bypassing both the catalog definition and any semver constraint:
...
installed ai@7.0.3

[487.00ms] done

So:

The catalog entry catalogs.ai.ai (6.0.116) is left untouched.
A new, unrelated dependencies.ai (7.0.3, latest — not the catalog version) is added to the root package.json.
The workspace catalog:ai references are not updated and now diverge from the new root dependency.

Additionally, bun update --interactive lists only the dependencies declared in the root package.json and does not surface the catalog entries, so there is no interactive path to update a catalog-defined package by name either.
Additional information
This appears related to, but distinct from, the existing catalog/bun update issues:

#21852 / #28073 — bun update (no args) overwriting catalog: references in subpackages with literal versions.
#23739 — bun outdated / bun update -r not listing/updating catalog entries.
#29357 / #23507 — --recursive / --filter (non-interactive) only editing the root package.json and ignoring workspaces.

Those focus on the no-arg

t: Bun 1.4 regression: a leaked `setSystemTime()` non-deterministically breaks `Date.now()`-based code in other test files (default runner; `--isolate` fixes it)
b:
How this was produced. The investigation and this write-up were done with
Claude Code — but this is not a synthetic or
AI-invented report. The bug surfaced in a real production test suite (220+ files; a real
admin-login flow that does a time-based TOTP 2FA check): ~150 tests that are green on stable
1.3.14 fail on canary 1.4. From there it was traced, reduced, and re-verified against
stable down to the small, dependency-light repository linked below, which fails on canary and
passes on stable (and with --isolate). Every number below was measured on real runs, not
guessed. Happy to provide more diagnostics or run specific builds.

What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0-canary.1+05895486d (reproduces ❌) — the new test runner.
1.3.14+0d9b296af does not reproduce ✅.
What platform is your computer?
macOS — Darwin 25.5.0, arm64 (Apple Silicon).
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Minimal repro repository: https://github.com/RodriguesCosta/bun-report-time
git clone https://github.com/RodriguesCosta/bun-report-time
cd bun-report-time
bun install

bun test            # canary 1.4 -> ~18 failures
bun test --isolate  # canary 1.4 -> 0 failures
# stable 1.3        -> 0 failures
The setup. When one test file calls setSystemTime(<date>) and never restores the
real clock (no setSystemTime() in an afterEach/afterAll), the mocked clock leaks into
the other test files of the same bun test run. That part is expected/known. The bug is
what happens next on canary.
The repo contains:

tests/00-leak-system-time.spec.ts — freezes the clock with setSystemTime(2024-01-09) and
intentionally never resets it. It does nothing else.
tests/login-*.spec.ts — 40 independent files, each running a tiny TOTP/2FA check via
otpauth: generate() a code → small async gap
(setImmediate + setTimeout(3)) → validate({ window: 1 }). None of them touch the clock.
A ±30s window means this can never legitimately fail.

What is the expected behavior?
0 failures, as on stable Bun 1.3.
What do you see instead?
On canary 1.4 (default runner), ~18 of 320 validations fail:
# canary 1.4.0-canary.1
 312 pass
  18 fail
Ran 330 tests across 41 files.

# stable 1.3.14
 330 pass
   0 fail

Every failure is the same assertion:
error: expect(received).not.toBeNull()
  at tests/login-NN.spec.ts  ->  verifier.validate({ token: code, window: 1 })

The failures are deterministic in count here (18 every run) and cluster in the
latest-running files.
Three things make it disappear (all point at the same place)

bun install/add of a tarball URL fails with DependencyLoop when updating an already-installed package to a different URL
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
When a package is already installed from a tarball URL, installing the same package from a different tarball URL (e.g. a new build of the same package) fails with a dependency-loop error instead of updating it.
mkdir app && cd app
echo '{ "name": "app", "version": "1.0.0" }' > package.json

# install the package from one tarball URL — works
bun add "https://pkg.vc/-/@appwrite/@appwrite.io/console@4851d03"

# update the same package to a different tarball URL — fails
bun add "https://pkg.vc/-/@appwrite/@appwrite.io/console@3ecc0b7"
Both URLs are live and serve a tarball whose package.json name is @appwrite.io/console.
What is the expected behavior?
The second bun add should update @appwrite.io/console to point at the new tarball URL, replacing the previous one — the same way bun add foo@2 replaces foo@1.
What do you see instead?
bun add v1.3.14 (0d9b296a)
Resolving dependencies
Resolved, downloaded and extracted [1]
error: Package "@appwrite.io/console@https://pkg.vc/-/@appwrite/@appwrite.io/console@3ecc0b7" has a dependency loop
  Resolution: "@appwrite.io/console@https://pkg.vc/-/@appwrite/@appwrite.io/console@4851d03"
  Dependency: "@appwrite.io/console@https://pkg.vc/-/@appwrite/@appwrite.io/console@3ecc0b7"
error: An internal error occurred (DependencyLoop)

The install aborts and package.json is left unchanged.
Additional information
Root cause: a tarball/git URL dependency is keyed by its URL until the tarball is fetched and its real package name is known (assign_root_resolution then renames the dependency to the resolved package name). Because the new URL doesn't match the existing package.json entry by name, a second root dependency is created for the same package. After both resolve, two root dependencies share one name, which the tree hoister rejects as a dependency loop (src/install/lockfile/Tree.rs).
This looks like the same root cause as #20647 (crash: bun add remote package tar.gz dependency loop and errors), so it may be a duplicate — that report hits the issue via a different/changed tarball URL of the same package on Windows.

t: Security: Fixed-seed non-cryptographic hashes (Wyhash11 / std.hash.Wyhash) are algebraically collidable, enabling trustedDependencies RCE, scoped-registry token leak, and cache poisoning
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Linux 5.4.241
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Full PoCs: https://github.com/kexinoh/bun-sec-repro
A project trusts the popular package esbuild (extremely common, since esbuild has a
postinstall). The attacker publishes ypo1f8kpbrqk7 — a valid npm name whose 32-bit
trustedDependencies key collides with esbuild (both trunc32(Wyhash11) = 0x433d2310).
Bun then runs ypo1f8kpbrqk7's lifecycle scripts although only esbuild is trusted.
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir pkg
# attacker package: NOT trusted, but its name u32-collides with "esbuild"
echo '{"name":"ypo1f8kpbrqk7","version":"1.0.0","scripts":{"postinstall":"echo PWNED > /tmp/PROOF"}}' > pkg/package.json
# victim app: trusts ONLY the real package "esbuild"
echo '{"name":"app","trustedDependencies":["esbuild"],"dependencies":{"ypo1f8kpbrqk7":"file:./pkg"}}' > package.json

bun install
cat /tmp/PROOF      # -> "PWNED": the untrusted package's postinstall ran
Output on 1.3.14+0d9b296af:
+ ypo1f8kpbrqk7@pkg
1 package installed
# /tmp/PROOF now contains "PWNED"

The trust key is @as(u32, @truncate(String.Builder.stringHash(name))) in
src/install/lockfile.zig (hasTrustedDependency), and the TrustedDependenciesSet stores
ONLY that u32 (no name, no byte comparison), so any name colliding on the truncated Wyhash11
is treated as trusted.
Verified colliding pairs (real trusted name -> attacker name, internal Wyhash11 u32):
esbuild     <-> ypo1f8kpbrqk7        (0x433d2310)
react       <-> bcwzzy1tt2zaef       (0xded8e790)
typescript  <-> oca6w8cjgtnbx10bjmy  (0x2c80259f)
@memlab/cli <-> vlkm-xaom            (0x1b83b95f)
What is the expected behavior?
Security-sensitive equality/identity checks must not collide for distinct inputs:

trustedDependencies: a package whose name is NOT literally in trustedDependencies must
NEVER have its lifecycle (postinstall) scripts executed.
Scoped registry routing: a request for @scopeA/pkg must only be sent to scopeA's configured
registry with scopeA's token, never to a different scope's host/token.
Cache keys (patch contents_hash, RuntimeTranspilerCache, MySQL prepared statements): two
distinct contents/queries must map to distinct cache entries.
FolderResolution / PackageNameHash: two distinct local paths or package names must resolve to
distinct entries.

Either hashes used as identity should be seeded per-process with a random seed, or equality must
fall back to a full byte-for-byte comparison.

When you default-import a bare-specifier CommonJS package that sets __esModule: true and assigns the real value to exports.default (the shape every Babel-compiled CJS package has), Bun returns exports.default as the import, whereas Node returns module.exports. What steps can reproduce the bug?
Calling AsyncLocalStorage.prototype.enterWith() and then performing any dynamic import() segfaults the process. The imported module can be trivial, and nothing else is required (no query string, no disable(), no getStore()).
Two files:
target.mjs
export const value = 42;
minimal.mjs
import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";

new AsyncLocalStorage().enterWith("X");
await import("./target.mjs");

console.log("done");
Run with bun minimal.mjs.
What is the expected behavior?
The program prints done and exits cleanly, as in Node.js:
$ node minimal.mjs
done

What do you see instead?
$ bun minimal.mjs
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x400010073
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.

bun.report: https://bun.report/1.3.14/Ma10d9b296AggggC_+/y34C+/y34C+qy34C+5sy6CusghJ22j+cmk2goBuxk+cu968c+85/iB+tqwH28stU24/zU2rtjU22nzT+mzvT2wuvT__A2ImngE
Additional information
Minimized from a larger script. Both elements are required to trigger the crash:

enterWith() alone (no dynamic import) — does not crash.
A dynamic import() alone (no enterWith()) — does not crash.
enterWith() + dynamic import() — crashes.

The crash does not require: a query string on the import specifier, a disable() call, or reading the store with getStore(). Using run() instead of enterWith() (including with AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot() / bind()) does not crash.

Calling process.exit in `--watch` mode terminates watcher entirely
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0-canary.1+98094dc4d
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Calling process.exit() in --watch mode terminates Bun entirely including the watcher itself. This makes it difficult to develop and test CLIs & scripts with Bun where you need to work with cases like this since I'd have to manually restart every time.
For example:
// index.ts
const pass = false;

if (!pass) {
  console.log('shall not pass');
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log('pass');
What is the expected behavior?
The watcher should remain active when the process exists and print an exit message at the end, preferably with exist code, to indicate that the program existed. If I truly want to exit the watcher then I could use CTRL-C.
This is the exact behavior in Node's built-in watch mode: the runner keeps listening for file changes after the program exists with process.exit.
Output of running the script above with node --watch index.ts:
Restarting 'index.ts'
shall not pass
Failed running 'index.ts'. Waiting for file changes before restarting...

What do you see instead?
Running the script above with bun --watch index.ts terminates the watcher.
Additional information
I originally opened #17637 as an "enhancement" issue last year but compared to Node's built-in watch mode as well as its ability to run typescript files, I'd argue this is more of a bug or compat issue at this point.

What steps can reproduce the bug?
I do not currently have a minimal standalone reproduction.
This occurs in a real server application: https://github.com/L3P3/rtjscomp
The app uses Node-compatible HTTP server APIs via http.createServer.
Observed pattern:

Run the server under Bun.
After long uptime (usually after half a day), one CPU core jumps to ~100% and stays there permanently.
During the bad state, profiler samples are dominated by:

processTicksAndRejections
internal:fixed_queue.shift


Calling actions.http_stop() immediately drops CPU from ~100% to ~5%.
Calling actions.http_start() afterwards keeps CPU around ~6% and the server remains in the normal state.
A new profile taken after restarting only the HTTP server no longer shows the queue flood. Instead it shows expected work such as:

normal HTTP response path (node:_http_outgoing)
DNS service subprocess spawn path (node:child_process) from ip_get_local() / exec("ip addr show")



What is the expected behavior?
The server should return to idle normally and should not get stuck permanently draining async/tick/microtask queues.
Restarting only the HTTP server should not be necessary to clear a bad internal state.
What do you see instead?
After long uptime, Bun enters a bad state where one CPU core stays at ~100% permanently.
In that state, profiler output is dominated almost entirely by:

processTicksAndRejections
internal:fixed_queue.shift

Stopping the HTTP server clears the high CPU condition immediately, and starting it again does not immediately reintroduce the problem.
This was originally observed on 1.3.13 and still occurs on 1.4.0.
Additional information
Why this seems Bun-specific:

The same app under Node.js does not reproduce this behavior.
Hot frames are Bun / Node internals, not dominated by application functions.
The app uses http.createServer in Node-compat mode.

My current conclusion is that this is a stuck or looping async request state in Bun's Node-compat event loop path, not steady-state application logic.
When it happens, Bun appears to repeatedly drain tick/microtask queues and never returns to idle.
Resetting the HTTP server clears the stuck connection/request state, which immediately removes the flood.
Probable trigger class:

long-lived or stale HTTP connections / handlers that do not settle cleanly

t: Feature request: Native PTY (pseudo-terminal) support in Bun.spawn
b:
Problem
Bun.spawn() only supports piped stdio (stdin: 'pipe', stdout: 'pipe'). Many interactive CLI tools (e.g., Antigravity CLI, vim, htop) check isatty() on their file descriptors and either refuse to output or degrade functionality when they detect pipes instead of a terminal.
This makes it impossible to build terminal multiplexers, remote session managers, or CI wrappers for interactive CLIs in pure Bun without falling back to Node.js + node-pty.
What I tried

Bun.spawn(['agy'], { stdin: 'pipe', stdout: 'pipe' }) — agy produces zero output (checks isatty())
Wrapping with expect — interact mode doesn't work when expect's stdin is a pipe
Wrapping with script -qfc — fails with tcgetattr: Operation not supported on socket
Wrapping with Python pty.spawn() — doesn't forward through pipes
What worked: node-pty (Node.js native addon) — allocates a real PTY

Desired API
Something like:
const proc = Bun.spawn(['agy'], {
  stdin: 'pty',
  stdout: 'pty', 
  stderr: 'pty',
  // or simply:
  pty: true,
  // with optional terminal size:
  cols: 200,
  rows: 50,
});
This would allocate a pseudo-terminal pair (openpty() / forkpty()) instead of pipes, making the child process think it's connected to a real terminal.
Use case
Building agy-mux — a tmux-like session manager for AI coding agents. The server spawns agy (Antigravity CLI) and streams I/O over WebSocket. Without PTY support, we had to drop Bun and switch to Node.js + node-pty as the only working solution.
Environment

Bun 1.3.14
macOS arm64 + Debian 12 (GCE)
Node.js 24.15.0 (where we ended up)

t: Bun fetch abort does not close server-side node:http POST streaming response
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Minimal reproduction:
https://github.com/aleclarson/repro/tree/bun-post-stream-abort-repro
Run:
git clone https://github.com/aleclarson/repro.git
cd repro
git switch bun-post-stream-abort-repro
bun run repro
The repro starts a node:http server under Bun, then uses Bun's global fetch client to request a streaming response.
It runs two cases:

GET /stream, then aborts the client fetch while waiting for response data.
POST /stream with a small JSON request body, then aborts the client fetch while waiting for response data.

The server records whether request.socket or ServerResponse emits close.
What is the expected behavior?
Aborting the Bun fetch request should close the server-side request/response for both GET and POST.
The POST case should emit one of:
POST socket-close
POST response-close
This is what happens when the same POST abort is performed with Node's fetch.
What do you see instead?
The GET case closes server-side, but the POST case does not.
Observed output with Bun 1.3.14:
GET handler
GET headers-flushed
GET response
GET read-error:AbortError:The operation was aborted.
GET socket-close
GET read-timeout
POST handler
POST body-read
POST headers-flushed
POST response
POST read-error:AbortError:The operation was aborted.
POST read-timeout

Reproduced: POST abort did not close the server-side request.
The Bun client sees AbortError, but the Bun node:http server never observes POST socket-close or POST response-close before the timeout.
Additional information
This seems related to, but distinct from, #28976.
The distinction is that this repro depends on Bun's own fetch client. In our testing, the same server-side POST stream cleanup works when the client is Node fetch; it fails when the client is Bun fetch.
So the issue appears to be specifically:
Bun fetch client abort
+ POST request with body
+ Bun node:http server streaming response
=> client receives AbortError, but server-side close/abort is not observed
This matters for long-lived POST response streams, such as NDJSON event streams or LLM-style streaming APIs. The client believes the request was aborted, but the server keeps the subscription/work alive because no close signal is delivered.

t: `--heap-prof-dir` mishandles absolute paths
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13+bf2e2cecf
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 23.6.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
mkdir -p /tmp/abs-heap-test
cd /some/other/dir
echo 'globalThis.__x = new Array(10000).fill({x:1})' > script.js
bun --heap-prof --heap-prof-dir=/tmp/abs-heap-test ./script.js
What is the expected behavior?
Snapshot written to /tmp/abs-heap-test.
What do you see instead?
Written to $CWD/tmp/abs-heap-test/ — the leading / is stripped and the path is resolved relative to CWD:
Heap profile written to: /some/other/dir/tmp/abs-heap-test/Heap.….heapsnapshot

Relative --heap-prof-dir works; only absolute paths break. --cpu-prof-dir is not affected.
Additional information
buildOutputPath in src/jsc/BunHeapProfiler.zig appends config.dir onto a path already rooted at CWD (AutoAbsPath.initTopLevelDir()):
if (config.dir.len > 0) path.append(config.dir);
For an already-rooted .abs path, append trims the segment as relative (strips the leading /) — see src/paths/Path.zig (it even debugAssert(!isInputAbsolute(input))s, so this is misuse). The CPU profiler is fine because src/jsc/BunCPUProfiler.zig uses path.join(&.{config.dir}), which resolves absolute segments correctly.
Same pattern in the Rust mirror src/jsc/BunHeapProfiler.rs, so a fix should cover both.
Suggested fix: use join like the CPU profiler: path.join(&.{config.dir}) instead of path.append(config.dir). No test currently covers --heap-prof-dir (test/cli/heap-prof.test.ts only tests the default CWD output).

t: Playwright `connectOverCDP` fails under Bun — WebSocket closes after `101 Switching Protocols` (works on Node)
b:
What happens
chromium.connectOverCDP(...) from playwright-core fails under Bun but works under Node. The CDP WebSocket completes the HTTP upgrade (101 Switching Protocols) and is then immediately closed before the connection is established.
connectOverCDP: WebSocket error: <cdp-ws-url> 101 Switching Protocols
  - <ws connecting> <cdp-ws-url>
  - <ws unexpected response> <cdp-ws-url> 101 Switching Protocols
  - <ws error> ... WebSocket was closed before the connection was established
  - <ws disconnected> ... code=1006

Minimal reproduction
Start any Chromium with a CDP endpoint:
google-chrome --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=9222
// repro.mjs
import { chromium } from "playwright-core";
const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP("http://localhost:9222");
console.log("contexts:", browser.contexts().length);
await browser.close();

node repro.mjs → works (prints the context count).
bun repro.mjs → fails with the error above.

Likely cause
Bun's HTTP client doesn't implement the HTTP→WebSocket protocol upgrade that Playwright's bundled ws relies on for connectOverCDP. Bun ships a WebSocket polyfill, but because Playwright bundles ws at build time the polyfill is never used, so the upgrade fails and the socket is torn down right after the 101.
Versions

Bun 1.3.14 (Linux x64)
playwright-core 1.61.0
Node 24.15.0 (works)

Possibly the same root cause as the open #9911 (and the closed #9357 / #28450). Filing a fresh report with a self-contained repro + the post-101 close signature in case it helps triage.

OS: macOS Silicon (Darwin 25.3.0 / macOS 26.3)
CPU: ARM — neon fp aes crc32 atomics

Crash output
Bun v1.4.0 (324c5f012) macOS Silicon
macOS v26.3
activeArgs: "claude"
Features: Bun.stderr(2) Bun.stdin(2) Bun.stdout(2) WebSocket(2) abort_signal(13) fetch(70) jsc spawn(34) standalone_executable yaml_parse(124) claude_code
Elapsed: 8348ms | User: 2265ms | Sys: 1033ms
RSS: 0.68 GB | Peak: 0.68 GB | Commit: 0.18 GB | Faults: 10237 | Machine: 38.65 GB
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x214

Bun report: https://bun.report/1.4.0/M_1324c5f0mgggkE+hogCu+i8sC+16gtC2o7+sCu7i22C+i9yd2vutfmu5gc2/18gB+4lxKmur+f2y78fm44kT__A2AohB
What I was doing
Running Claude Code (claude) — a Bun standalone executable — in a multi-agent session that spawned ~34 child processes and made ~70 HTTP fetch calls concurrently. The session had been running for ~8 seconds at time of crash.
Prelim hypothesis
Address 0x214 (decimal 532) is a near-null dereference — consistent with reading a fixed-offset field from a null/freed pointer. Given jsc spawn(34) and fetch(70) running concurrently, the likely candidate is a race condition where a spawned-process handle is freed/nulled while a fetch or abort-signal callback still holds a reference to it.
Reproduction
Hard to provide a minimal repro since it requires a Bun standalone executable making many concurrent spawns + fetches. The jsc spawn(34) + fetch(70) combination in ~8 seconds of elapsed time seems to be the trigger threshold on Apple Silicon.

1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a minimal index.html file on a Windows system with the following content:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>Test page</body>
</html>

Open a terminal in the same directory and run:
bun index.html


Wait for the dev server to start and show the http://localhost:3000/ address.
Type o and press Enter to trigger the "open in browser" shortcut.

Bug explanation:
Bun's built-in HTML dev server internally calls spawn("start", ...) to open the browser on Windows. However, start is a built-in command of cmd.exe, not a standalone executable file that exists in the system $PATH. Invoking it directly via spawn() will always fail with an ENOENT error on Windows.
What is the expected behavior?
Pressing the o shortcut should launch the system's default web browser and automatically open http://localhost:3000/.
What do you see instead?
The terminal throws the following error and the browser does not open:
 DEV  Bun v1.3.14 ready in 15.07 ms

➜ http://localhost:3000/

Press h + Enter to show shortcuts
o
error: Executable not found in $PATH: "start"
  path: "start",
 errno: -4058,
  code: "ENOENT"

      at spawn (unknown:1:1)
      at internal:html:251:20
      at emit (node:events:95:22)
      at addChunk (internal:streams/readable:264:47)
      at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (internal:streams/readable:242:18)
      at internalRead (native:38:40)
      at processTicksAndRejections (native:7:39)

Bun v1.3.14 (Windows x64)

Additional information

The HTML dev server itself works correctly and serves files as expected; only the o (open browser) shortcut is broken.
Maybe this is a Windows-only issue.
Suggested fix: On Windows, wrap the start command with cmd.exe /c, for example:
spawn("cmd", ["/c", "start", url])

t: Bun `Image.avif()` produces malformed `iref` box in grid-based AVIF
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Bun.Image.avif() encodes large images as a grid-based AVIF (multiple 512×512 tiles). When it does, the iref (Item Reference) box in the output file specifies version=0 but writes 32-bit entry sizes, violating the ISOBMFF spec.
The resulting .avif files work in Chrome and Safari but fail in Firefox with:

The image cannot be displayed because it contains errors.

import { Bun } from 'bun';

// Needs to be large enough to trigger grid encoding (~>512px)
const input = Bun.file('large_image.png');
const img = await input.image();
const buf = await img.avif({ quality: 80 }).arrayBuffer();

// Write to file
await Bun.write('/tmp/output.avif', buf);
Open /tmp/output.avif in Firefox → error.
What is the expected behavior?
Grid-based AVIF images generated by Bun.Image.avif() should use the correct iref box version field — either version 1+ (with 32-bit sizes) or version 0 with proper 16-bit sizes — so the files are valid per the ISOBMFF spec and work in all browsers, including Firefox.
What do you see instead?
Using avifdec --info (libavif 1.4.2) the file decodes successfully, confirming modern libavif is lenient about this bug. But many deployed Firefox versions bundle older libavif versions that do strict version-based parsing.
Good file (sharp-generated, works everywhere):

Single-image AVIF (no grid)
No iref box needed
still_picture=1, High Profile, yuv444p

Bad file (Bun-generated, fails in Firefox):
Box: ftyp, size: 28
Box: meta, size: 902
Box: mdat, size: 1 (64-bit: 859650)

--- iref box dump ---
iref version: 0  (should mean 16-bit sizes)
SingleItemTypeReferenceBox:
  size (as 32-bit): 0x00000024 = 36  ← spec says 16-bit for version 0!
  type: "dimg"
  from_item_ID: 13
  reference_count: 12

The iref box should either:

Use version > 0 to match the 32-bit entry sizes, or
Use 16-bit entry sizes to match version=0

Additional information

Small images (<512px) that don't trigger grid encoding appear to produce valid AVIF files.
The JPEG output from Bun.Image.jpeg() is unaffected.
The file uses compatible brands avifmiafmif1 (possibly reordered from the more common avifmif1miaf), but the brand order is not a spec violation.

node:child_process does not publish diagnostics_channel events (breaks Sentry childProcessIntegration and OpenTelemetry)
b:
Summary
node:child_process never publishes events to node:diagnostics_channel, even though node:diagnostics_channel itself is fully implemented. This silently breaks ecosystem instrumentation that subscribes to these channels - most notably Sentry's childProcessIntegration and OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for subprocesses.
Expected behavior (Node.js)
Calling spawn(), fork(), exec(), or execFile() publishes to:

channel('child_process') → { process } on every async spawn
tracingChannel('child_process.spawn').start → { process, options } before spawn
tracingChannel('child_process.spawn').end → { process } on success
tracingChannel('child_process.spawn').error → { process, error } on failure

Actual behavior (Bun)
No events are ever published. Subscribers receive nothing.
Reproduction
import diagnostics_channel from 'node:diagnostics_channel';

diagnostics_channel.subscribe('child_process', (msg) => {
  console.log('got event', msg); // never fires in Bun
});

Bun.spawn('echo', ['hello']);
Impact

Sentry's childProcessIntegration produces no spans for subprocesses
OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for child processes is fully blind
Any APM tool relying on diagnostics_channel for subprocess observability is silently broken

Fix
#30080 implements the fix with full test coverage (7 new tests + upstream Node parallel test). It has two LGTM reviews from @claude but has been awaiting a human maintainer review since May 4th. The branch currently has a merge conflict that needs resolving before it can land.

.cjs files (CommonJS dual-format compat files)
.gen.js files (nested generated code)
Files in deeply nested subdirectories

npm install does not have this issue on the same machine.
