Dev server ships HTML route module as a JS HMR module when a failed CSS root recovers
b:
Found while testing the fix for #31903 (PR #31905), which made this path reachable in debug builds.
Scenario
Dev server with an HTML route linking a CSS file. The client loads the page successfully, then a hot reload makes the CSS root fail (e.g. url(./missing.png) fails to resolve), then another hot reload fixes the CSS file.
What happens
The recovery hot update contains the HTML route's JS module (replaceModules receives {"index.html": ...}) but the payload is not flagged as a server-side route update, so the client does not call performRouteReload() before processing the modules. index.html is a root module that does not self-accept, so replaceModules takes the "not accepted" failure path:

Debug builds of the HMR client runtime crash on DEBUG.ASSERT(!boundary.endsWith(".html")); // caller should have already reloaded in src/runtime/bake/hmr-module.ts.
Release builds fall back to fullReload() after printing the "Hot update was not accepted" warning, so recovery works but through the wrong path and with a misleading console message.

Expected
When a failed CSS root recovers and the HTML route's module changes as a result, the update should be delivered as a route update (client performs a route reload) instead of shipping the HTML module through replaceModules.
Repro
With a debug build, append a connected client recovery step to the test "css url resolve error on hot reload is recoverable" in test/bake/dev/css.test.ts (added in #31905): keep the client from the error phase alive, write valid CSS again, and interact with the client. The client fixture exits with ASSERTION FAILED ... at replaceModules. The existing recovery tests ("css import before create", "css import before create project relative") do not hit this because their clients are in the fatal-error state from the initial load, and hasFatalError && reader.hasMoreData() full-reloads before modules are processed.

t: Dev server debug assert: !chunk.content.is_css() when a CSS rebuild fails to parse

Debug builds hit this assertion when a dev server rebuild produces a CSS chunk while parse_graph().css_file_count == 0:
panic: assertion failed: !chunk.content.is_css()
bun_bundler::linker_context::generate_chunks_in_parallel::generate_chunks_in_parallel::<true>
    src/bundler/linker_context/generateChunksInParallel.rs:132
<bun_bundler::bundle_v2::BundleV2>::finish_from_bake_dev_server
    src/bundler/bundle_v2.rs

css_file_count is only incremented when a parse task completes with a CSS AST (result.ast.css.is_some() in on_parse_task_complete), so when the only CSS file in a hot-reload rebuild fails to parse or hits a resolution error, the count stays 0 while the chunk list still contains a CSS chunk, and the debug_assert!(!chunk.content.is_css()) in the else branch fires.

bun bd test test/bake/dev/css.test.ts -t "syntax error crash"
bun bd test test/bake/dev/css.test.ts -t "css import before create project relative"

Verified on the unmodified merge-base (a1dd647) with src/ checked out clean, so this predates any recent loader changes. CI does not catch it because test lanes run release builds where debug_assert! compiles out; the release behavior silently skips the CSS dedup/prepare pass for those chunks.
Found while validating #28923.

t: Bun.Image: Expose raw RGBA buffer from Bun.Image API
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun.Image allows encoding images into common formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP) and exposes the result via .bytes(), .buffer(), .blob(), etc. However, there is no way to obtain access to the raw RGBA pixel data after decode or transformation (resize, rotate, etc.). Some applications require direct manipulation or analysis of raw pixel data, and extracting this requires additional decoding steps outside Bun.Image.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Expose a method or encoding option in the Bun.Image pipeline to provide direct access to the raw RGBA (or RGB) buffer. Ideally, for example, an encode("raw") or .raw() terminal that allows subsequent .bytes(), .buffer(), .blob(), etc., to return a pixel buffer instead of an encoded image. This would enable interoperable and efficient low-level manipulation without having to round-trip through PNG or other formats.
What alternatives have you considered?

Using .png(), then decoding the image manually (inefficient, extra step)
Using native modules or non-Bun pipelines to manipulate buffers
Implementing a JS-side decoder or relying on external libraries

t: repl: terminal width is cached at startup and never refreshed (no SIGWINCH handling)
b:
What
The interactive REPL (src/runtime/cli/repl.rs) caches the terminal width once in setup_terminal() and never refreshes it:

Repl.terminal_width defaults to 80 and is only overwritten from Output::TERMINAL_SIZE at startup
Output::TERMINAL_SIZE is never populated anywhere in the tree (no store() call sites; run_command.rs has a comment noting "Output.terminal_size is never populated; query stdout"), so in practice the REPL always runs with terminal_width == 80
There is no SIGWINCH handler, so resizing the terminal mid-session has no effect

Symptoms
All width-dependent rendering in refresh_line() uses the stale value:

The cursor-restore guard (if cursor_pos < self.terminal_width) emits \r + CUF based on the cached width; when the typed line wraps on the real (narrower) terminal, the cursor lands one row below the text and the next \r+ESC[2K clears the wrong row, leaving duplicated prompt lines
The inline ghost-suggestion wrap guard (added in #30413) inherits the same limitation: a suggestion that fits per the cached 80 columns can still wrap on a narrower real terminal

Cosmetic only (cleared by Ctrl+L/Enter), but visible on any terminal narrower than 80 columns, no resize required.
Fix direction
Either install a SIGWINCH handler that writes Output::TERMINAL_SIZE (making the comment at bun_core/output.rs:300 true), or query TIOCGWINSZ directly the way update_interactive_command.rs::get_terminal_size() does, and re-read it in refresh_line() / at prompt redraw.
Noted during review of #30413 (#30413 (comment)).

t: Bun.Image.metadata() exposes only width/height/format (no colorspace / hasAlpha / channels)
b:
What is the problem this feature will solve?
Bun.Image.prototype.metadata() returns only { width, height, format }. There is no way to inspect the source image's colour space, alpha presence, or channel count.
This matters for content-negotiation logic — e.g. serving PNG/WebP only when the source actually has transparency, and JPEG otherwise. Today that decision can't be made from metadata(); it requires re-decoding the image with another library (sharp), which defeats the purpose of a built-in image API.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Expose richer fields from metadata(), matching sharp where practical:

space / colorspace (e.g. srgb, cmyk, b-w)
hasAlpha (boolean)
channels (number)

Optionally density, hasProfile, orientation.
What alternatives have you considered?
Falling back to sharp solely to read metadata.
Related to the broader sharp-compatibility tracking (#30032), but filed separately as it's a focused, self-contained addition. Bun 1.3.14.

t: Bun.Image: CMYK JPEG decode fails with "Image: decode failed"

1.3.14 (Linux x64, glibc)
What steps will reproduce the bug?
Create a baseline CMYK JPEG and transform it with Bun.Image:
magick -size 64x64 xc:cyan -colorspace CMYK cmyk.jpg   # any 4-component (CMYK/YCCK) JPEG
const bytes = await Bun.file("cmyk.jpg").bytes();
await new Bun.Image(bytes).resize(32, 32).jpeg().bytes();
What is the expected behavior?
The CMYK JPEG is decoded and re-encoded to sRGB, like libvips/sharp and ImageMagick do (they auto-convert CMYK→sRGB on output).
What do you see instead?
The pipeline throws Image: decode failed.
Notably, await new Bun.Image(bytes).metadata() succeeds and returns { width, height, format: "jpeg" } — the header parses fine, but pixel decoding of 4-component (CMYK / YCCK) JPEGs fails.
Additional information
CMYK JPEGs are common in print-oriented / publishing image libraries. sharp (libvips) and ImageMagick both decode them and convert to sRGB. This currently forces a fallback to sharp for the affected images.

t: ReadableStream::isLocked in C++ never matches: nothing stores $reader === true
b:
What
WebCore::ReadableStream::isLocked (both overloads in src/jsc/bindings/webcore/ReadableStream.cpp) checks:
return readableStream->getDirect(globalObject->vm(), privateName).isTrue();
but nothing in the tree stores the literal true in the $reader private slot. The streams builtins store either a reader object (getReader(), ReadableStreamInternals.ts acquireReadableStreamDefaultReader) or an {} sentinel ($readDirectStream, lazyLoadStream, readableStreamToArrayBufferDirect), and they define lockedness as:
// ReadableStreamInternals.ts
export function isReadableStreamLocked(stream) {
  return !!$getByIdDirectPrivate(stream, "reader") || stream.$bunNativePtr === -1;
}
So the C++ helper returns false for every stream, locked or not. (The $bunNativePtr === -1 arm also appears to be dead: nothing assigns -1 anymore.)
Consequences

ReadableStream__cancel early-returns unless isLocked, so the Rust stream.cancel() teardown calls are currently no-ops (call sites in FileSink.rs, Blob.rs, subprocess/Writable.rs, ResumableSink.rs).
Guards using the Rust ReadableStream::is_locked never fire for locked streams: Body.rs (used-body check), ResumableSink.rs (locked-or-disturbed check), RequestContext.rs ("was locked but it shouldn't be").
In RequestContext.rs's response-stream completion path, !stream.is_locked(...) is always true, so that branch's condition reduces to !is_in_progress.

Why this was not fixed in #31689
Widening isLocked to the builtin definition makes the dead ReadableStream__cancel live at six teardown call sites and changes the !is_locked branch in Bun.serve's response-stream completion (assignToStream always leaves $reader set, either a real reader or {}). Both need their own validation. #31689 instead scoped its preflight to a new ReadableStream__hasReader that reads the private slot directly.
Suggested fix
Make both C++ isLocked overloads match the builtin definition (reader && !reader.isUndefinedOrNull()), then audit the consumers above (cancel-on-teardown semantics and the serve branch), and fold ReadableStream__hasReader into the fixed helper.

What platform is your computer?
Alpine Linux 3.22.4, aarch64, AWS ECS Fargate (2 tasks behind a NAT gateway).
What steps can reproduce the bug?
No minimal local repro yet — the trigger appears to need a real HTTP/2 origin plus a connection that sits idle long enough for an intermediary (NAT) to silently drop the socket. Production setup:

firebase-admin@13.8.0 messaging().sendEach() → FCM v1 over node:http2 (the SDK uses node:http2, not fetch).
Low send rate (a few pushes/minute per task), so HTTP/2 connections sit idle between calls.

What is the expected behavior?
Each FCM request completes in <1s, as it does on Bun 1.3.13 and on Node.
What do you see instead?
~16% of requests hang with no response, killed only by our app-level 15s timeout. Latency is strongly bimodal: healthy 0–1s vs hung 15s, nothing in between — the signature of a reused-but-dead (stale) connection.
Production evidence:

Deployed 1.3.14 at 18:35 → first hang at 18:43 (8 min later). Zero hangs before.
Rolled back to 1.3.13 → hangs stopped immediately (timeout logs: 10 per 35 min → 0).
Hangs occur across both tasks (not AZ-specific).

Suspected area
node:http2 + TLS connection reuse changes that landed in 1.3.14:

#30024 tls: native weak SSL_CTX cache + WeakGCMap SecureContext dedup
#29932 socket: replace us_socket_context_t with embedded groups

Likely related: #30307 (node:http2 misbehaving after idle), #30342 (node:http2 hang).

t: panic: Segmentation fault at address 0xD — "multiple threads are crashing" under Worker spawn/terminate churn (1.3.14, long-running server)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14 (stable), Linux x64 (kernel 6.17.0, Ubuntu, glibc)
What happened?
A long-running Bun.serve() daemon that dispatches work to a pool of ~15 new Worker() threads (spawn on demand, worker.unref(), respawn-on-close, worker.terminate() on shutdown) crashes several times a day with:
oh no: multiple threads are crashing
panic: Segmentation fault at address 0xD

The crashes correlate with worker spawn/terminate churn: the process is restarted frequently by a supervisor (PM2), and each restart terminates the pool (possibly with dispatches in flight) while new requests can race fresh new Worker() spawns. The panic signature matches #30205 (bun test 4x PARALLEL, v1.3.14-canary, addresses 0xD0/0x68) — this report adds a non-test reproduction surface: plain Worker API on a stable release.
Crash reports (bun.report)

NativeZlib/NativeBrotli/NativeZstd estimated_size reads JsCell state from the GC marking thread
b:
The estimatedSize codegen contract (src/codegen/class-definitions.ts, "Called from any thread") means it can run on JSC's concurrent GC marking thread. NativeBrotli::estimated_size (src/runtime/node/zlib/NativeBrotli.rs) and NativeZstd::estimated_size (src/runtime/node/zlib/NativeZstd.rs) read self.stream.get().mode through a JsCell, whose Sync impl is documented (src/jsc/JSCell.rs) as sound only under JS-thread affinity. While the JS thread holds &mut inside a with_mut drive loop, the marking thread can materialize an aliasing &, which is a Rust aliasing violation (practically benign today: the fields read are fixed after construction).
Fix pattern: cache the per-mode footprint in a plain immutable field set at construction, as CompressionStreamTransformer does after #31728, or use an atomic like BlockList::estimated_size (src/runtime/node/net/BlockList.rs).

t: X509Certificate.ca: incorrect true value when basicConstraints is absent
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0-debug+a3464c666
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
import { X509Certificate } from "node:crypto";

// Self-signed X.509 v1 certificate. No extensions of any kind — no
// basicConstraints, no keyUsage. Per RFC 5280 this is NOT a CA.
const cert = new X509Certificate(`-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIICAjCCAagCCQDFYI3zR8B/izAKBggqhkjOPQQDAjAPMQ0wCwYDVQQDDAR0ZXN0
MB4XDTI2MDUyODE3MDYwNVoXDTM2MDUyNTE3MDYwNVowDzENMAsGA1UEAwwEdGVz
dDCCAUswggEDBgcqhkjOPQIBMIH3AgEBMCwGByqGSM49AQECIQD/////AAAAAQAA
AAAAAAAAAAAAAP///////////////zBbBCD/////AAAAAQAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAP//
/////////////AQgWsY12Ko6k+ez671VdpiGvGUdBrDMU7D2O848PifSYEsDFQDE
nTYIhucEk2pmeOETnSa3gZ9+kARBBGsX0fLhLEJH+Lzm5WOkQPJ3A32BLeszoPSh
OUXYmMKWT+NC4v4af5uO5+tKfA+eFivOM1drMV7Oy7ZAaDe/UfUCIQD/////AAAA
AP//////////vOb6racXnoTzucrC/GMlUQIBAQNCAAR1hd/nVei+or93b6B6lA0v
U52t80TD/E7NVfub7GJbHxbCX48zQH8YzMEsi/C/0G6N0/kf/ilwVuZXzwPVuTM/
MAoGCCqGSM49BAMCA0gAMEUCIFTzv2XBNlegDgPaDlhmcxwOx9FaIfy/9SF6+qmV
7IPSAiEAkQ1u46qvg4y2tr47yLzr0PbtPVYgjNS7VYLNDWf/btw=
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
`);

console.log(cert.ca);         // Node: false   | Bun: true
console.log(typeof cert.ca);  // Node: boolean | Bun: boolean (type matches; value wrong)
What is the expected behavior?
Same as Node: false. A certificate without basicConstraints (or with basicConstraints CA:FALSE) is not a CA per RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9, regardless of X.509 version.
What do you see instead?
true — bun marks the cert as a CA when it has no basicConstraints extension.
The same wrong value also leaks into cert.toLegacyObject() and cert.toJSON() output (the ca: field is set there too).
Additional information
OpenSSL/BoringSSL's X509_check_ca() returns:

0 — not a CA
1 — v3 with basicConstraints CA:TRUE
2 — X.509 v1 certificate (historical compat)
3 — self-signed v3 with extensions but no basicConstraints
4 — Netscape CA
5 — keyUsage has keyCertSign

Node's crypto_x509.cc checks X509_check_ca(...) == 1, so values 2–5 correctly return false. The cert above is v1, so X509_check_ca returns 2.
Bun's getter (src/jsc/bindings/ncrypto.cpp:1235 → X509View::isCA()) also writes == 1, but the property reports true on this v1 cert, so something is yielding 1 for a value that BoringSSL should return 2 for, or there's another code path setting ca independently. The two consumers I found are:

src/jsc/bindings/JSX509CertificatePrototype.cpp:473 (prototype getter)
src/jsc/bindings/JSX509Certificate.cpp:887

t: CI: bunx.test.ts fails on all platforms — @angular/cli@latest now requires Node >= 24.15.0, bun reports 24.3.0
b:
What happened
test/cli/install/bunx.test.ts > should handle package that requires node 24 is failing on every platform in CI since ~Jun 4 (first seen on PR builds 60281 and 60284; main's last green build 60245 predates it). This blocks all PRs.
Cause
The test runs bun x --bun @angular/cli@latest --help against the live npm registry. Angular published a new @angular/cli@latest whose version check now requires:
Node.js version v24.3.0 detected.
The Angular CLI requires a minimum Node.js version of v22.22.3 or v24.15.0 or v26.0.0.

Fix
Bump the self-reported Node.js version to a 24.x release ≥ 24.15.0 — latest is 24.16.0, and NODE_MODULE_VERSION is still 137, so the N-API/addon ABI is unchanged:

scripts/build/deps/nodejs-headers.ts: NODEJS_VERSION = "24.3.0" → "24.16.0" (headers tarball exists at nodejs.org; ABI constant stays 137)
Probably in lockstep (as in the 22.6.0 → 24.3.0 bump, [publish images] 172aecb): scripts/bootstrap.sh, scripts/bootstrap.ps1, .buildkite/Dockerfile (ARG NODE_VERSION), plus any tests pinning the version string (test/js/node/process/process.test.js).

t: `bun test --isolate`: module records retained across per-file global swaps → linear RSS growth (OOMs large suites); still present in 1.3.14
b:
What versions of Bun are running?
1.3.13+bf2e2cecf
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Linux 7.0.0-14-generic x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
mkdir bun-isolate-leak && cd bun-isolate-leak

# 1000 trivial modules + a barrel that imports them all
mkdir mods
for i in $(seq 0 999); do echo "export function f$i(){return $i}" > "mods/m$i.ts"; done
: > graph.ts; for i in $(seq 0 999); do echo "import './mods/m$i';" >> graph.ts; done

# N test files that each import the shared graph
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  printf "import './graph';\nimport { test } from 'bun:test';\ntest('noop', () => {});\n" > "t$i.test.ts"
done

# --isolate: peak RSS grows with file count
/usr/bin/time -v bun test --isolate t{1..10}.test.ts   # ~106 MB
/usr/bin/time -v bun test --isolate t{1..20}.test.ts   # ~148 MB

# default (shared global): flat
/usr/bin/time -v bun test            t{1..20}.test.ts   # ~65 MB
(bun test --isolate --preload ./graph.ts t{1..N}.test.ts reproduces identically — the growth tracks the graph, whether imported per-file or via preload.)
bun test --isolate runs each test file in a fresh global within one process. Module records / namespace objects instantiated for one file are not released when the global is swapped for the next file, so peak RSS grows linearly with the number of files, proportional to each file's imported module-graph size. On a large real suite (≈300 files sharing a big import graph) this reaches ~13 GB and OOMs; the run never completes. Default (shared-global) mode loads the graph once and stays flat.
This is not mock.module-related (reproduces with zero mocks) and not generic-native (a bun:sqlite-only graph stays flat). It is the JS module graph itself not being reclaimed across --isolate global swaps. 1.3.14 reduces the per-file slope ~12% but does not fix it.
What is the expected behavior?
When --isolate swaps to a fresh global between files, the finished file's module records / namespace objects should be reclaimed, so peak RSS stays roughly flat across files — as it does in default (shared-global) mode.
What do you see instead?
Peak RSS grows linearly with file count. Module records from already-finished files are retained across the global swap. On large suites this OOMs (and under --parallel, workers hit their own OOM ceiling; on ≤1.3.13 the coordinator silently restarted them, masking the failure as a green exit 0).

t: bun build --splitting produces chunks that hang at runtime (circular chunk dependency deadlock)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14 (also reproduced on 1.3.11)
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.17.0-1021-nvidia aarch64
Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

What steps can reproduce the bug?

Build a large TypeScript project (~6000 modules) with code splitting:

bun build src/entrypoints/cli.tsx \
  --outdir=dist \
  --splitting \
  --target=bun


The entry point (cli.js) uses dynamic import() to load chunks lazily.


Run the built output:


bun dist/cli.js -p "hello"
What is the expected behavior?
The process starts, loads the necessary chunks, and responds to the prompt.
What do you see instead?
The process hangs indefinitely — no output, no error, 100% CPU on one core. It never progresses past the chunk loading phase.
Key observations:



Test
Result




bun dist/cli.js --version
✅ Works (fast path, no chunk loading)


bun run src/entrypoints/cli.tsx -p "hello"
✅ Works (dev mode, no splitting)


bun dist/cli.js -p "hello" (splitting build)
❌ Hangs


bun dist-nosplit/cli.js -p "hello" (no-splitting)
✅ Works


Same splitting build on Bun 1.3.11
❌ Same hang


Same splitting build on Bun 1.3.14
❌ Same hang



Workaround
Building with --no-splitting produces a working single-file bundle. But this defeats code splitting — the single-file bundle causes ~500MB RSS vs ~35MB for --version with the split version.
Root cause hypothesis
This appears to be a circular dependency in the chunk graph created by the splitting algorithm. The source modules themselves may not have circular imports, but the splitting algorithm's chunk assignment creates import cycles between chunks that deadlock at runtime.
The --metafile-md output shows 244 code-split chunks with 258 dynamic entry points. The main chunk (cli.js, 5 KB) loads main-*.js (0.34 MB) via dynamic import, which in turn depends on other chunks.
Additional info

Project: https://github.com/GhostDragon124/claude-code-best
Bundle size: ~28 MB, 6037 input modules, 244 chunks
Full --metafile-md output: Available on request (14 MB markdown file)
strace output: Shows the process spinning on read()/write() on file descriptors, consistent with deadlock

bun update writes a bun.lock that fails the very next bun install --frozen-lockfile
b:
What
bun update writes a bun.lock that does not validate against the package.json it itself just wrote, so the immediate next bun install --frozen-lockfile fails with lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen.
This breaks weekly "update dependencies" CI bots: they run bun update, commit the result, open a PR, and CI immediately red-X's on bun install --frozen-lockfile.
Version
Bun 1.3.14 (macOS arm64, also seen on ubuntu-24.04-arm GitHub runners).
Reproduce
mkdir bun-update-repro && cd bun-update-repro

cat > package.json <<'PKG'
{
  "name": "bun-update-repro",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "nuxt": "4.4.6",
    "vite": "7.3.3"
  },
  "overrides": {
    "vite": "$vite"
  }
}
PKG

bun install                                  # locks nuxt@4.4.6, vite@7.3.3
sed -i.bak 's/"4.4.6"/"^4.4.6"/; s/"7.3.3"/"^7.3.3"/' package.json && rm package.json.bak
bun install --frozen-lockfile                # passes — starting state is consistent

bun update                                    # bumps nuxt + vite, "Saved lockfile"
bun install --frozen-lockfile                # ❌ "lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen"
Workaround: bun install after bun update reconciles the lockfile.
What bun update leaves wrong
After bun update bumps nuxt 4.4.6 -> 4.4.7 and vite 7.3.3 -> 7.3.5 and updates package.json, the produced bun.lock:

Stale workspace snapshot — embedded package.json copy at the top still shows pre-bump ranges ("nuxt": "^4.4.6", "vite": "^7.3.3").
Stale overrides snapshot — "overrides": { "vite": "^7.3.3" } instead of "^7.3.5".
Orphan transitive entry — "vite-node/vite": ["vite@7.3.3", ...] lingers even though root vite is now 7.3.5 and the "vite": "$vite" override should propagate.

A plain bun install afterwards reconciles all three.
Trigger ingredients
All three are needed:

A self-referencing override: "overrides": { "vite": "$vite" }. Without it, frozen-lockfile passes after bun update.
A dep with a transitive on the overridden package (nuxt → vite-node → vite).
Starting bun.lock versions older than what bun update would install.

Expected
bun update should leave bun.lock in a state where bun install --frozen-lockfile passes — i.e., refresh the workspace and overrides snapshots and re-resolve transitives of overridden packages.

t: bun minifier doesn't remove `return` on single-expression arrow functions
streaming `Bun.hash.xxHash3` for hashing files larger than RAM
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun.hash.xxHash3 needs the entire input passed in at once, as a single buffer or string. That causes two problems with large files:

You can't hash a file bigger than available RAM, since you can't hold the whole thing in memory to pass it in.
Even when a file does fit, reading it fully into memory just to hash it spikes memory usage — wasteful when hashing many large files (e.g. media assets).

I want to hash large files on disk at xxHash3 speed, without loading each entire file into memory.
ASC MHL (Media Hash List), the standard manifest format for verifying media-file integrity across film and post-production, names XXH3 as an accepted hash algorithm. These manifests store an XXH3 value per file and later verify against it, and the files involved — camera footage, masters — are routinely larger than RAM. A streaming hasher that reproduces the canonical XXH3 value is what makes those large-file integrity workflows possible at all.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A streaming/incremental xxHash3 hasher with the same shape as the existing CryptoHasher: create a hasher, call .update(chunk) repeatedly while reading the file in fixed-size chunks, then call .digest() for the final hash.
const hasher = new Bun.hash.xxHash3Updated(); // exact name/entry point up to you
for await (const chunk of Bun.file("huge.mov").stream()) {
  hasher.update(chunk);
}
const hash = hasher.digest(); // === Bun.hash.xxHash3(wholeFile)
It would need to:

Produce the exact same value as a one-shot Bun.hash.xxHash3 over the full file, so streaming and one-shot are interchangeable.
Stay SIMD-fast — no throughput regression versus the one-shot call.
Hold only one chunk at a time, so memory stays constant regardless of file size, making files larger than RAM hashable.

What alternatives have you considered?

CryptoHasher already does .update()/.digest() streaming, but only for cryptographic hashes (sha256, etc.), which are far slower than xxHash3 — too slow for large-file throughput.
Reading the whole file into memory and calling Bun.hash.xxHash3 once: fails outright above RAM size, and is memory-heavy otherwise.
Hashing each chunk separately and combining the results: changes the output, so it isn't a real xxHash3 of the file and can't match the one-shot value.

Summary

t: tls: sni_cb should return SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_ALERT_FATAL when SNICallback throws or returns non-SecureContext
b:
Follow-up from #31155
Backlink: PR #31155 — comment #31155 (comment)
Requested by @cirospaciari.
Problem
In packages/bun-usockets/src/crypto/openssl.c, sni_cb (the OpenSSL/BoringSSL SNI servername callback registered via SSL_CTX_set_tlsext_servername_callback) currently always returns SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_OK, regardless of the outcome of the JS SNICallback.
This means:

If the JS SNICallback throws an error, the handshake falls through and continues using the default/existing certificate, rather than aborting.
If SNICallback returns a non-SecureContext result (or calls back with an error the way Node's API requires), the handshake still proceeds — this is a fail-open behavior that does not match Node.js semantics.

Expected Behavior (Node.js)
Node's SelectSNIContextCallback returns SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_ALERT_FATAL with *al set to an appropriate alert (e.g. SSL_AD_UNRECOGNIZED_NAME or SSL_AD_INTERNAL_ERROR) when the JS callback signals an error. The TLS handshake is aborted with a fatal alert.
Root Cause
The on_server_name callback in us_listen_socket_t returns an SSL_CTX* (owned reference) or NULL. A NULL return currently cannot distinguish:

"No override, continue with the default certificate" (benign)
"JS threw or returned a non-SecureContext value" (should abort)

Required Work

Thread an error sentinel (e.g. a flag in the loop SSL data, or a separate out-param on on_server_name) from us_dispatch_server_name (Rust) through the C on_server_name function pointer back into sni_cb.
In sni_cb, after us_internal_ssl_loop_state_restore, check the sentinel:

If it signals a JS exception or invalid return: set *al to SSL_AD_UNRECOGNIZED_NAME (or SSL_AD_INTERNAL_ERROR) and return SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_ALERT_FATAL.
If NULL without error ("no override"): return SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_OK or SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_NOACK to continue with the default cert.


Ensure the alert is not flushed prematurely mid-ClientHello (the abort must happen at the correct point in the TLS state machine).

Files Involved

packages/bun-usockets/src/crypto/openssl.c — sni_cb, us_listen_socket_on_server_name
packages/bun-usockets/src/internal/internal.h — us_listen_socket_t::on_server_name callback signature
src/runtime/socket/Listener.rs — us_dispatch_server_name

b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11
What platform is your computer?
Linux arm64; also reproduces on macOS arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Minimal reproducer:
  const http = require("node:http");
  const req = http.request({
    method: "CONNECT",
    host: "127.0.0.1",
    port: 1055,
    path: "example.com:443",
  });
  req.on("connect", (res, socket) => { console.log("ok", res.statusCode); socket.end(); });
  req.on("error", (e) => console.error("err", e.code, e.message));
  req.end();

What is the expected behavior?
TCP CONNECT to the proxy at 127.0.0.1:1055 requesting tunnel to example.com:443.
In Node.js this works; the proxy returns 200  Connection established and the connect event fires with the tunneled socket.
What do you see instead?
Throws synchronously on req.end():
  TypeError: fetch() URL is invalid
   code: "ERR_INVALID_URL"
        at go (node:_http_client:206:47)
        at startFetch (node:_http_client:266:16)
        at send (node:_http_client:305:17)

Additional information
Bun's node:_http_client shim routes http.request through fetch(), which has no representation for CONNECT (it's a hop-by-hop method, not a  content URL). opts.path here is a host:port tunnel target, not a URL path - fetch() rejects it.
Impact: Breaks every HTTP CONNECT proxy client in Node, notably @grpc/grpc-js proxy support (grpc_proxy / http_proxy envs are documented and widely used -- see @grpc/grpc-js/build/src/http_proxy.js). Any app that wants gRPC through an HTTP proxy currently can't do it in Bun.
Workaround in our codebase (in case it helps reproducing or comparing): hand-roll the tunnel with net.connect and re-emit connect to match Node's http.ClientRequest interface. ~80 lines.
Suggested fix: detect method === "CONNECT" in the shim, bypass the fetch path, and use raw TCP - same code path Node's real http module uses internally.

t: `LinearFifo::ordered_remove_item` uses wrong bounds in wrapped-buffer branch
b:
What version of Bun is running?
No response
What platform is your computer?
No response
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Summary
LinearFifo::ordered_remove_item has incorrect slice bounds when the readable region wraps around the end of the backing buffer.
In the wrapped case, the implementation splits into two sub-branches:

removing an item from the wrapped prefix (index < head)
removing an item from the tail segment before wrap (index >= head)

Both branches use the wrong expression for the wrapped-prefix length:

count - head
head - count

The correct wrapped-prefix length is:
let wrap_len = head + count - buf_len;
Because of this, ordered_remove_item can panic in debug builds or corrupt FIFO contents in release builds.
Affected code
File: src/collections/linear_fifo.rs
Current wrapped branch:
if index < head {
    shift_down_one(&mut buf[index..count - head]);
} else {
    let wrap = unsafe { ptr::read(buf.as_ptr()) };
    shift_down_one(&mut buf[index..]);
    unsafe { ptr::write(buf.as_mut_ptr().add(buf_len - 1), wrap) };
    shift_down_one(&mut buf[..head - count]);
}
Why this is wrong
When readable data wraps, the readable region is split into two segments:

tail: buf[head..buf_len)
wrapped prefix: buf[..wrap_len)

where:
wrap_len = head + count - buf_len
The two wrapped sub-branches correspond to those two segments:

index < head: the removed item lies in the wrapped prefix
index >= head: the removed item lies in the tail

That wrap_len must be used for shifts inside the wrapped prefix.
Also, in every valid wrapped state:
wrap_len <= head
because:
wrap_len = head + count - buf_len
count <= buf_len
=> wrap_len <= head
So buf[..wrap_len] stays entirely inside the wrapped prefix and does not overlap the tail segment buf[head..buf_len).
Bug 1: index < head
Current code:
shift_down_one(&mut buf[index..count - head]);
This is wrong because count - head is not the wrapped-prefix length.
Possible outcomes:

usize underflow when head > count
shifting too much or too little even when it does not underflow

Bug 2: index >= head
Current code:
shift_down_one(&mut buf[..head - count]);
This is wrong because head - count is not the wrapped-prefix length.
Possible outcomes:

usize underflow when head < count
release-only corruption from using a wrapped bogus bound

  bavail: s.bavail,
  bsize:  s.bsize,
  blocks: s.blocks,
  free_mb: Math.floor(s.bavail * s.bsize / 1048576),
});
For comparison, run the equivalent in Node.js on the same path.
What is the expected behavior?
bavail should match what Node.js returns (and what the Linux statvfs64 syscall reports). On the affected filesystem here:
{ bavail: 3248532185, bsize: 4096, blocks: 3747442852, free_mb: 12689578 }

That is, bavail is a uint32-or-larger block count (~3.2 × 10⁹ blocks of 4 KiB ≈ 13.3 TB free).
What do you see instead?
Bun returns bavail truncated to a signed 32-bit integer. The product bavail * bsize / 1048576 then comes out negative.
I observed this indirectly through Claude Code 2.1.153 (which is shipped as a Bun-compiled binary). Its disk-space diagnostic uses fs.statfs and reports:
the temp filesystem at /tmp/... is full (-4087625MB free)

That value is exactly what you get if bavail was reinterpreted as int32:
bavail (uint32) = 3,248,532,704
bavail (int32)  = 3,248,532,704 − 2^32 = −1,046,434,592
× 4096 / 1048576 ≈ −4,087,440 MB     ← matches the reported −4,087,625 MB
                                       (small drift = bavail changed between
                                        repro runs)

The same path through Node.js's fs.statfsSync on the same filesystem returns the correct positive value, so this is not a kernel quirk or statvfs64 issue — it's specifically in Bun's fs.statfs binding.
Additional information

Reproduces on btrfs with 13.3 TB free; the bug should reproduce on any Linux FS where bavail × bsize exceeds 2^31 bytes (≈ 2 GB), and more visibly past 2^31 blocks.
Bun's recent #31133 (closed) was a darwin-x64 struct-misalignment bug in the same API; this is a separate linux-x64 issue affecting bavail spe

t: Bun canary Rust fetch reuses sockets after `Connection: close` appears in a token list
b:
Summary
Bun canary's Rust HTTP/fetch implementation can reuse a socket after a response says the connection should close, when the Connection header is a comma-separated token list such as:
Connection: close, keep-alive
This appears to be specific to the canary Rust rewrite path. It was reproduced on Bun canary 1.4.0-canary.1+2148214d4 from oven-sh/bun@2148214d40fc9f844f61ae5f8575d6d94a9d038c.
This is not related to BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_EXPERIMENTAL_HTTP3_CLIENT or --experimental-http3-fetch; neither is enabled in the environment where this was originally observed.
Impact
Outgoing fetch() calls intermittently fail when Bun reuses a socket that the peer has already marked for closure. In application code the error is:
The socket connection was closed unexpectedly. For more information, pass `verbose: true` in the second argument to fetch()

In retries/observability this often appears as ECONNRESET. Switching the same workload to real npm undici, or forcing fetch(..., { keepalive: false }), avoids the failures.
Root Cause
The Rust HTTP client appears to compare the entire Connection header value against close or keep-alive.
Connection is a comma-separated token list. A response header like Connection: close, keep-alive must be parsed as tokens, and the presence of a close token should prevent socket reuse. close must also win if both close and keep-alive are present.
Because Bun does not currently recognize close inside a token list, it can return a closing socket to the pool and later reuse it for another request.
Minimal Reproduction
A raw HTTP/1.1 server responds with a fixed body and:
Content-Length: 2
Connection: close, keep-alive
It then delays socket close briefly. A concurrent POST workload against that server causes native Bun canary fetch to reuse the socket before the close is fully observed.
A regression test and fix are being opened in a related PR. The test uses a local node:net server and 500 concurrent POST fetches to make the issue deterministic.
Observations
Reproduced with the latest canary/Rust rewrite at the time of testing:



Client / mode
Requests
Completed
Failures




Native Bun canary fetch, default keepalive
2000
1017
983


Real npm undici
2000
2000
0


Native Bun canary fetch with { keepalive: false }
2000
2000
0


Patched Bun debug build
2000
2000
0



The newly added regression test fails on unpatched canary with about half the POST requests failing, and passes with the patch.
Expected Behavior
Bun should parse Connection as a comm

t: Add non-S4U Windows mode for Bun.cron OS-level jobs
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun.cron(path, schedule, title) on Windows currently registers OS-level cron jobs through Windows Task Scheduler using S4U semantics, per the Bun Cron docs.
That is a good default for Linux-crontab-like behavior because it can run as the registering user even when the user is not logged in and does not store a password. However, in managed enterprise Windows environments, S4U/batch-logon task registration can be denied for standard users unless they have the Windows user right SeBatchLogonRight / "Log on as a batch job" or equivalent policy allowance.
Observed result on a managed Windows workstation:
PS> bun run docs:cron:install -- --schedule "0 9 * * *"

t: ws client does not emit upgrade event in Bun 1.3.8
node:sqlite not implemented in Bun — forces dual-runtime code to fork imports
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
node:sqlite shipped stable in Node.js v22.5 (behind --experimental-sqlite) and unflagged in v23.x / v24.x. Deno 2.2 added it. Bun ships bun:sqlite with similar semantics but no node:sqlite shim, so any codebase that needs to run under both Node and Bun must either:

Fork the import per runtime (bun:sqlite vs node:sqlite), or
Pull in better-sqlite3 and pay the native-rebuild + node-gyp cost, defeating the point of using Bun.

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Expose node:sqlite as a thin shim over the existing bun:sqlite engine. API surface to cover:

DatabaseSync class — open, close, prepare, exec, function, aggregate, loadExtension, enableLoadExtension, location
StatementSync class — all, get, iterate, run, columns, setReadBigInts, setAllowBareNamedParameters
constants.SQLITE_*
backup() (Node v23.x+)
Session / applyChangeset (Node v23.x+)

Reusing the bun:sqlite engine should keep the native footprint zero-cost; only the API wrapper needs writing.
What alternatives have you considered?

bun:sqlite directly — works under Bun only, breaks portability.
better-sqlite3 — heavy native dep, slow install, defeats Bun's pitch.
Conditional imports — clutters every consumer module.

Real-world impact
Modern Node codebases are starting to standardize on node:sqlite for embedded storage (config, caches, queues) precisely because it removes the native-dep tax. Without a Bun shim, any package adopting node:sqlite becomes Bun-incompatible by default, which cuts against Bun's drop-in-replacement positioning.
Additional information

Duplicate of #20412 (open since 2026-02, last comment 2026-05-21, no maintainer commitment).
Filing fresh report to surface continued ecosystem pain — node:sqlite adoption has accelerated since #20412 was filed, and the silence on that issue suggests it's been deprioritized.
Could a maintainer comment on whether this is on any roadmap, or whether bun:sqlite-only is the intended long-term stance?

What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
Multiple (macOS, Linux, Windows) — affects Bun runtime regardless of host OS.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Any code path importing mkdtempDisposable from node:fs/promises crashes at module-load time under Bun:
import { mkdtempDisposable } from "node:fs/promises";
Bun aborts before any code runs:
SyntaxError: Export named 'mkdtempDisposable' not found in module 'node:fs/promises'.

What is the expected behavior?
Bun should export mkdtempDisposable (and the sync mkdtempSyncDisposable counterpart) from node:fs/promises / node:fs, matching Node.js v24.8+. The disposable returns an object with a path string and a Symbol.asyncDispose that wipes the directory on scope exit, intended for await using syntax.
What do you see instead?
Module fails to load. Any package depending on the export is unusable under Bun — even when the call site is on a cold path, because the import is resolved eagerly.
Real-world impact
A shipped Bun-targeted CLI eagerly resolved imports from two service modules that used mkdtempDisposable for scope-bound temp dirs (download staging, scratch dirs). Entire CLI crashed under Bun 1.3.13 before any subcommand could dispatch.
Workaround: drop the disposable, use mkdtemp + try/finally calling rm(..., { recursive: true, force: true }). Same semantics, portable across Node and Bun.

Duplicate of #24499 (filed against 1.3.1, still open and confirmed). Filing fresh report against 1.3.13 to confirm export still missing two minor versions later.
PR #22068 (Claude/robobun, August 2025) appears to implement this but stalled awaiting human review for ~3 months.
Could a maintainer either land #22068 or comment on what's blocking it? Missing export forces every downstream Bun consumer to fork their disposable usage.

git clone https://github.com/THernandez03/bun-update-interactive-issue

 Packages   Current   Target    Latest
───────────────────────────────────────
 □ ai       0.0.1     4.3.16    4.3.16
 □ git-cz   1.8.4     4.9.0     4.9.0
 □ taze     0.18.0    0.19.3    0.19.3

What do you see instead? (v1.4.0)

 □ git-czr....1.8.4....4.9.0....4.9.0
 □ tazer....0.18.0....0.19.3....0.19.3

Spaces between package names and version columns are replaced by visible .... dots. Every column separator is corrupted.

Note: the r suffix on package names (air, git-czr, tazer) is a separate artifact already tracked in #30693 and addressed by PR #30694.
This issue is specifically about the dots artifact in the version columns, which is NOT fixed by #30694.


Root cause
The version column rendering in src/runtime/cli/update_interactive_command.rs uses diff_fmt() to render version strings. diff_fmt() emits ANSI underline and dim sequences (\x1b[4m, \x1b[2m, \x1b[0m) around version segments to highlight the differing parts.
These version strings are then composed into the row via Output::pretty(format_args!("...{}", version_col)). The function-form Output::pretty substitutes {} at runtime, then feeds the combined result to pretty_fmt_runtime for <tag>-to-ANSI rewriting.
pretty_fmt_runtime does not expect arbitrary ANSI bytes in the substituted value. When it encounters \x1b bytes from the ANSI underline/dim sequences interleaved with the padding spaces and column separators, the byte stream around those padding characters is corrupted, and the padding renders as visible . characters instead of spaces.

t: bun install forwards Authorization header on cross-host redirect (npm.pkg.github.com → Azure Blob), causing 401
b:
Summary
bun install forwards the Authorization header when following a cross-host redirect from npm.pkg.github.com → Azure Blob storage (pkg-npm.githubusercontent.com). This causes a 401 from Azure because Azure pre-signed URLs are invalidated by any additional auth header. Per RFC 9110 §15.4, clients MUST NOT forward authorization credentials to a different host on redirect.
This makes it impossible to install packages from GitHub Packages using bun install, regardless of how the token is configured.
Versions

Bun: 1.3.14 (also reproduced on 1.3.10, 1.2.x)
Platform: Darwin arm64 (Apple Silicon), also reproducible on Linux
Registry: npm.pkg.github.com (GitHub Packages)

Steps to reproduce

Add a scoped private package from GitHub Packages to package.json:

{
  "dependencies": {
    "@myorg/my-package": "^1.0.0"
  }
}

Configure auth in bunfig.toml:

[install.scopes]
"@myorg" = { token = "ghp_YOUR_TOKEN", url = "https://npm.pkg.github.com" }

Run bun install. The download step fails with 401.

What actually happens
GitHub Packages redirects tarball downloads to Azure Blob storage:
GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@myorg/my-package/1.0.0/<hash>
Authorization: Bearer ghp_YOUR_TOKEN
→ 302 Location: https://pkg-npm.githubusercontent.com/<signed-path>?sig=...&se=...&sp=...

GET https://pkg-npm.githubusercontent.com/<signed-path>?sig=...&se=...&sp=...
Authorization: Bearer ghp_YOUR_TOKEN   ← bun forwards this
→ 401  (Azure rejects: pre-signed URL + extra auth header = invalid)
Azure Blob Storage uses pre-signed URLs. Azure treats any Authorization header alongside a pre-signed URL as an error and returns 401.
Expected behavior
When following a redirect to a different host, bun should drop the Authorization header — consistent with RFC 9110 §15.4 and how curl, wget, and node-fetch behave:
# curl correctly drops auth on cross-host redirect — succeeds:
curl -fsSL \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ghp_YOUR_TOKEN" \
  "https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@myorg/my-package/1.0.0/<hash>" \
  -o package.tgz
Workaround
Manually download tarballs using curl and pre-populate bun's .bun/ cache directory before running bun install, so bun sees the package as already cached and skips the download.
Related

#20219 — distinct issue (auth fails at the initial npm.pkg.github.com request via bunfig.toml); this issue is about the Authorization header being forwarded in the redirect to Azure

t: Windows: re-add the arm64 LTO bun-webkit prebuilt once LLVM's CodeView emitter handles ARM64 register tuples
b:
Follow-up to oven-sh/WebKit#239.
bun-webkit-windows-arm64-lto was dropped from the cross-compile matrix because the LTO codegen of jsc.exe aborts with:
LLVM ERROR: unknown codeview register Q22_Q23_Q24_Q25

LLVM 21's CodeView (Windows debug info) emitter has no register mapping for ARM64 NEON sequential register tuples (the quad-register groups used by ld4/st4), and the more aggressive LTO codegen allocates values into them. The x64 LTO variant builds fine. Dropping /Zi just moves the crash to whoever links the bitcode archives next with debug info enabled, so it isn't a workaround.
Re-add the matrix entry (and the release job's download/rename/upload lines) once an LLVM release maps these registers in llvm/lib/Target/AArch64's CodeView register table. The matrix entry that was removed is preserved as a comment in .github/workflows/build-reusable.yml.

t: Windows: add an ASAN bun-webkit prebuilt (the cross-compile plumbing is already wired)
b:
Follow-up to oven-sh/WebKit#239.
There has never been a Windows ASAN WebKit prebuilt (Linux and macOS both have -asan and -debug-asan variants). The Windows cross-compile Dockerfile already wires everything needed to build one:

ENABLE_SANITIZERS is plumbed through Dockerfile.windows / windows-cross-release.sh / the workflow matrix.
The Windows ASAN/UBSan runtimes (clang_rt.asan_dynamic-x86_64.{dll,lib}, the runtime thunks, clang_rt.ubsan_standalone-x86_64.lib) are mirrored at the compiler-rt-windows-21.1.8 release tag and a -fsanitize=address,undefined /MT cross-link was verified to produce a working PE.
-D_DISABLE_STRING_ANNOTATION -D_DISABLE_VECTOR_ANNOTATION is required because xwin's MSVC splat doesn't include stl_asan.lib (it's a separate VS component) — this loses std::string/std::vector container-overflow annotations but keeps all core ASAN checks.

What's left:

Add a bun-webkit-windows-amd64-asan entry to the windows-cross matrix (ENABLE_SANITIZERS: "address,undefined") plus the release job's download/rename/upload entries. x64 only — LLVM ships no Windows ARM64 ASAN runtime.
The Windows ASAN runtime is a DLL even for /MT builds (the static ASAN runtime was removed in LLVM 17), so a bun Windows ASAN lane would need to ship clang_rt.asan_dynamic-x86_64.dll next to bun.exe.
There is currently no Windows ASAN lane in bun's CI to consume the artifact, so this is gated on wanting one.

t: ld64.lld's LTO pipeline never runs the SLP vectorizer (lld/MachO/LTO.cpp is missing PTO.SLPVectorization)
b:
Follow-up to #31303.
lld/ELF/LTO.cpp::createConfig() sets c.PTO.SLPVectorization = c.OptLevel > 1 (and LoopVectorization). lld/MachO/LTO.cpp never got the equivalent line, so the Mach-O LTO pipeline inherits PipelineTuningOptions()'s default of SLPVectorization = false — at every --lto-O level, including --lto-O3. Loop vectorization defaults on, so most loops are unaffected; only straight-line code that depends on SLP autovectorization regresses.
Verified by extracting the bitcode for printable_mask_latin1 (the Bun.stringWidth ASCII kernel) from libbun_rust.a and replaying it through every pipeline with the same LLVM:



pipeline
SLPVectorizerPass runs?
result




opt -passes='lto<O2>' + llc
yes
28 NEON ops, 75 insns


ld.lld (ELF) --lto-O2
yes
28 NEON ops


ld64.lld default / --lto-O2 / --lto-O3 / -mllvm -vectorize-slp
no
0 vector ops, 131 insns — bit-identical to the shipped LTO binary


ld64.lld --lto-newpm-passes='lto<O3>'
yes
28 NEON ops — but the custom-pipeline path skips the export summary and silently disables whole-program devirtualization, so it's not a usable workaround



This is why Bun.stringWidth's ASCII path is ~2x slower in the LTO macOS builds while everything else got faster.
What to do:

Upstream the one-line fix to lld/MachO/LTO.cpp (mirror the ELF port's PTO.SLPVectorization = ltoo > 1).
Until that ships in a released LLVM, either carry the patch in the lld we link with, or accept the gap — the only code that regresses is scalar code that relies on SLP to become SIMD, and the affected kernels are being rewritten with explicit intrinsics anyway.
Add a workarounds.ts entry keyed on the LLVM version once the upstream fix lands so the tracking self-obsoletes.

t: macOS LTO: the -O2 on the darwin link line is silently dropped — pass --lto-O3/--lto-CGO3 to ld64.lld
b:
Follow-up to #31303.
The darwin cross link passes -O2 on the link line (scripts/build/flags.ts, the "Without -O at link time, clang's driver defaults LTO codegen to -O2" entry). That flag does something on ELF targets — clang's driver forwards it to the linker as -plugin-opt=O2 — but the Darwin driver forwards no opt-level flag to ld64.lld at all (verifiable with clang++ -### …). So the LTO codegen runs at ld64.lld's built-in defaults: --lto-O2 for the IR pipeline and --lto-CGO2 (CodeGenOptLevel::Default) for instruction selection, while the native per-TU build codegens everything at -O3 + CodeGenOptLevel::Aggressive. Concretely that means an inline threshold of 225 instead of 275 and less aggressive isel/scheduling across the whole binary.
What to do:

Replace the ineffective -O2 on the darwin LTO link line with -Wl,--lto-O3 -Wl,--lto-CGO3.
A/B the HTTP plaintext throughput on an M-series Mac before/after. The LTO build is currently ~6% behind the non-LTO build on Bun.serve plaintext under oha (0.5–2.7% under bombardier) with no identified cause — ICF didn't fold any hot symbols and the parser hot loops are SWAR — so the O2-vs-O3 inline threshold and CG opt level are the leading remaining suspects, along with code layout.
This does not fix the Bun.stringWidth regression (that's the SLP vectorizer issue, tracked separately) — the SLP pass is off in ld64.lld's LTO pipeline at every --lto-O level.

t: Bun.Image: add "hash" output mode to placeholder()
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun.Image#placeholder() currently returns a data:image/webp;base64,... URL (~210 bytes). This is fine for a handful of images, but at scale — say, a feed with 50+ images — you're paying ~210 bytes × N in your HTML/JS payload just for blur placeholders.
The ThumbHash format itself is only 5–25 raw bytes (~28–36 base64 chars). For pages with many images it makes more sense to ship the ~800-byte ThumbHash decoder once and store one tiny hash per image.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A placeholder("hash") overload that returns the raw ThumbHash as a Uint8Array:
const img = new Bun.Image(src);
const hash = await img.placeholder("hash"); // Uint8Array, 5–25 bytes
const base64 = Buffer.from(hash).toString("base64"); // ≤36 chars
The hash can then be decoded client-side with evanw/thumbhash (~800 bytes minified).
This would also clarify the existing API — placeholder() / placeholder("dataurl") continues to return a ready-to-use data URL, while placeholder("hash") gives the raw bytes for more advanced use cases.
Type signature
interface Image {
  placeholder(as?: "dataurl"): Promise<string>;  // data:image/webp;base64,...
  placeholder(as: "hash"): Promise<Uint8Array>;  // raw ThumbHash bytes
}
What alternatives have you considered?

Computing the ThumbHash outside of Bun (e.g. pure-JS) — but this means decoding the full image in JS just to re-encode to a hash, which defeats the point of Bun.Image.
Storing the data URL — works, but is ~8× larger than the hash per image.

Real-world vitest → bun test migration: gaps that force per-file process isolation
b:
Context
I migrated a large production test suite — 316 files / 2756 tests (Next.js + Prisma + React Testing Library) — from Vitest to bun test. It now runs fully green under Bun (incl. 1.4.0-canary.1, the Rust build), but only via a custom compatibility shim + a per-file parallel runner. Sharing the gaps that stop this from being a clean, fast migration, since each one is individually small but together they block both correctness and the speed win.
The headline blocker: mock.module is not scoped per test file
mock.module() mutates a process-global registry that is never reset between test files, so running multiple files in one bun test process leaks mocks across files. This forces every file into its own process to stay correct — which throws away Bun's single-process speed advantage (native single-process is ~3–4× faster than per-file in my measurements, but leaks make it unusable).
Minimal repro (still fails on 1.4.0-canary.1):
// dep.ts
export const a = "REAL_A"
export const b = "REAL_B"

// a.test.ts
import { mock, it, expect } from "bun:test"
mock.module("./dep", () => ({ a: "MOCK_A" })) // partial mock, drops `b`
import { a } from "./dep"
it("A sees mock", () => { expect(a).toBe("MOCK_A") })

// b.test.ts
import { it, expect } from "bun:test"
import { a, b } from "./dep" // never mocked here
it("B sees real", () => { expect(a).toBe("REAL_A"); expect(b).toBe("REAL_B") })

bun test b.test.ts → passes
bun test a.test.ts b.test.ts → b.test.ts fails — a's partial mock leaks in (and the dropped b export breaks the static import binding)

This appears to contradict #12823 ("Bun mocks to be scoped to test file", closed COMPLETED). Related: #7823 (mock.restore doesn't undo mock.module), #30242 (in-place namespace mutation).
Full gap list (what a vitest suite needs)

Per-file mock isolation, or a documented way to reset the module-mock registry between files (vi.resetModules equivalent). This single feature unlocks both correctness and single-process speed. ← most important
mock.module factory must be synchronous — an async factory that awaits a dynamic import() deadlocks the loader. vitest allows async factories.
No importActual that bypasses the active mock — needed for the extremely common vi.mock(x, () => ({ ...actual, override })) pattern. Workaround: require(Bun.resolveSync(x) + "?actual").
spyOn does not propagate through ESM named imports / re-export barrels — so the isolatable alternative to mock.module is unreliable for real module graphs (related

SIGSEGV in pas_local_allocator_refill_with_known_config on Windows — JSC bmalloc corruption during DFG JIT compilation
b:
Environment

Bun: 1.3.14 (standalone executable, embedded in Claude Code)
OS: Windows 11 (x86_64), 32 GB RAM
CPU: Intel i9-13980HX (SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2)

Crash Report
https://bun.report/1.3.14/e_1521eeddmgggkE+hogC27i42Cqvj22Cwmh22C8vi/oDo7p/oDm0j4iD0r+tnD20zjnDg/+45C+wgu3Cg5r72Cgk03zCy/ygsCmuox3DCYKERNEL32.DLLu10LCSntdll.dll4nhBA2AwB
Symptoms
Non-deterministic SIGSEGV during long-running CLI sessions. Process RSS ~0.5 GB at crash time, machine had plenty of free memory. Happens roughly every few hours of active use. The crash is always at a near-null address (observed 0x18, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF in previous occurrences).
Decoded Backtrace
The crash originates in JSC's DFG JIT compilation, triggered from a JIT worker thread, not from bad user JS code:
ThreadPool → JITWorklistThread::work
  → JITPlan::compileInThread
    → DFG::Plan::compileInThreadImpl
      → ObjectAllocationSinkingPhase::run → performSinking
        → OSRAvailabilityAnalysisPhase::run
          → AvailabilityMap::pruneByLiveness → filterByLiveness
            → Operands<Availability> construction (Vector allocation)
              → FastMalloc → bmalloc_allocate_casual
                → pas_try_allocate_intrinsic → pas_local_allocator_try_allocate
                  → pas_local_allocator_refill_with_known_config:469
                    → SIGSEGV at 0x00000018

Analysis

The DFG JIT compiler was running the Object Allocation Sinking optimization phase
The OSR Availability Analysis phase needed to allocate a Vector<Availability> to track variable liveness
This allocation went through bmalloc → libpas → the thread-local allocator
When pas_local_allocator_refill_with_known_config tried to traverse the free list to refill the local allocator, it dereferenced 0x00000018 — a near-null pointer suggesting corrupted free list state
The corruption likely happened earlier (on another thread or during a prior allocation), and this JIT allocation was just the unlucky consumer

This crash appears identical in nature to #20606 (same PAS allocator corruption on Windows). It is also related to the broader class of JSC-on-Windows stability issues seen in #25798, #14332, #18871.
Key Point
This is not a bug in the JS code running on Bun. The corruption is in JSC's C++ memory allocator state. The JIT worker thread is the victim, not the cause.

b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14 (stable) and 1.4.0-canary (upgraded via bun upgrade --canary)
What platform is your computer?
macOS 15.5 (Darwin 24.6.0) arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install Bun 1.3.14 on macOS arm64 via curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
Run: bun -e "import { Database } from 'bun:sqlite'; console.log(new Database(':memory:').query('SELECT sqlite_version()').get());"
Observe output: 3.43.2
Upgrade to canary: bun upgrade --canary
Run the same command again
Observe output: still 3.43.2

What is the expected behavior?
According to the Bun v1.3.14 blog post:
▎ "Bun's built-in SQLite has been updated from 3.51.2 to 3.53.0."
Expected sqlite_version() to return 3.53.0.
What do you see instead?
{
"sqlite_version()": "3.43.2"
}
This is a full 10 minor versions behind the claimed version.
Additional context
This is not just a cosmetic version mismatch. SQLite 3.43.2 contains a critical FTS5 bug where any UPDATE or DELETE on an FTS5 virtual table causes SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB (errno 267) with the message "database
disk image is malformed". We reproduced this with a minimal script:
import { Database } from 'bun:sqlite';
const db = new Database(':memory:');
db.run('CREATE TABLE docs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, content TEXT)');
db.run(INSERT INTO docs (title, content) VALUES ('a', 'b'));
db.run('CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE docs_fts USING fts5(title, content, content='docs', content_rowid='id')');
db.run('UPDATE docs SET content = ? WHERE id = ?', ['c', 1]);
// Throws: database disk image is malformed, errno: 267
Because of this bug, we were forced to downgrade our application from FTS5 to FTS4 standalone, losing the storage efficiency of FTS5 external content mode.
This appears to be a recurring issue on macOS — a previous report (#24957) documented the same discrepancy where macOS builds shipped SQLite 3.37.0 while the release notes claimed 3.51.0.

t: Bun.openInEditor can install spawnSync signal forwarding from editor helper thread
b:
Summary
Bun.openInEditor() starts a detached helper thread to wait for the editor process. That helper currently calls sync::spawn(), and on POSIX sync::spawn() unconditionally installs the process-wide spawnSync signal-forwarding handlers.
That signal-forwarding path uses process-global state (Bun__currentSyncPID, Bun__pendingSignalToSend, and previous_actions[NSIG]) and is intended for foreground sync spawns such as bun run / bunx. For openInEditor(), the caller's JS program keeps running while the helper waits in the background, so replacing process signal handlers can interfere with signals intended for the main Bun process.
Why this matters
If user code has a JS signal handler such as process.on("SIGUSR2", ...), an editor helper spawned by Bun.openInEditor() can temporarily install the sync-spawn forwarding handler over it. During that window, the signal can be forwarded to the editor child instead of being delivered to the Bun process.
Expected behavior
Bun.openInEditor() should not install foreground spawnSync signal forwarding from its detached editor helper thread.
Proposed fix
Add a Unix forward_signals option to sync spawn options, defaulting to true, and set it to false for the openInEditor() helper spawn. Normal foreground sync spawn behavior remains unchanged.

What version of Bun is running?
1.4.0-canary.1 -- revision b3d086e26f3a6fc39733316d7af7b1d661fe81c6 (oven/bun:canary).
Every stable release tested is unaffected: 1.3.5, 1.3.13, 1.3.14, latest.

Also reproduced cleanly in the official oven/bun:canary Docker image, so it is not
environment-specific.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
const a = 1779314400000; // a millisecond timestamp
const b = 1779400800000; // a different timestamp, one day later

console.log(a === b); // false -- these are two distinct numbers

const m = new Map();
m.set(a, "A");
m.set(b, "B");

console.log(m.size);   // 1   ← expected 2
console.log(m.get(a)); // "B" ← expected "A"
console.log(m.get(b)); // "B"

console.log(new Set([a, b]).size); // 1 ← expected 2
Map and Set treat every integer-valued number key with magnitude ≥ 2³¹ as the
same key. It is not just a hash-bucket collision -- the keys compare equal, so
membership is wrong too:
const m = new Map([[2 ** 40, "only-key"]]);
console.log(m.has(2 ** 41)); // true ← expected false (never inserted)
What is the expected behavior?
m.size === 2, m.get(a) === "A", new Set([a, b]).size === 2,
m.has(<never-inserted-key>) === false -- i.e. distinct numbers are distinct keys.
This is what Node.js, every browser, and every stable Bun release do.
What do you see instead?
The second set() overwrites the first. get() / has() on any large-integer key
resolve to the most-recently-inserted large-integer entry. All large-integer keys
behave as a single equivalence class.

non-integer doubles (e.g. 2³² + 0.5)

plain object property keys

t: Event loop permanently dies when Go CGo .so + WASM coexist on Linux (SIGPWR storm)
Missing signal in WritableStreamDefaultController (breaks libraries)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Linux 7.0.0-15-generic x86_64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Per WHATWG Streams §4.5.2, a WritableStreamDefaultController exposes a readonly signal attribute — the AbortSignal that fires when the writer or stream is aborted, so the sink can react before/while its own abort() callback runs. Bun's implementation returns undefined for it.
Minimal repro:
const ws = new WritableStream({
  start(controller) {
    console.log('signal:', typeof controller.signal, controller.signal instanceof AbortSignal);
  },
  write() {}
});
ws.getWriter().write('x');
Run with bun ./repro.js.
What is the expected behavior?
Per spec, controller.signal is an AbortSignal. Both Node.js and Deno conform:
$ node ./repro.js
signal: object true

$ deno run ./repro.js
signal: object true

What do you see instead?
$ bun ./repro.js
signal: undefined false

Downstream impact: any library that uses the sink-side controller.signal to coordinate abort handling crashes on Bun. We hit it in stream-chain v4 (src/asWebStream.js:229):
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'controller.signal.addEventListener')
    at start (.../stream-chain/src/asWebStream.js:229:20)
    at WritableStream (unknown)

The library uses controller.signal.addEventListener('abort', …) inside the sink's start(controller) to wake a write() that's blocked on per-item backpressure — without it, an aborted writer would deadlock on Bun. Workaround on the consumer side is a feature-probe and skip, but the fix wants to be in Bun.
Additional information

Spec reference: WHATWG Streams §4.5.2 — WritableStreamDefaultController.signal. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WritableStreamDefaultController/signal
Same probe against ReadableStreamDefaultController and TransformStreamDefaultController also returns undefined for .signal on Bun — those are not required by the spec (no signal attribute defined on either), so this report is narrowly about the Writable case.
Bun docs (https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/streams and https://bun.com/reference/node/stream/web/WritableStream) don't mention this gap — the omission appears unintentional.
Possibly related but a different surface: #26392 — Unable to abort pipes with an AbortSignal (that one is about pipeTo({signal}); this one is about the sink-side controller.signal exposed inside new WritableStream({start(c){…}})).

What version of Bun is running?

What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.6.0 x86_64 (macOS on Intel)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
import fs from "node:fs";
const s = await fs.promises.statfs("/");
console.log(s);
What is the expected behavior?
Same values as Node.js on the same machine:
{
  type: 26,
  bsize: 4096,
  blocks: 488475719,
  bfree: 473415905,
  bavail: 473415905,
  files: 4292221443,
  ffree: 4291794580
}
What do you see instead?
{
  type: 0,
  bsize: 0,                 // should be 4096
  blocks: 4096,             // should be 488475719  (this is bsize value)
  bfree: 1048576,           // should be 473415905
  bavail: 488475719,        // should be 473415905  (this is blocks value)
  files: 473415902,
  ffree: 473415902
}
The fields look shifted by one slot, suggesting the struct layout used to decode the macOS statfs64 syscall is misaligned on darwin-x64. With bsize=0, any consumer that computes blocks * bsize reports zero available space.

darwin-arm64 is unaffected — same Bun version on M-series Macs returns the correct values.
Both darwin-x64-modern and darwin-x64 baseline compile targets reproduce.
Confirmed against Node.js on the same volume — Node returns the expected values, so this is Bun-specific, not a kernel quirk.
Downstream impact: hit in Unity Hub CLI — every disk-space pre-check on Intel Macs failed with "not enough space" because the underlying statfs.bsize was 0. Workaround in place via a df -Pk fallback until this is fixed.

t: Bun.Glob.scan throws ENOENT on directories that exist when walking a Docker Desktop VirtioFS bind-mount (macOS)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
macOS 14.x (Apple Silicon, arm64) host running Docker Desktop with the default VirtioFS file-sharing implementation. Stack runs in oven/bun:1.3.13 (linux/arm64) under Docker Desktop's Linux VM.
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Check out any multi-package Bun workspace monorepo onto a macOS host.
Bring up a container that bind-mounts the repo at /app:
services:
  bun:
    image: oven/bun:1.3.13
    working_dir: /app
    volumes:
      - .:/app
    command: ['bun', 'run', 'scan.ts']

Inside the repo write scan.ts:
const glob = new Bun.Glob('**/*.ts')
for await (const f of glob.scan({ cwd: '/app/packages/ui/src', absolute: true })) {
  console.log(f)
}

docker compose run --rm bun.

The scan crashes intermittently with:
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/app/packages/ui/src/contexts'
    path: "/app/packages/ui/src/contexts",
 syscall: "open",
   errno: -2,
    code: "ENOENT"

docker compose run --rm bun ls -la /app/packages/ui/src/contexts from the same container confirms the directory exists and contains files. Bun.Glob enumerated contexts itself one syscall earlier — it's failing on the recursive open.
Repro rate ≈ 60–80% on cold container start. Switching Docker Desktop → Settings → General → file sharing to gRPC FUSE drops the rate to 0% on the same repo.
What is the expected behavior?
Bun.Glob.scan returns the matching files without throwing on directories that exist.
What do you see instead?
ENOENT thrown from inside Bun.Glob's recursive walk for a directory that exists and was discovered by the same walk one step earlier.
Additional information

VirtioFS-only. gRPC FUSE works. osxfs (legacy) untested.
Smells like a stale-inode-cache issue between Bun's directory fd cache (resolver/dir-info cache) and what virtiofs returns. Adjacent reports: #25730 (now closed, "directory mismatch for directory … fd 3") and #5841 (--hot/--watch flakiness in certain network filesystems).
Workaround for downstream users: switch Docker Desktop to gRPC FUSE, or replace Bun.Glob calls with node:fs/promises readdir({ recursive: true }) / fast-glob, both of which walk via readdir syscalls and do not hit this.
Also reproducible by replacing the generator with bun --hot --watch against the same bind-mount — the same ENOENT storm appears during initial module-graph build (this is the underlying reason the project wraps its server with a Bun.build-bundled dev driver instead).

t: soundness: AtomicCell<T> unsafe impl Send/Sync missing T: Send bound
soundness: StoreSlice<T> Copy + slice_mut aliasing allows &mut [T] aliasing
b:
Summary
StoreSlice<T> in src/ast/nodes.rs has a soundness hole: because StoreSlice<T> is Copy and slice_mut takes self by value, two copies of the same handle can independently call slice_mut and each receive a &mut [T] over the same backing allocation. This produces aliased mutable references, which is immediate undefined behaviour.
The unsafe impl Send/Sync bound-narrowing landed in #30924 (EXP-019) does not close this hole.
Reproduction sketch
let a: StoreSlice<Foo> = …;
let b = a;                    // Copy — both name the same slice
let r1 = a.slice_mut(store);  // &mut [Foo]
let r2 = b.slice_mut(store);  // &mut [Foo] — same memory → UB
Proposed fix
Either:

Remove the Copy impl on StoreSlice<T>, or
Change slice_mut to take &mut self instead of self.

Both options require updating every StoreSlice consumer, so this warrants a dedicated PR.
References

Identified during UB audit — see #30903
Partial mitigation (Send/Sync bounds) landed in #30924 (EXP-019)
Raised by @coderabbitai code review on #30924
Requested by @Dicklesworthstone

t: MySQL options documentation incorrect for SSL settings
Expose `sqlite3_interrupt()` on `bun:sqlite` Database/Statement
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
bun:sqlite's API is intentionally synchronous and high-performance — that's a feature, not a bug. But synchronous execution combined with no way to cancel a running query means long-running or runaway queries are unkillable from JavaScript. The only mechanism today is to spawn the query into a subprocess and SIGKILL it on timeout, which:

Forces every "this query might take too long" code path into a subprocess + IPC architecture (heavy)
Loses transaction-rollback grace — SIGKILL leaves the engine in WAL recovery state on next open
Forces a full backup-restore cycle on every timeout (expensive, brittle, requires a backup-before-migrate step)
Cannot interrupt a query whose results we have partially consumed in-process — the only escape is process death

SQLite's C API has supported sqlite3_interrupt() for over twenty years. It is explicitly designed to be called from a different thread to abort a running query — the flag is checked in the sqlite3_step() VDBE loop, and the in-flight statement returns SQLITE_INTERRUPT so the JS side can observe and respond. better-sqlite3, node-sqlite3, GRDB, and most mature SQLite wrappers expose it. bun:sqlite does not.
Real-world use case
We run a self-hosted platform OS where the migration runner spawns each migration into a Bun subprocess specifically so we can SIGKILL it if it wedges. We hit this recently — a WITH RECURSIVE CTE was outrunning its 800ms budget, and our hand-rolled SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL ladder had a structural bug that left subprocesses hung when SIGTERM was eaten by the in-flight sqlite3_step(). We fixed the ladder (the SIGKILL path is now unconditional), but the underlying need for a subprocess at all stems from not having interrupt() in-process. If interrupt() were available, we could run migrations in-process with a watchdog timer — significantly simpler architecture, no backup-restore dance on every timeout, graceful ROLLBACK semantics.
This is not unique to migrations. Any platform that exposes user-driven queries (search, reports, analytics, permission BFS) needs the ability to cancel a query whose user navigated away, whose request timed out, or whose payload turned out to be a runaway. The current bun:sqlite story is "spawn a subprocess and kill it" — which is fine for one batch job but not viable for an interactive query path.

t: feat: expose raw JavaScriptCore (JSC) code coverage data
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun has built-in code coverage support via bun test --coverage. However, the output is limited to predefined formats like Text, Lcov.
In Node.js, developers can leverage the raw, low-overhead code coverage native to the V8 engine via process.env.NODE_V8_COVERAGE or the v8.takeCoverage() API. This raw data is crucial for monorepos, specialized enterprise toolchains, and building custom coverage reporters without relying on heavy source-instrumentation tools like c8, monocart-coverage-reports. Since Bun is powered by JavaScriptCore (JSC), we currently lack a similar way to extract the raw bytecode-level execution data that JSC natively tracks internally.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
We would like Bun to provide parity with Node.js's V8 coverage capabilities by exposing JSC's native coverage data, either programmatically or via environment variables.
1, Programmatic API (Mirroring Node's v8 module)
// Proposed API in Bun (equivalent to Node's v8.takeCoverage())
import { jsc } from "bun"; // or via a new/existing internal module

jsc.startCoverage();
// ... execute code / tests ...
const rawJscData = jsc.takeCoverage(); // Returns raw JSC bytecode/block execution map
jsc.stopCoverage();
2, Environment Variable
An env var like BUN_JSC_COVERAGE=./dir, mirroring Node's NODE_V8_COVERAGE, which dumps raw JSC coverage JSON profiles to a specified directory upon process exit.
Additional context
Just as Node.js exports raw coverage data in the native V8 coverage format, Bun should ideally export data in the native JSC coverage format.
JavaScriptCore already features a highly optimized internal tracking system via its Type Profiler and Code Coverage Profiler at the LLInt and Baseline JIT layers. Bun does not need to convert this to standard V8 or Lcov formats internally for this API; simply dumping JSC's native raw JSON/structural execution maps directly to the user would be enough. The community and custom tooling builders can then handle the parsing or conversion to third-party formats. This ensures maximum execution performance while granting full flexibility for advanced test engineering workflows.
What alternatives have you considered?
No response

t: ReadableStream with type:"direct" throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE in node-compat path (breaks React 19 react-dom/server.edge.js)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
v1.3.13 (also reproduced on later versions)
What platform is your computer?
Linux
What steps can reproduce the bug?
// repro.ts
const stream = new ReadableStream({
  type: "direct",
  pull(controller) {
    controller.close();
  },
});
Run with bun run repro.ts
What is the expected behavior?
type: "direct" is Bun's own extension to ReadableStream (also used by Cloudflare Workers). Bun's native ReadableStream supports it. The node-compat path (node:internal/webstreams/readablestream) should either support it too, or silently ignore the unknown type and delegate — not throw.
What do you see instead?
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]: The property 'source.type' is invalid. Received 'direct'
    at new ReadableStream (node:internal/webstreams/readablestream:278:15)

The error originates from Bun's Node.js-compat ReadableStream implementation, not the native Bun one. This means the native and node-compat paths disagree on whether type: "direct" is valid.
Real-world impact
React 19's react-dom/server.edge.js calls new ReadableStream({ type: "direct", ... }) for prerendering. When Nitro bundles a project for the bun preset, it resolves server.edge.js (the CF Workers / edge build), and the bundled output crashes with the above error during prerendering.
Tracked upstream in nitrojs/nitro: nitrojs/nitro#4259
Nitro has worked around this with a polyfill (nitrojs/nitro#4265), but the correct fix is for Bun's node-compat ReadableStream to accept type: "direct" consistently with the native implementation.
Additional information

Bun native ReadableStream supports type: "direct" ✅
Bun node-compat ReadableStream (node:internal/webstreams/readablestream) rejects it ❌
This inconsistency is the root cause.

What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon). Also reproduced on Linux arm64 (oven/bun:1-debian container).
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Cyclic ESM where a subclass module does class X extends Base and Base comes from a package barrel that is part of the same strongly-connected import component. On 1.3.14 the extends clause is evaluated before the imported binding is initialized; on 1.3.13 (and Node) it is not.

loaded OK

What do you see instead?
On Bun 1.3.14:
19 | class DecoratorBlockNode extends DecoratorNode {
                                      ^

      at node_modules/@lexical/react/LexicalDecoratorBlockNode.dev.mjs:19:34
