t: Add `--implementation-language` flag now that RIIR is solved — let users pick the next rewrite
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
First of all: congratulations on the Rust rewrite. Truly historic. 1.3.14 was a tearful goodbye and I poured one out for Zig on the night of the merge.
However, this raises a much more serious problem.
For the past four years, the entire JavaScript community has been organized around a single shared activity: demanding that Bun be rewritten in Rust. It was our common language. It was the thing we did. Hacker News threads, Reddit posts, Twitter quote-tweets — all of it scaffolded on the unshakable foundation of "but why isn't it in Rust?"
Now that's gone. Merged. Done. One million lines, shipped over a weekend by Claude. What are we supposed to talk about now? TypeScript decorators? Be serious.
The community is in mourning. We have no purpose. I opened Hacker News this morning and the top comment was agreeing with the article. The vibes are off.
Also, secondary concern: now that we've established that an AI agent can port the entire Bun codebase from Zig to Rust in approximately one (1) Jarred Sumner weekend, the marginal cost of a full-language rewrite has effectively dropped to zero. It would be irresponsible not to make this a runtime flag.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add a --implementation-language flag (alias: --impl-lang) that triggers an on-the-fly rewrite of the entire Bun codebase into the user's language of choice before executing their script.
bun run index.ts --impl-lang=go
bun install --impl-lang=c++ --edition=23
bunx create-vite --impl-lang=zig  # for the nostalgic
How it works

User invokes bun run with --impl-lang=<target>.
Bun spawns a Claude Code subprocess.
Claude reads the current Rust codebase, the existing PORTING.md, and writes a new PORTING.md for the target language (~300 rules, as is tradition).
Phase A: faithful logic capture, doesn't need to compile.
Phase B: crate-by-crate (or equivalent) build until 99.8% of the test suite passes on Linux x64 glibc.
The user's console.log("hi") is then executed.
Total time: 47 minutes to 3 days, depending on target language and how distracted Claude gets.

Supported targets

rust — current default. No-op. Returns immediately. Prints "based" to stderr.
zig — reverses the May 2026 merge. For users experiencing rewrite-grief. Comes with a complimentary RIIZ.md rules file.
go — adds a GC and three goroutines that do nothing but make the binary feel more "cloud native"
c++ — Sumner has expressed openness. Template metaprog

t: Feature Request: `bun test` --exclude / --include for file paths (use case: gating live network canary tests)
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
In a monorepo with mixed test types (unit, integration, and live network canary tests against real upstream APIs), we need to run different subsets in different contexts:

bun test in CI → fast, hermetic, no network — unit + integration only
bun test:live on demand or in a scheduled lane → only the live network canaries

Bun's test runner has no path-level include/exclude flag. Two prior issues flag this gap:

#21395 — closed in March 2026 without explanation despite multiple "still needed" comments
#29477 — open, but scoped to skipping single tests by name, not files

Opening a fresh issue with a concrete use case + the workaround we discovered, in case the prior reports were closed for lack of grounding.
Current workaround (works today, but ugly)
Bun's default test matcher requires .{test,spec,_test,_spec}. in the filename. Naming live test files *.livetest.ts (no .test. substring) makes them naturally invisible to bun test. A separate script picks them up by explicit positional path:
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "bun test",
    "test:live": "bun test ./src/providers/**/*.livetest.ts"
  }
}
The leading ./ is required — otherwise bun's matcher rejects unrecognised filenames as test-name filters with note: To treat the "..." filter as a path, run "bun test ./...".
This works (verified across 8 live canary tests in ~2.6s wall-clock), but it's a special-filename hack. Costs:

Live tests can't use the conventional *.test.ts suffix.
Editor / IDE test-file detection misses them.
Anyone reading the script has to know about bun's matcher rules.
Doesn't help projects that already have hundreds of *.test.ts files and want to skip a subset (e.g. e2e.test.ts everywhere).

What is the feature you are proposing?
Either, ideally both:
CLI flag (Jest / Vitest parity — Vitest uses --include / --exclude)
bun test --exclude='**/*.live.test.ts'
bun test --include='**/*.unit.test.ts'
bunfig.toml (cleaner for the common project-wide case)
[test]
exclude = [\"**/*.live.test.ts\", \"**/__fixtures__/**\"]
include = [\"src/**\", \"tests/**\"]
Why a fresh issue instead of bumping #21395?
#21395 was closed in March 2026 with no closing comment and no reason given, despite several follow-up comments asking for it. Reopening it from outside the team is unclear. This issue contributes:

A concrete real-world use case (live network canaries in a Bun monorepo)
The filename-gate workaround so other users hitting this can ship today
A scope dis

b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Bun documents two global config paths: $HOME/.bunfig.toml and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml. The XDG path implementation breaks convention in three ways:

It's a hidden file. The leading dot makes $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml a hidden file. The XDG Base Directory Specification designates $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config) as the canonical location for user config precisely to avoid dotfile clutter in $HOME - files inside it should not be hidden.
It lacks an app subdirectory. The conventional XDG path for an application named bun is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bun/bunfig.toml. Placing the file directly in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME rather than a bun/ subdirectory conflicts with how every other XDG-compliant tool organises its config.
It doesn't apply the spec default. The spec states that if $XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset, it defaults to ~/.config. Bun does not honour this: ~/.config/.bunfig.toml is only read when $XDG_CONFIG_HOME is explicitly set to ~/.config; leaving it unset causes bun to skip ~/.config entirely.

The following script tests each candidate path by writing a config that points registry at an unreachable sentinel URL. If the config is read, bun add fails with FailedToOpenSocket. If the config is silently ignored, bun add succeeds.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Requires: bun 1.3.14, network access.

SENTINEL_REGISTRY="https://sentinel-test-registry.invalid"
PKG="is-odd"

cleanup() {
  rm -rf /tmp/bun-xdg-test
  rm -f ~/.bunfig.toml
  rm -f ~/.config/.bunfig.toml
  rm -f ~/.config/bunfig.toml
  rm -f ~/.config/bun/bunfig.toml
  rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache/is-odd* ~/.bun/install/cache/is-number* 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT
cleanup

BUNFIG_CONTENT="[install]
registry = \"$SENTINEL_REGISTRY\""

run_test() {
  local label="$1"
  local config_path="$2"
  shift 2
  local env_prefix=("$@")

  rm -rf /tmp/bun-xdg-test && mkdir -p /tmp/bun-xdg-test
  rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache/is-odd* ~/.bun/install/cache/is-number* 2>/dev/null || true

  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config_path")"
  echo "$BUNFIG_CONTENT" > "$config_path"

  local output
  output=$(cd /tmp/bun-xdg-test && "${env_prefix[@]}" bun add "$PKG" 2>&1) || true

  if echo "$output" | grep -q "FailedToOpenSocket"; then
    echo "PASS  $label"
  else
    echo "FAIL  $label"
  fi

  rm -f "$config_path"
}

echo "bun $(bun --version)"
echo ""

run_test '~/.bunfig.toml, XDG_CONFIG_HOM

css/rules/mod.rs: arena_static() lifetime erasure workaround — needs CssRule<'bump> migration
b:
Summary
src/css/rules/mod.rs has 6 unsafe call sites sharing one root cause: arena_static(bump: &Arena) -> &'static Arena erases the arena lifetime via raw pointer cast. This is an acknowledged workaround (see PORT NOTE at line 223-228).
Pattern
unsafe fn arena_static(bump: &Arena) -> &'static Arena {
    unsafe { &*core::ptr::from_ref(bump) }
}
Used from:

decl_block_static() — line 271
decl_block_empty_static() — line 283
decl_handler_static() — line 301
page.rs:215 — same pattern

Root cause
CssRule, DeclarationBlock, and related types use 'static as a placeholder instead of a real 'bump lifetime parameter. The arena DOES outlive all rules (it owns their memory), so the lifetime extension is semantically correct — but the types don't reflect this.
Fix
Migrate CssRule\<'bump, R\> and downstream types from 'static to 'bump. This collapses all 6 arena_static call sites to plain decl_block/new_in — no unsafe needed.
The code itself documents this in its PORT NOTE (line 223):

"Callers whose storage is still pinned to DeclarationBlock<'static> must fix that storage type — the lie belongs there, not here, and collapses when CssRule<'bump, R> re-threads the arena lifetime."

Found by
Unsafe audit — triage phase.

Android aarch64 binary killed by SIGSYS (seccomp) on close_range syscall
b:
What version of Bun is running?
Latest Rust-based Android aarch64 prebuilt (bun-linux-aarch64-android, NDK r27c, BuildID eabccd1c3534a456345e6a567cc562fd893371d7, target API 28).
What platform is your computer?
Linux localhost 4.19.132 aarch64 Android — Android 12 (SDK 31), Termux on a real device. Reproduces on every stock Android device because the cause is the zygote's seccomp-bpf filter, not the device.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
chmod +x bun-linux-aarch64-android
./bun-linux-aarch64-android --version
Output:
Bad system call

Exit status 159 (= 128 + 31 = killed by SIGSYS).
What is the expected behavior?
Bun should print its version (or at least not be killed before reaching main logic).
Root cause
The binary is killed by SIGSYS from seccomp when it invokes the close_range(2) syscall.
strace confirms it:
rt_sigaction(SIGSYS, {sa_handler=0x74bfeb0d2c, ...}, NULL, 8) = 0
--- SIGSYS {si_signo=SIGSYS, si_code=SYS_SECCOMP,
            si_call_addr=0x74bd4a8ca0,
            si_syscall=__NR_close_range,
            si_arch=AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64} ---
+++ killed by SIGSYS +++

Why this happens on Android specifically:

Every process on Android inherits a seccomp-bpf allowlist installed by the zygote before execve. That allowlist was frozen years ago and does not include __NR_close_range (syscall 436, added in Linux 5.9).
The filter is configured with SECCOMP_RET_TRAP, so unknown syscalls don't return ENOSYS — they raise SIGSYS and the process dies. Bionic prints Fatal signal 31 (SIGSYS), code 1 (SYS_SECCOMP) to logcat.
The seccomp filter cannot be removed from userspace, even with root, so this affects 100% of Android users running the prebuilt.

This is a regression vs. the old Zig-based bun, which did not call close_range.
Where it's called from in the binary
close_range is not in bun's dynamic symbol table — it's emitted as a direct svc #0 via libc::syscall / inline asm (likely from Rust std's Command fd-cleanup path or from bun's own pre-exec cleanup). objdump shows two call sites that load the syscall number 436 (0x1b4) into w4 and call a generic syscall wrapper:
1f2b418: mov w3, #0x241          // = 577 (CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC flag)
1f2b41c: mov w4, #0x1b4          // = 436 = __NR_close_range
1f2b420: bl  0x21a2250           // syscall wrapper -> svc #0

1f2b5e0: mov w3, #0x241
1f2b5e4: mov w4, #0x1b4
1f2b5e8: bl  0x21a2250

Because it's a raw syscall (not a libc symbol), LD_PRELOAD shims cannot intercept it — the only userspace fixes are a binary patch

t: bunx silently accepts --minimum-release-age flag but does not enforce it (no-op)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14 (also reproduced on 1.3.10 and 1.3.11)
What platform is your computer?
Linux ubuntu-latest x86_64 (GitHub Actions runner); also reproduced on macOS 14 arm64.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
bunx accepts --minimum-release-age=<N> without error but does not enforce it. The same flag passed to bun add works correctly. This asymmetry makes bunx unsuitable for the supply-chain defense use case the flag was designed for.
Pick any package with a version published within the last 7 days (e.g. tsx typically has multiple recent releases).
PKG=tsx

# Clean cache to force a fresh fetch
rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache ~/.bun/install/global

# ─── Control: `bun add` enforces the flag ───
mkdir -p /tmp/bun-add && cd /tmp/bun-add
echo '{"name":"x","version":"1.0.0"}' > package.json
bun add --minimum-release-age=3155760000 "$PKG"   # 100 years
# → errors: "error: All versions of <pkg> blocked by minimum-release-age"
# Confirms the flag is wired up correctly for `bun add`.

# ─── Bug: `bunx` with SAME flag is a silent no-op ───
rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache ~/.bun/install/global
mkdir -p /tmp/bunx && cd /tmp/bunx
bunx --minimum-release-age=3155760000 "$PKG" --version
# → no error, installs latest version, runs it, prints today's release version
The 100-year value eliminates ambiguity: any successful install proves the flag has zero effect on bunx. The bug is not a config-loading edge case or cache hit — bunx accepts the flag, then ignores it entirely.
A full empirical matrix testing this and adjacent age-gate channels (global bunfig, project bunfig, bun add flag, pnpm add flag, pnpm dlx flag) is in this workflow run for reference: https://github.com/AtipicalLabs/dotfiles/actions/runs/25887869917
What is the expected behavior?
One of:

bunx --minimum-release-age=N enforces the gate the same way bun add does — either fails when no version satisfies the constraint, or resolves to the most-recent satisfying version.
bunx rejects the unknown flag with error: unknown flag --minimum-release-age.

The current silent no-op is the worst of both: users reasonably believe their supply-chain age gate applies to bunx (since it shares bun install plumbing) and get no protection.
What do you see instead?
bunx --minimum-release-age=3155760000 <pkg> accepts the flag without error and installs the latest version regardless of age. Verified by:

Setting the value to 100 years (3155760000 seconds) and watching bunx install a package version published the same

error: "bun" exited with code 126

claude investigation, i don't know rust so i won't submit a PR for this:
Reproduction
Confirmed the bug exactly as described: bun run --bun bun run --bun vite --version produced ELOOP — Too many levels of symbolic links and exit 126, with /tmp/bun-node-/{node,bun} pointing at /tmp/bun-node-/bun (self-loop).
Root cause
In src/install/lib.rs:603-629 (create_fake_temporary_node_executable), the code preferred argv[0] whenever absolute. But the bun internal shell (src/runtime/shell/states/Cmd.rs:508-535) explicitly replaces argv[0] with the PATH-resolved absolute path before exec'ing — and bun's run_binary_without_bunx_path (src/runtime/cli/run_command.rs:2130) also passes the resolved path as argv0. After the outer --bun prepended BUN_NODE_DIR to $PATH, the inner bun's argv[0] was exactly <BUN_NODE_DIR>/bun — the symlink the inner call was about to rewrite. It wrote that path back as the symlink target, creating node -> bun -> bun -> ....
Fix
src/install/lib.rs: switched the symlink target to bun_core::self_exe_path() (Linux: /proc/self/exe readlink; macOS/Windows: canonicalized exe path). It's memoized via Once, so the cost is paid once per process. argv[0] survives only as a last-resort fallback if self_exe_path() fails.

bun update -i (Rust port) renders trailing r on short package names due to OSC 8 / pretty tag escape conflict
b:
What version of Bun is running?
Broken: bun update --interactive v1.3.14-canary.1 (19d8ade2c)
(Last known good: bun update --interactive v1.3.14 (0d9b296a))
What platform is your computer?
macOS (reproduced on both VS Code Terminal and Ghostty)
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Have a project that depends on package ai (the Vercel AI SDK)
Run bun update -i
The package name ai is rendered as air in the interactive list

In VS Code Terminal, the ai portion renders with a hyperlink underline but the trailing r does not, suggesting the hyperlink covers ai correctly but r is leaked as plain text.
What is the expected behavior?
The package name displays as ai.
What do you see instead?
The package name displays as air.
Additional information
Root cause: A collision between pretty_fmt_runtime's tag-escape parser and the TerminalHyperlink OSC 8 output.
TerminalHyperlink::Display (update_interactive_command.rs:58) emits an OSC 8 hyperlink:
\x1b]8;;URL\x1b\ai\x1b]8;;\x1b\

The closing string terminator ST is the final two bytes \x1b\ (ESC + backslash 0x5C).
This is then wrapped via Output::pretty(format_args!("<r>{}<r>", hyperlink)). The rendered string tail is ...\x1b\<r>.
When pretty_fmt_runtime (output.rs:2095) encounters \ (0x5C), its b'\\' arm treats it as a Bun-format escape: \< means "literal <." Since the next byte is < from <r>, the handler drops the \ and outputs just <, corrupting the ST. The > is then silently consumed by the b'>' arm.
The leftover r becomes plain text visible after the hyperlinked name.
The original Zig version does not have this bug because Output.pretty processes <tag> markers at compile time — the \ bytes emitted by the hyperlink at runtime never pass through the tag parser.
Affected code:

src/bun_core/output.rs — pretty_fmt_runtime, the b'\\' arm (~line 2095)
src/runtime/cli/update_interactive_command.rs — 4 call sites at lines 1805, 1807, 1809, 1812


Issue researched and drafted with AI assistance.

t: Bun.SQL Postgres: idleTimeout and maxLifetime kill in-flight queries instead of draining
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14 (issue first observed in 1.2.x, persists through 1.3.14)
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (Cloud Run, container oven/bun:1). Backend is Neon Postgres via the Neon transaction-mode pooler.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
import { SQL } from 'bun';

const sql = new SQL({
  url: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
  max: 25,
  idleTimeout: 120,   // or any non-zero value
  maxLifetime: 1800,  // or any non-zero value
});

// Continuous, low-but-nonzero traffic over the lifetime window:
setInterval(() => {
  void sql`SELECT pg_sleep(0.5)`.catch((e) => console.error(e.code, e.message));
}, 250);
After ~maxLifetime seconds, queries that happen to be in-flight on a connection when its lifetime timer fires reject with:
PostgresError: Max lifetime timeout reached after 30m
  code: "ERR_POSTGRES_LIFETIME_TIMEOUT"

Same shape with idleTimeout:
PostgresError: Idle timeout reached after 2m
  code: "ERR_POSTGRES_IDLE_TIMEOUT"

The pool does not retry the killed query on a fresh connection; the rejection bubbles up to the caller.
What is the expected behavior?
When idleTimeout or maxLifetime fires on a connection that has in-flight queries, Bun should let those queries finish and close the connection only once it returns to idle (matching what postgres (postgres-js) and pg already do). Today the timer hard-fails the connection — sets it to failed, rejects every queued/in-flight query, and closes the socket — even when the query itself is healthy and the server is fine.
What do you see instead?
Healthy queries fail with ERR_POSTGRES_LIFETIME_TIMEOUT / ERR_POSTGRES_IDLE_TIMEOUT purely because of a client-side timer race. End-users see a 500 / "page not responding".
Production impact (why we're filing yet another issue on this)
We're running Bun 1.3.14 on Cloud Run against Neon Postgres. We hit both variants of this race in production:

idleTimeout race (default 120s): users would intermittently get 500s after a brief lull in traffic. Sentry caught these as ERR_POSTGRES_IDLE_TIMEOUT originating from internal:sql/postgres. Worked around in our #989 by setting idleTimeout: 0 and adding maxLifetime: 1800 to rotate connections explicitly.
maxLifetime race (the workaround): the workaround moved the failure mode from 2-minute idle to 30-minute lifetime. Same shape — ERR_POSTGRES_LIFETIME_TIMEOUT rejecting an in-flight query. 137 occurrences in 24h under our error grouping ALLY-HOME-5A, surfacing to users as "page not responding".

b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14+0d9b296af
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Create a minimal project with this package.json:
{
  "type":"module",
  "dependencies":{
    "@lexical/react":"0.44.0",
    "lexical":"0.44.0",
    "react":"19.2.6",
    "react-dom":"19.2.6"
  }
}
Create repro.mjs:
await Promise.all([import("@lexical/react/LexicalComposer"), import("@lexical/react/LexicalContentEditable"), import("@lexical/react/LexicalHistoryPlugin"), import("@lexical/react/LexicalListPlugin"), import("@lexical/react/LexicalOnChangePlugin"), import("@lexical/react/LexicalRichTextPlugin")]); console.log("ok");
Run:
bun i
bun repro.mjs
What is the expected behavior?
The imports should complete successfully and print ok.
What do you see instead?
Bun v1.3.14 throws an ESM temporal-dead-zone error from a Lexical module, for example:
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'HISTORY_MERGE_TAG' before initialization

at `.../node_modules/@lexical/react/LexicalComposer.dev.mjs:47:8`

I have also seen the same class of failure as:
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'ElementNode' before initialization

at .../node_modules/@lexical/list/LexicalList.dev.mjs:589:28

Additional information
lexical@0.44.0 uses the node condition for ESM imports, which resolves to Lexical.node.mjs. That file dynamically selects dev/prod via top-level await:
const mod = await (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? import('./Lexical.dev.mjs') : import('./Lexical.prod.mjs'));
It then re-exports many named bindings from mod.
A workaround is to replace that dynamic import with static namespace imports:
import * as modDev from './Lexical.dev.mjs'; import * as modProd from './Lexical.prod.mjs'; const mod = process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? modDev : modProd;

After applying that change, the same imports succeed. This looks like Bun is exposing named exports from the top-level-await wrapper before the underlying module namespace has fully initialized.
📣 Important: Rolling back to Bun 1.3.13 makes the error go away, so I believe this is a regression in Bun 1.3.14.

t: 🚀 Feature Request: Customizable Connection Pool Strategy (eager vs lazy) mysql / postgres
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
This proposal suggests introducing a poolStrategy option (eager vs lazy) and a min connection setting to bun:sql. This would allow users to prevent the current behavior where Bun immediately opens the maximum number of connections upon the first query, instead allowing the pool to grow dynamically from a minimum baseline up to the max limit.

Feature Request: Flexible Connection Pool Scaling (min & poolStrategy)
1. Problem Description
Bun's SQL adapters for MySQL and PostgreSQL currently employ an eager initialization strategy. Regardless of actual demand, the pool instantiates and starts every connection up to the max value as soon as the pool is first accessed. 1
Current Impact:

Thundering Herd: A high max value (e.g., 500) causes 500 simultaneous TCP/TLS handshakes to the database server on the first query. 3
Resource Waste: Applications with low traffic still consume the full memory and connection overhead of the max setting.
Aggressive Recovery: If a pool times out, a single new request triggers a retry of all closed slots simultaneously. 4

2. Proposed API Changes
Update the PostgresOrMySQLOptions in packages/bun-types/sql.d.ts to support these new controls: 5
interface PostgresOrMySQLOptions {
  /**
   * Initialization strategy:
   * - 'eager': Create 'max' connections on startup (current default).
   * - 'lazy': Create connections only as needed.
   * @default "eager"
   */
  poolStrategy?: 'eager' | 'lazy';

  /**
   * Minimum number of connections to keep warm. 
   * Used with 'lazy' strategy to provide a baseline capacity.
   * @default 1
   */
  min?: number;

  max?: number; // Existing option
}
3. Implementation Plan
A. Configuration Parsing
The new options should be integrated into the shared parsing logic in src/js/internal/sql/shared.ts. 6
B. Adaptive Initialization
Modify MySQLAdapter.connect and PostgresAdapter.connect to respect the min and poolStrategy settings. 1

Eager (Current): Loop from 0 to max.
Lazy: Loop from 0 to Math.max(1, min). The remaining slots in the this.connections array (pre-allocated via new Array(max)) should remain null.

C. Dynamic Growth
Update the query request handler. If readyConnections is empty 8 , the adapter should:

Check if the current number of active/pending connections is less than max.
If so, instantiate a new PooledConnection into a null slot in the connections array instead of just queueing the request. 9

t: Feature request — Bun.Image.trim()
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Sprite and icon images frequently have transparent padding around the subject. When resizing
to a small target (e.g. 32×32 favicon), that padding eats into the available space and the
actual content ends up tiny. There is currently no way to remove transparent borders using
Bun.Image alone.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add a chainable .trim() method to Bun.Image that removes border pixels whose alpha is 0
(or optionally matches a specified background colour), equivalent to Sharp's .trim().
Proposed API:
.trim(options?: { threshold?: number }): this
threshold — alpha value below which a pixel is considered background (default 0).

Example:
await new Bun.Image(blob)
.trim()
.resize(32, 32, { fit: "inside" })
.png()
.write("favicon.ico");
What alternatives have you considered?
Manually decoding the PNG with node:zlib (inflateSync), walking every pixel to find the
non-transparent bounding box, cropping the raw RGBA data, and re-encoding — roughly 150
lines of TypeScript just to replicate what Sharp's .trim() does in one call. Works, but
defeats the purpose of having a batteries-included image API.

Bun's Node-compatible process.stdin wrapper owns a TTY.
A Bun.file(...).stream().getReader() starts for an unrelated regular file.
One line is sent through the TTY.
process.stdin receives/pushes the byte, then a later stdin wrapper read returns EOF and closes stdin.

Bun file reader cancelled immediately

latest, currently 1.3.13: fails
1.3.13: fails
1.3.0: fails
1.2.23: fails
1.2.22: fails
1.2.21 and older sampled controls: pass

Version sweep:
https://github.com/art-shen/bun-stdin-bun-file-stream-repro/blob/main/README.md
What is the expected behavior?
Reading an unrelated regular file through Bun.file(...).stream().getReader() should not affect TTY stdin.
After stdin receives the input line:

process.stdin.closed should stay false
process.stdin.destroyed should stay false
process.stdin.readable should stay true
no end / close should be emitted unless fd 0 actually reaches EOF

final state is closed=true, destroyed=true, readable=false

t: Non-ASCII bytes corrupted in String.raw, RegExp.source, and runtime transpiler cache
b:
Bug
Bun's runtime transpiler corrupts non-ASCII (codepoint > 0x7F) bytes in JavaScript-visible values that are contracted to round-trip the source verbatim.
String.raw`╭─╮`.length    // → 18  (expected 3)
/╭─╮/.source.length       // → 18  (expected 3)
String.raw`╭─╮`           // → 18-char Latin-1 mojibake string
The same corruption is persisted to disk by the runtime transpiler cache for source files ≥ 50 KB containing non-ASCII inside a tagged-template raw portion or a regex literal, so once cached, the wrong bytes are served on every subsequent run.
Root cause
The bug spans two layers.
Layer 1 — printer. src/js_printer/js_printer.zig's printRawTemplateLiteral and printRegExpLiteral re-escape codepoints > 0x7F to \uXXXX. Both TemplateStringsArray.raw (which String.raw reads) and RegExp.prototype.source are required by spec to expose the source bytes verbatim — escaping changes the runtime string values.
Layer 2 — JSC handoff. The printer's output buffer is then handed to JSC. Five src/jsc/ sites clone that buffer (or related user-source bytes) as Latin-1 unconditionally:



Site
Bytes cloned
Path




src/jsc/ModuleLoader.zig
printer output
sync module load


src/jsc/RuntimeTranspilerStore.zig
printer output
async runtime transpile


src/jsc/AsyncModule.zig
printer output
async module load


src/jsc/RuntimeTranspilerCache.zig (put())
printer output
runtime cache write


src/jsc/ModuleLoader.zig (already-bundled branch, ~L390)
raw source.contents
pre-bundled JS source


src/jsc/RuntimeTranspilerStore.zig (already-bundled branch, ~L513)
raw source.contents
pre-bundled JS source



For the first four, cloneLatin1 was only correct because the printer historically guaranteed ASCII output (i.e. Layer 1 covered for Layer 2). Once the printer is fixed, all four mis-interpret multi-byte UTF-8 sequences as Latin-1 chars and split each codepoint into garbage.
The last two are not printer output — they clone raw user source on the already_bundled path. Whether the corruption is user-visible depends on what JSC does with source_code when .already_bundled = true and .bytecode_cache is populated (error formatting, Function.prototype.toString, sourcemap mapping, etc.); needs verification, but the call shape is the same class of bug and should be audited.
Reproduction
Plain runtime path:
bun -e 'console.log(String.raw`╭─╮`.length, /╭─╮/.source.length)'
# prints: 18 18
# expected: 3 3
Runtime transpiler cache (file must be ≥ 50 KB to trigger the cache):
mkdir -p /tmp/btc

minimumReleaseAge currently helps reduce supply-chain risk during dependency installation by avoiding packages that were published too recently.

t: minimumReleaseAge is silently bypassed for versions already in bun.lock
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13 (bf2e2ce) on macOS (Darwin 25.4.0)
What is the problem?
minimumReleaseAge in bunfig.toml is only checked during dependency resolution. If a version is already pinned in bun.lock, both bun install and bun install --frozen-lockfile install it without enforcing the cooldown, even when that locked version was published well within the configured window.
This means the cooldown does not protect against the very scenario it's marketed for: a poisoned version that has already landed in the lockfile (e.g., committed by a developer whose local bunfig was less strict, or pulled in before the cooldown was added).
Reproduction
mkdir bun-minage-bypass && cd bun-minage-bypass

cat > package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "minage-bypass", "private": true, "dependencies": { "is-odd": "3.0.1" } }
JSON

# 1. Install with no cooldown to populate bun.lock
bun install

# 2. Add a cooldown that the locked version should violate.
#    is-odd@3.0.1 was published in 2017; a 10-year cooldown means
#    "only install versions >= 10 years old" — 3.0.1 is younger than that.
cat > bunfig.toml <<'TOML'
[install]
minimumReleaseAge = 315360000
TOML

# 3. Reinstall — cooldown should reject is-odd@3.0.1
rm -rf node_modules
bun install                      # → installs 3.0.1, exit 0
bun install --frozen-lockfile    # → installs 3.0.1, exit 0
Expected behavior
bun install (and especially bun install --frozen-lockfile) should fail or warn when a version in the lockfile violates minimumReleaseAge. Otherwise the setting is only a barrier at the moment a new dependency is added — not a durable guarantee about what gets installed in CI.
Actual behavior
The cooldown is silently ignored. The package installs with exit 0 in both modes.
Why this matters
This is the same flaw class as pnpm/pnpm#10438, filed in the wake of the May 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud TanStack compromise. The cooldown is widely understood as supply-chain protection — defenders adding it after the fact (e.g., in response to a published advisory) reasonably expect it to gate every `bun install`, not just net-new resolutions.
The current behavior also asymmetrically penalizes the disciplined case: a team that adds `minimumReleaseAge` after an incident is no safer than one that doesn't, because any already-resolved bad version remains installable.
Possible fixes

Enforce the cooldown at install-from-lockfile time, not only during resolution.
Or add a `--resolution-only`-style mode (like pnpm has) that forces

t: --env-file and Bun.file().text() silently drop data on FIFOs; breaks 1Password's local-env-file integration
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13+bf2e2cecf
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
1Password's Environments → Local env file feature exposes secrets through a FIFO at a path of the user's choosing. Opening the FIFO for read triggers 1Password to write the resolved env data to it, so secrets never touch disk. cat, dotenv, and Node's fs.readFileSync all read it correctly. Bun does not.
The same behavior reproduces with a hand-rolled FIFO and a backgrounded writer, so 1Password isn't required to repro:
printf 'console.log("FOO=", process.env.FOO ?? "<unset>")\n' > /tmp/test.ts

# (A) FIFO, no writer — Bun hangs forever
mkfifo /tmp/p
timeout 5 bun --env-file=/tmp/p /tmp/test.ts
echo "exit=$?"   # 124

# (B) FIFO with writer attached — Bun proceeds but loads nothing
rm /tmp/p && mkfifo /tmp/p
( printf 'FOO=worked\n' > /tmp/p ) &
sleep 0.2
bun --env-file=/tmp/p /tmp/test.ts
# FOO= <unset>

# (C) Bun.file().text() exhibits the same hang on the same FIFO
rm /tmp/p && mkfifo /tmp/p
cat > /tmp/read.ts <<'INNER'
console.log(await Bun.file(process.argv[2]).text());
INNER
timeout 5 bun /tmp/read.ts /tmp/p
echo "exit=$?"   # 124

# (D) Control: node:fs.readFileSync drains the same FIFO correctly
rm /tmp/p && mkfifo /tmp/p
( printf 'FOO=worked\n' > /tmp/p ) &
sleep 0.2
bun -e 'console.log(require("node:fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"))' /tmp/p
# FOO=worked
What is the expected behavior?
Bun should read FIFO-backed env files the same way cat, dotenv, and node:fs.readFileSync do: open, read to EOF, parse. This is a documented and supported 1Password workflow.
What do you see instead?

bun --env-file=<FIFO>: blocks forever if no writer is attached; silently loads zero vars when a writer is attached and EOF is reached.
Bun.file(<FIFO>).text(): same two failure modes.
node:fs.readFileSync(<FIFO>, 'utf8'): works correctly.

Additional information
Workaround (no extra deps): use the Node-compat APIs Bun already ships.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { parseEnv } from "node:util";
Object.assign(process.env, parseEnv(readFileSync(path, "utf8")));
Unverified hypothesis (for maintainers to confirm): Bun's native file reader appears to size its read buffer from stat().size and short-circuit on size == 0. FIFOs always report st_size == 0, so the read either blocks forever (no data ever arrives via stat) or returns "0 bytes" once a writer attaches. The Node-compat layer evidently uses a read-until-EOF loo

What version of Bun is running?

What platform is your computer?
Reproduced on both macOS arm64 and Alpine Linux x64 (oven/bun:1-alpine). Not OS-specific.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Scenario
A GitLab package consumer setup that mixes instance-level scope resolution with project-level auth — a common pattern in self-hosted GitLab where packages are published per-project but consumed through the instance-wide registry endpoint.
.npmrc
@myorg:registry=https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/packages/npm/

Note the two paths:

Scoped registry URL path: /api/v4/packages/npm/ (instance-level)
_authToken scope path: /api/v4/projects/123/packages/npm/ (project-level)

These paths diverge — neither is a prefix of the other.
What bun install --frozen-lockfile does
The lockfile contains the tarball URL resolved to the project-level path that GitLab returned in the metadata response:
https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/123/packages/npm/@myorg/web-ui-kit/-/@myorg/web-ui-kit-0.3.6.tgz

> HTTP/1.1 GET https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/123/packages/npm/@myorg/web-ui-kit/-/@myorg/web-ui-kit-0.3.6.tgz
> Connection: keep-alive
> User-Agent: Bun/1.3.13
> Accept: */*
> Host: gitlab.example.com
> Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd

GitLab masks unauthenticated package-registry requests as 404 (not 401), so the resulting error is:
error: GET https://gitlab.example.com/.../@myorg/web-ui-kit-0.3.6.tgz - 404

The same .npmrc is handled correctly by npm CLI and previously by bun ≤ 1.3.10: the _authToken whose scope path is /api/v4/projects/123/packages/npm/ is sent on requests to URLs under that path (which the tarball URL is).
Per npm's .npmrc spec, auth credentials are nerf darts that apply to request URLs matching their scope by longest prefix. The matching is done against the request URL at fetch time, not against the registry URL at config-load time.

bun install makes the tarball request without the Authorization header, so GitLab returns 404 and the install fails.

$ bun build --minify ./without-comment.js
var e=1,r=2,a=3,c=4,f=5,n=6;function o(){return e+r+a+c+f+n}export{o as go};

The two outputs assign different single-letter names to the same variables, and occasionally differ in total byte count.
The letter chosen for the most-frequent name tracks the contents of the leading comment: stuff the comment with 42 q characters and the output starts with var q=1,.... The same effect appears with any mid-file block comment of ≥ 32 bytes.
What is the expected behavior?
Minified output should be byte-identical for source files that differ only in comments. Comments are stripped during minification and should not influence the renamer.
What do you see instead?
Identifier assignment shifts based on the literal characters inside dropped comments, producing different (and unstable) minified output for semantically identical input. This hurts gzip ratios across rebuilds and produces unnecessary diffs in committed bundles.
Additional information
No response

t: [Docs] Contributor onboarding: component map and beginner-friendly entry points
b:
Summary
Bun has a remarkable architecture — Zig core, JSC engine, Node.js/Deno compatibility
layers, and a growing set of built-in modules. But for someone arriving at the repo
for the first time (whether beginner or experienced in other ecosystems), there is
no single place that answers: "Where should I start, and why?"
This issue proposes adding a contributor component guide to the docs or
CONTRIBUTING.md — something that maps the major subsystems, explains what each one
does, and points new contributors toward the areas where their time will have the
most impact with the least upfront cost.

Note: The examples in this issue were chosen at random as a starting point
to illustrate the format. They are almost certainly incomplete or inaccurate in
places. I'd love input from the core team and the community to correct the
difficulty signal, add missing components, and point to reference PRs that show
the idiomatic pattern for each area. The goal is a living map, not a one-shot
document.


Problem
Right now, a first-time contributor faces:

A large, polyglot codebase (Zig, C++, TypeScript, JavaScript) with no clear
entry-point signal
No explanation of which pieces are original Zig implementations vs. ported/adapted
from Node.js, Deno, or other runtimes
No suggested reading path: no "start here" PRs, no "these 3 files explain the
pattern" pointers
A high activation cost: you have to spend hours just understanding the lay of
the land before you can form a meaningful contribution idea

This raises the barrier disproportionately for developers who believe in Bun's
vision but don't yet know where to plug in.

Proposed Addition
Section 1 — Suggested Reading (Architecture at a Glance)
A short prose overview covering:

JavaScript engine: Bun uses JavaScriptCore (JSC) from WebKit, not V8.
Why this matters for contributors touching JS bindings.
The three-layer pattern: as introduced in the recent src/ restructure,
each subsystem is split into src/<component>/ (pure Zig, no JSC deps),
src/<component>_jsc/ (JSC bridge — toJS/fromJS/JSValue), and optionally
src/<component>_types/ (shared leaf types used across layers). Understanding
this boundary is the single most important mental model for new contributors.
The binding layer: how Zig functions are exposed to JS (napi, JSC C API,
or custom bindings generated via bindgen).
Build system: why make bun is just the start, and what bun.zig and
the build.zig files orchestrate.

Suggested format: 3–5 paragraphs + a diagram of th

`Bun.build()` inside a `bun --hot` entry permanently disables hot reload
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13+bf2e2cecf
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 (WSL2 on Windows host). Filesystem: ext4.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
mkdir /tmp/bun-bug && cd /tmp/bun-bug
cat > app.ts <<'TS'
declare global { var n: number | undefined; var done: boolean | undefined; }
globalThis.n = (globalThis.n ?? 0) + 1;
console.log(`n=${globalThis.n} v=A`);
if (!globalThis.done) {
  globalThis.done = true;
  try { await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['nonexistent.ts'] }); } catch {}
}
TS
bun --hot app.ts &
sleep 1; sed -i 's/v=A/v=B/' app.ts
sleep 1; sed -i 's/v=B/v=C/' app.ts
sleep 1
What is the expected behavior?
Log prints:
n=1 v=A
n=2 v=B
n=3 v=C

i.e. --hot re-evaluates the entry on each save. Removing the await Bun.build(...) block and re-running prints all three values as expected, so --hot itself works — it's the presence of the build call that breaks it.
What do you see instead?
Log prints only:
n=1 v=A

Subsequent sed -i saves are ignored. The single await Bun.build({entrypoints: ['nonexistent.ts']}) call (which itself rejects, since the entrypoint doesn't exist) silently disables --hot's reload pipeline for the rest of the process's life.
Additional information

It doesn't matter whether Bun.build's entrypoint exists, whether the build resolves or rejects, or whether outdir is set vs in-memory. Any Bun.build() call from the entry kills --hot.
The one exception: if Bun.build's entrypoints is the running script itself ('./app.ts' here), --hot continues to fire. Targeting any other file (or a non-existent file) breaks it.
The inotify FD remains in /proc/<pid>/fd after the build call, so the watcher isn't being torn down. The reload-on-event pipeline is what's silently disabled.
This breaks any framework that runs a build pipeline inside the user's entry script (e.g. SSR/SSG frameworks that pre-bundle client code on dev-server startup). It's how I hit it: AbsoluteJS's prepare() runs several Bun.build() calls for frontend bundles before listening, after which backend HMR (server entry edits) is silently dead while frontend HMR — which goes through the framework's own fs.watch + module server, not --hot — keeps working.
Happy to share traces / a minimal real-world repro if it helps.

b:
First, thanks again for publishing the bun-webkit autobuild archives — I filed #30427 the other day asking about a Windows /MD CRT variant; this is a separate (and smaller) report on a different consumer-facing edge case. I want to be upfront that this issue describes a code path Bun itself doesn't use, so the priority on your end should be very low. I'm flagging it because it's a consequence of the archive being reused outside of Bun, and you may want to know.
Background
I'm embedding libJavaScriptCore.a from your archive in a Swift package on Linux x64 + arm64 (glibc + musl) and Android NDK — full integration in Cocoanetics/SwiftBash#23. The standalone JSC C API (JSGlobalContextCreate / JSGlobalContextRelease) is the natural entry point for non-Bun consumers: stable headers, symbol-compatible with Apple's framework, no C++ ABI dependency.
Symptom
Calling JSGlobalContextRelease on a context allocated via JSGlobalContextCreate(NULL) deadlocks for approximately 62 seconds, then SIGABRTs (Aborted (core dumped), no diagnostic output). Reproduces every run on:

Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 against bun-webkit-linux-amd64.tar.gz
Android NDK x86_64 against bun-webkit-linux-amd64-android.tar.gz

(WebKit-fork commit pinned at 88b2f7a2159c913f7dd0d73c0e88d66138cd67ba.)
For comparison, the same call works on:

Apple's system framework JSC (no hang).
WebKitGTK's libjavascriptcoregtk (used by JXKit, the next-largest non-Bun JSC-on-Linux consumer — they call JSGlobalContextRelease unconditionally without issue).

So the issue appears specific to the bun-webkit standalone build's C-API teardown path.
Likely cause: the path is dead code in your codebase
I checked the Bun source — JSGlobalContextRelease is never called anywhere. Bun bypasses the C-API context entirely by redefining JSGlobalContextRef as a direct pointer to a C++ JSGlobalObject:
// src/jsc/javascript_core_c_api.zig:18
pub const JSGlobalContextRef = ?*jsc.JSGlobalObject;
VM lifecycle is managed via C++ JSC::VM::tryCreate / JSC::JSGlobalObject::create. Since Bun never reaches OpaqueJSContext::~OpaqueJSContext (or wherever WebKit's standalone C-API release path winds up), any breakage there is dead code from your perspective and would have gone unnoticed. We may be the first non-Bun consumer to hit it.

t: YAML.stringify does not quote strings with trailing colons, producing invalid YAML
b:
Bug Report
Bun version: 1.3.2 (Linux x64)
Description
YAML.stringify from bun does not quote string values that end with a colon (:). The resulting YAML is structurally invalid — subsequent YAML.parse calls (and third-party parsers) reject it with a parse error.
A colon at the end of a plain scalar is ambiguous in YAML (it can be read as beginning a new mapping value). Conformant YAML emitters quote such strings.
Steps to Reproduce
import { YAML } from 'bun'

const obj = {
  subject: 'Q2 planning followup:',   // trailing colon — should be quoted
  note: 'foo:',                        // trailing colon — should be quoted
  safe: 'bar: baz',                    // colon + space — correctly quoted
  id: '0e6836',                        // looks like scientific notation — NOT quoted (bonus issue)
}

const out = YAML.stringify(obj, null, 2)
console.log('--- output ---')
console.log(out)

try {
  YAML.parse(out)
  console.log('parsed ok')
} catch (e) {
  console.log('round-trip parse error:', e.message)
}
Actual Output
--- output ---
subject: Q2 planning followup:
note: foo:
safe: "bar: baz"
id: 0e6836

round-trip parse error: YAML Parse error: Unexpected token

Expected Output
All values that would be structurally ambiguous in YAML must be quoted. The emitted YAML must round-trip through YAML.parse without error.
subject: 'Q2 planning followup:'
note: 'foo:'
safe: 'bar: baz'
id: '0e6836'
Notes

safe: "bar: baz" (colon followed by a space mid-string) is correctly quoted — so the quoting logic exists but is incomplete.
id: 0e6836 is not quoted; in YAML 1.1 this can be misread as scientific notation (0e+6836 = 0). It is a separate but related gap in the quoting heuristic.
The practical impact: any application that serialises domain objects containing strings ending in : (e.g. email subjects, log messages, URLs) will silently write corrupt YAML files that cannot be reloaded, with no error at write time.

Workaround
Use the js-yaml npm package (npm install js-yaml) which correctly quotes all values that require it:
import { dump } from 'js-yaml'
dump({ subject: 'Q2 planning followup:', note: 'foo:' }, { indent: 2 })
// subject: 'Q2 planning followup:'
// note: 'foo:'

t: Windows: publish /MD (dynamic CRT) JSC archive alongside /MT to enable third-party static linking
b:
First, sincere thanks — the bun-webkit-<triple>.tar.gz archives are by far the cleanest pre-built JavaScriptCore artifact available anywhere. Stripping out WebCore / WebKit2 / GTK glue and shipping just libJavaScriptCore.a + libWTF.a + libbmalloc.a + ICU + the Apple-compatible C-API headers makes JSC realistically reusable for runtimes that aren't Bun. The JSC C API stability + your build means JSContextRef/JSValueRef-using Swift, Rust, Zig, etc. code can target macOS, Linux glibc/musl x64+arm64, Android, and FreeBSD without writing per-platform glue. That's a real gift to the runtime ecosystem and it's appreciated.
I'm writing because there's one Windows-specific roadblock that a tiny build-config flip on your end would unlock for every non-Bun consumer, and I wanted to surface it without assuming priorities.
Context
I've been wiring Bun's JSC artifact into SwiftBash — a Swift bash interpreter — to give its embedded JS runtime (SwiftJSCore) the same engine on every supported platform. Apple uses the system framework; Linux/Android consume libJavaScriptCore.a from your tarball. End-to-end smoke (sample binary, runs JSGlobalContextCreate → JSEvaluateScript → JSValueToNumber) is green on macOS, iOS, Linux, and Android via the C API. Excellent.
Windows is where it stops, and the reason is interesting.
What we hit on Windows
Bun's bun-webkit-windows-amd64.tar.gz .libs are compiled with MSVC's /MT (static CRT) flag — which is the right choice for Bun's own use case, since the final bun.exe is a single statically-linked binary. But Swift's runtime on Windows is built with /MD (dynamic CRT) because swiftCore.dll/swift_Concurrency.dll/etc. ship as DLLs that interop through the dynamic CRT.
lld-link reads the embedded /FAILIFMISMATCH:RuntimeLibrary=... directives in each .obj/.lib and refuses the mix:
lld-link: error: /failifmismatch: mismatch detected for 'RuntimeLibrary':
>>> swiftrt.obj has value MD_DynamicRelease
>>> JavaScriptCore.lib(UnifiedSource-d93d10ff-1.cpp.obj) has value MT_StaticRelease

This isn't paperwork — overriding via /FORCE:MULTIPLE produces a binary that corrupts memory at runtime (separate malloc heaps between CRTs, separate FILE* tables, separate errno thread-locals, separate atexit chains). The check is doing exactly what it should.
The same restriction applies to anyone trying to link your Windows JSC into a Rust binary built against MSVC's default /MD, a Zig binary, a Tauri plugin, or any other runtime that didn't make Bun's "single-binar

t: TOCTOU Vulnerability in `Buffer.prototype.write`
b:
What version of Bun is running?
No response
What platform is your computer?
No response
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Severity: High
Component: src/jsc/bindings/JSBuffer.cpp
Affected Versions: Bun v1.3.12 through v1.3.14-canary.1 (6d0d86b), and all prior versions
Tested On: Windows 11 x64, Bun Canary v1.3.14-canary.1 (6d0d86b)
Related Prior Fix: PR #29731 — same bug class, fixed in Buffer.prototype.copy and Buffer.prototype.fill only
Fixes: #29730

Background
PR #29731 (fixing issue #29730) established the pattern: buffer state — pointer and logical length — must not be cached before user-controlled JavaScript has a chance to run. When toInteger(), toInt32(), or toWTFString() is called on an argument object, the object's valueOf() or toString() fires. That callback can call ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer(), which detaches the backing store and sets the internal data pointer to nullptr. Any subsequent native read or write through that pointer crashes the process.
Buffer.prototype.write has two distinct call branches where the same mistake is repeated: byteLength() is cached before a user-visible coercion runs, and no isDetached() guard is added before the final writeToBuffer() call.
I found this by walking every other call site in JSBuffer.cpp that follows the same capture-then-coerce order that copy and fill used before they were fixed.

Vulnerability 1: Denial of Service via Buffer.prototype.write — string branch
Root Cause
When Buffer.prototype.write is called as buf.write(value, encoding) — where encoding is passed as the second argument (a string) — the interpreter hits the branch at line 2378:
// JSBuffer.cpp, line 2378–2386
if (lengthValue.isUndefined() && offsetValue.isString()) {
    encodingValue = offsetValue;
    offset = 0;
    length = castedThis->byteLength();      // ← length captured here

    auto* str = stringValue.toString(lexicalGlobalObject);  // ← user JS fires here
    auto encoding = parseEncoding(scope, lexicalGlobalObject, encodingValue, false);
    RETURN_IF_EXCEPTION(scope, {});
    RELEASE_AND_RETURN(scope, writeToBuffer(lexicalGlobalObject, castedThis, str, offset, length, encoding));
}
There is no call to Bun::V::validateString before stringValue.toString(). That means if stringValue is an object (not a primitive string), toString() invokes the object's toString method — a user-controlled JavaScript callback. Add a flag for `bun update` to update the lockfile without saving to `package.json`
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
bun update currently saves updated dependency specifiers to package.json by default.
--no-save is not a workaround because it disables both package.json writes and lockfile saving. So, confusingly, --no-save is not the opposite of --save.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I’d like a way to update resolved dependency versions in bun.lock while preserving the existing semver ranges in package.json. This is a workflow that is very common amongst other package managers (npm, Yarn Classic, Cargo, Composer, uv, Poetry, Bundler). pnpm supports this functionality with their --no-save flag, an unfortunately confusing change for anyone migrating.
It's clear from reading #5856 that many users strongly prefer the current default, and so I do not intend to suggest that it should be changed. However I see no reason why there should not be a way to achieve this with a flag. Given the backwards compatibility challenges associated with aligning the functionality of bun update --no-save with pnpm update --no-save, my suggestion is for the addition of a new flag, for example:

bun update --no-save-package-json
bun update --frozen-package-json

A related .bunfig.toml option could also be useful to let projects standardise the behaviour across contributors, local scripts, and CI without requiring every bun update invocation to remember the flag, for example:
[install]
savePackageJsonOnUpdate = false
What alternatives have you considered?
Today the closest workaround is to let bun update perform the update, then undo the unwanted package.json changes, then regenerate or validate the lockfile against the restored manifest:
bun update <pkg>
git restore package.json
bun install --lockfile-only

t: Bun fetch + HTTPS-over-CONNECT-proxy: raw upstream HTTP/1.1 leaks into response.body
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14
What platform is your computer?
Linux 5.15.0-106-generic x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14
What platform is your computer?
Linux 5.15.0-106-generic x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Background
I hit this trying to run Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI) through an HTTP CONNECT proxy. Every request would hang for ~10s and then time out. Claude Code uses Bun's native fetch(), and the Anthropic API endpoint serves chunked SSE over keep-alive HTTPS — exactly the combination this bug requires. Direct connections (no proxy) work fine; the same proxy works fine with curl, Node, and browsers, which is what pointed at Bun's CONNECT-tunnel code path.
Investigation and minimization to the repro below were done with Claude's help.
Summary
When Bun's fetch() is configured with an HTTP proxy: (or HTTPS_PROXY env var) and the target is https://, Bun establishes the CONNECT tunnel correctly but then fails to parse the upstream's HTTP/1.1 response inside the tunnel:

response.headers is populated from the proxy's CONNECT 200 envelope (proxy-agent, connection: close) instead of the upstream's actual headers.
response.body receives the raw, unparsed upstream bytes — the literal HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n… status line, all upstream headers, every chunked-encoding size prefix (1b\r\n), and the chunked terminator (0\r\n\r\n) — all delivered as body data.
Because the chunked terminator is never recognized, the stream only ends on TCP FIN. A spec-compliant keep-alive upstream (RFC 7230 §4.1 — terminator is the end-of-body signal, FIN not required) hangs the request indefinitely.

Direct mode (no proxy) works correctly. curl, Node/undici, Go, Python requests, and browsers all handle this case correctly. Source-code analysis below points at src/http/http.zig handleResponseMetadata being invoked twice with the CONNECT envelope and committing it as the user-facing response on the second call.
Repro
# 1. self-signed cert
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 1 -nodes \
  -subj '/CN=127.0.0.1' -addext 'subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1'

# 2. start the upstream server (chunked SSE, keep-alive, no FIN) in one terminal
python3 server.py

# 3. start any HTTP CONNECT forward proxy on 127.0.0.1:8888 in another terminal
# (e.g. tinyproxy, gost, mitmproxy --mode regular, or write 30 lines yourself). When finding the bug, gost is used as the proxy.

# 4. baseline: direct mode

t: bun test output truncated on Windows when test files leak async handles
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Prerequisite: A project with test files that leak async handles (recursive setTimeout / setImmediate) across files without proper cleanup.

Clone https://github.com/AlphaFoxz/buntui (commit 8ef0a17)
Run bun install
Run bun run --cwd ./packages/native build (builds the native Zig library)
Run bun run --cwd ./packages/core build (syncs native binary)
Run bun test ./packages/core/

Result: Output is truncated — only the version line appears:
bun test v1.3.13 (bf2e2cec)

The process exits with code 0 (tests pass), but no test results or summary are printed. Only 28 bytes are written to stdout.
What is the expected behavior?
Full test output with summary:
bun test v1.3.13 (bf2e2cec)

484 pass
0 fail
958 expect() calls
Ran 484 tests across 26 files. [166.00ms]

What do you see instead?
Output is truncated — only the version line appears:
bun test v1.3.13 (bf2e2cec)

The process exits with code 0 (tests pass), but no test results are printed. Piping through cat, tee, or redirecting to a file shows the same truncated output (only 28 bytes written).
Root Cause
The truncation is caused by leaked async handles (recursive setTimeout / setImmediate) in test files that are not properly cleaned up. In this project, TuiApp.test.ts calls app.start() which internally starts a RenderLoop (recursive setTimeout(tick, 5)), but some tests don't call app.dispose() to stop it.
The bug is in Bun's test runner output flushing on Windows — when leaked handles keep the event loop alive, the test runner appears to exit before flushing the buffered summary output to stdout. This is a Bun bug because:

--isolate fixes it — bun test ./packages/core/ --isolate shows full output every time (leaked handles are isolated per-file)
Explicit subdirectory listing fixes it — passing each subdirectory individually also avoids truncation
Not reproducible on macOS/Linux — only observed on Windows

Use --isolate: bun test ./packages/core/ --isolate

t: HTTP/2 Flow Control Bug in node:http2 - Requests Hang Indefinitely
b:
What version of Bun is running?
No response
What platform is your computer?
No response
What steps can reproduce the bug?
🐛 HTTP/2 Flow Control Bug in node:http2 - Requests Hang Indefinitely
What version of Bun is running?
Bun 1.3.10 and 1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
macOS arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use @grpc/grpc-js 1.14.3 with Pulumi runtime set to bun
Make a gRPC call with request body larger than 65,535 bytes (default HTTP/2 stream window)
The peer sends a connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE followed by a SETTINGS frame that increases SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE
The request hangs indefinitely

Example trace from Pulumi:
start ctfd:index/file:File tunnel-file-tunnel.zip contentb64=0 bytes=87136 jsonbytes=86155
transport create call=431 method=/pulumirpc.ResourceMonitor/RegisterResource
subchannel write call=431 bytes=87141
subchannel halfClose call=431

The write-callback-ok and stream-close events never occur.
What is the expected behavior?
Per RFC 7540 section 6.9.2, when INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE changes, existing streams' send windows must be adjusted by the delta between the new and old values. The request should complete successfully as it does in Node.js.
What do you see instead?
The request hangs indefinitely because:

Bun queues DATA frames when the request exceeds 65,535 bytes 1
When the peer sends SETTINGS to increase the window size, Bun incorrectly compares the new per-stream initialWindowSize with the connection-level remoteWindowSize 2
If the connection window was already raised, this condition is false, so stream windows are never updated
Queued DATA frames remain blocked indefinitely

Root Cause Analysis
The bug is in handleSettingsFrame() in src/bun.js/api/bun/h2_frame_parser.zig:
if (remoteSettings.initialWindowSize >= this.remoteWindowSize) {
    var it = this.streams.valueIterator();
    while (it.next()) |item| {
        const stream = item.*;
        if (remoteSettings.initialWindowSize >= stream.remoteWindowSize) {
            stream.remoteWindowSize = remoteSettings.initialWindowSize;
        }
    }
}
This violates RFC 7540 section 6.9.2 by:

Comparing per-stream window with connection window (independent flow control mechanisms)
Only updating streams if new size >= current window
Direct assignment instead of applying delta to all existing streams

The correct implementation should:

Store the previous initialWindowSize value
Calculate the delta: delta = new_size - old_size
Apply this delta to every existing stream

t: sideEffects glob patterns broken on Windows
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13+bf2e2cecf
What platform is your computer?
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
unzip the attached repro
cd bun-sideeffects-bug-repro
bun install
bun run build.ts

bun-sideeffects-bug-repro.zip
The repro has a local package (my-lib) with "sideEffects": ["adapters/**/*.js"] in its package.json. The consumer imports side-effect-only modules from that package. The bundler should preserve them.
What is the expected behavior?
Contains "foo adapter registered": true
Contains "bar adapter registered": true
✅ OK: Side-effect imports preserved correctly.

Side-effect-only imports matching the sideEffects globs should be kept in the bundle (as they are on Linux/macOS)
What do you see instead?
Contains "foo adapter registered": false
Contains "bar adapter registered": false
❌ BUG: Side-effect imports were tree-shaken despite sideEffects globs.

The bundler drops all side-effect imports because the glob patterns never match on Windows.
Additional information
Root cause: Bun resolves file paths with backslashes on Windows (e.g. adapters\foo.js) but matches them against forward-slash glob patterns from sideEffects (e.g. adapters/**/*.js). The globs never match, so Bun treats every file as side-effect-free and removes them.
Proof it's the glob matching:

"sideEffects": true → adapters preserved ✅
sideEffects field removed entirely → adapters preserved ✅
"sideEffects": ["adapters/**/*.js"] → adapters tree-shaken ❌ (Windows only)

Real-world impact: discovered in prebid.js@10.29.0 which uses "sideEffects": ["dist/src/modules/**/*.js", ...]. All bid adapters are silently dropped from the bundle on Windows.
Related: #18008

t: Private GitLab npm registry: scoped package resolution fails (401/404) since 1.3.x
b:
Bug Report
Summary
Since bun 1.3.x, resolving scoped packages from a private GitLab npm registry fails with a 404.
bun 1.2.23 works correctly. The regression was introduced when encoding the slash in scoped package
names for private registry manifest requests — bun 1.3.x now sends @scope%2fname (lowercase %2f)
where 1.2.x sent @scope/name (unencoded slash). GitLab's npm registry accepts the unencoded form
but rejects lowercase %2f.

Environment









Affected
bun 1.3.0 → 1.3.13 (all 1.3.x releases tested: 1.3.13)


Working
bun 1.2.23


OS
macOS 15 (arm64), Alpine Linux (node:22-alpine in CI)


Registry
GitLab self-hosted npm registry (/api/v4/packages/npm/)


.npmrc
scoped registry configured via @scope:registry=https://...




Reproduction
.npmrc (committed to repo):
@myorg:registry=https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/packages/npm/
//gitlab.example.com/:_authToken=${MY_TOKEN}
package.json (any scoped private dependency):
{                                                                                                                                                                                 
  "dependencies": {                                                                                                                                                               
    "@myorg/somepackage": "^1.0.0"
  }                                                                                                                                                                               
}                                                          
Run with a cleared bun cache:
rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache/@myorg
bun install

Actual behavior (bun 1.3.x)
error: GET https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/packages/npm/@myorg%2fsomepackage - 404
error: @myorg/somepackage@^1.0.0 failed to resolve
bun sends the package manifest request with the slash between scope and name percent-encoded as
lowercase %2f:
GET /api/v4/packages/npm/@myorg%2fsomepackage HTTP/1.1
Host: gitlab.example.com
Authorization: Bearer 
GitLab's npm registry returns 404 for this URL (it does not normalize %2f to /).

Expected behavior (bun 1.2.x)
bun 1.2.23 sends the manifest request with the unencoded slash:
GET /api/v4/packages/npm/@myorg/somepackage HTTP/1.1
Host: gitlab.example.com
Authorization: Bearer 
GitLab returns 200 with the package metadata, and resolution succeeds.
Evidence: bun 1.2.23 generates a working bun.lock with correctly resolved tarball URLs:
"@myorg/somepackage": ["@myorg/somepack

Repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess, os, signal, time, sys

print(f\"Parent Python PID: {os.getpid()}\", flush=True)
child = subprocess.Popen([\"bun\", \"run\", \"child.ts\"])
time.sleep(1)
print(f\"Killing self ({os.getpid()})...\", flush=True)
os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)
child.ts
console.log(\`Bun child PID: \${process.pid}, initial ppid: \${process.ppid}\`);
const initialPpid = process.ppid;
let tick = 0;

t: `Bun.Transpiler` does not emit React Fast Refresh transforms for `.tsx` (inconsistent with `Bun.build`)
`bun link` is silently ignored under the isolated linker
b:
Summary
Under the isolated linker (default for workspaces with configVersion = 1), running bun link in a producer package and bun link <pkg> in a consumer has no effect when the consumer's dependency resolves via npm or a catalog. The consumer's node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@<ver>/node_modules/<pkg> body is materialized from the registry tarball cache — the producer's working tree is never read. Edits in the producer never reach the consumer.
The hoisted linker honors the link as expected. There is no warning, no diagnostic, no opt-out flag — bun link simply does nothing.
Steps to reproduce
# Producer
mkdir -p /tmp/prod && cd /tmp/prod
echo '{"name":"my-pkg","version":"1.0.0","main":"index.js"}' > package.json
echo 'export const v = "from-producer";' > index.js
bun link

# Consumer (workspace or any project pinning my-pkg via npm version)
mkdir -p /tmp/cons && cd /tmp/cons
echo '{"name":"c","dependencies":{"my-pkg":"^1.0.0"}}' > package.json
bun link my-pkg
bun install
cat node_modules/my-pkg/index.js   # ← shows the registry tarball, not "from-producer"
Expected: consumer reads from-producer.
Actual: consumer reads whatever the registry tarball ships.
Why this matters
The point of bun link is the iteration loop on a locally-developed package. Under isolated installs the loop is broken silently — consumers run against stale cached versions. In monorepos this surfaces as mismatched versions of shared deps (e.g. two react instances) once a local fork of an npm package gets linked but the link is ignored.
Related
#29727 — different root cause (TS peer resolution against global symlink cache), but same general area of "isolated linker behaves unexpectedly in non-default paths."
Environment

Bun: 1.3.13
Linker: isolated
OS: macOS 26.3


PR #29615 seeks to implement a fix.

oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.

t: bun install reports success but creates empty package dirs on OneDrive-mounted Windows paths
b:
What version of Bun is running?
Bun v1.3.13 (latest stable as of May 2026)
What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 (x64), Git Bash on MSYS2
Working directory location
This issue ONLY reproduces in worktrees mounted under OneDrive sync (e.g. C:\Users\<user>\OneDrive\Downloads\<project>). The same bun install against a native NTFS path (e.g. C:\Users\<user>\Documents\<project>) works correctly.
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Clone any TypeScript repo with significant npm deps (e.g. @anthropic-ai/sdk, openai, @google/genai) into a OneDrive-synced path
Run bun install
Bun reports success: "722 packages installed [665ms]"
Try to import any installed package: runtime fails with Cannot find module '@anthropic-ai/sdk'
Inspect: ls node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/ shows the directory EXISTS but is EMPTY (0 files)
Workaround: npm install correctly populates package contents

What is the expected behavior?
bun install either correctly populates package contents OR fails loudly with an error indicating that the OneDrive filesystem is unsupported.
What do you see instead?
Silent partial install: directory entries are created but file contents aren't materialized. The reported "722 packages installed" number matches npm install output, but actual byte-count of node_modules/ is ~204KB (vs ~250MB for npm install).
Hypothesis on root cause
OneDrive's filesystem virtualization layer (Files On-Demand) intercepts file operations. Bun's install path appears to use hardlinks/symlinks for speed (per Bun docs), but OneDrive's reparse-point semantics differ from native NTFS hardlinks. The directory structure gets created but file content materialization is skipped or fails silently.
NPM's traditional mkdir + write install path correctly handles OneDrive (likely because OneDrive's file-write hooks are well-tested vs. less-common hardlink/symlink hooks).
Hit count this session
4+ different worktrees hit this in a single 24-hour session (claude-teams-bot project on May 4, 2026):

PR #88 fix-up
PR #94 build agent
PR #97 build agent
PR #106 merge resolution (this report's author)

Each instance manifested the same pattern: bun install reports success, runtime fails with Cannot find module 'X', npm install workaround resolves.
Workaround
Use npm install (NOT bun install) for OneDrive-mounted worktrees.
Additional context
This affects developers who put their projects under OneDrive for cross-machine sync (which is increasingly common — e.g. Microsoft's recommended Windows 11 setup)

t: Bun.Image should support generating actual ThumbHash placeholders + use a lossy format for data URLs
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?

Using a lossless format like PNG makes no sense for low-quality placeholders. The data URL placeholder should likely use JPEG or WebP (I'm not certain which will be smaller at such low qualities).

t: Bun.Image strips ICC profile
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.14-canary.1+d484fd6e2
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.19.13-300.fc44.x86_64 x86_64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Process the below butterfly-xyb.jpg through Bun.Image. This is encoded with Jpegli which can use an ICC profile to effectively encode the image in the XYB colorspace rather than YCbCr, which is more efficient. But this means that if the correct ICC profile is not used, the image's colors will appear completely wrong since you are essentially reinterpreting the color values with a different meaning:
Bun.file("butterfly-xyb.jpg").image().png().write("butterfly-xyb.png")

What is the expected behavior?
Bun should output a file that looks the same as the input JPEG. There should probably be an API to choose whether to preserve the input's color profile, or convert into another one. It's never correct to strip the color profile without changing the input's color values.
What do you see instead?
Bun removes the color profile resulting in incorrect colors when the output is interpreted as sRGB:

Additional information
I used an XYB image since it makes the issue more obvious, but this issue also applies to images using wide gamut colorspaces like P3 (which many smartphones use) or Adobe RGB (popular on professional cameras). In those cases, Bun's behavior will make the output image look less saturated than it should be.

What steps can reproduce the bug?
When process.stdin has a data listener attached AND stdin is actively producing data, registered signal handlers for SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 are never invoked. Node.js delivers the same signals correctly under identical conditions.
Repro script (/tmp/multi-sig.js):
process.on('SIGTERM', () => { console.error('[multi] SIGTERM'); process.exit(0); });
process.on('SIGINT',  () => { console.error('[multi] SIGINT');  process.exit(0); });

process.on('SIGUSR2', () => { console.error('[multi] SIGUSR2'); process.exit(0); });

Reproduce:
bun run /tmp/multi-sig.js < /dev/zero &
PID=$!
sleep 0.3
kill -TERM $PID    # process survives
kill -INT  $PID    # process survives
kill -USR1 $PID    # process survives
kill -KILL $PID    # only this terminates it
Compare with Node:
node /tmp/multi-sig.js < /dev/zero &
PID=$!
sleep 0.3
kill -TERM $PID    # prints "[multi] SIGTERM" and exits 0 immediately

t: Resolver: wildcard `exports` pattern fails when matched substring starts with `@`
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (also reproduces on macOS arm64 and Windows per local testing)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
A package's wildcard exports pattern "./*": "./dist/packages/*" fails to resolve subpaths whose matched substring starts with @. Plain subpaths work; @-prefixed subpaths do not, even though the underlying file exists on disk.
Minimal 4-file reproducer:
mkdir -p test/node_modules/test-pkg/dist/packages/@scope/sub
mkdir -p test/node_modules/test-pkg/dist/packages/plain
cd test
cat > node_modules/test-pkg/package.json <<EOJ
{
  "name": "test-pkg",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "exports": { "./*": "./dist/packages/*" }
}
EOJ
echo "export default 'plain';" > node_modules/test-pkg/dist/packages/plain/index.js
echo "export default 'scoped';" > node_modules/test-pkg/dist/packages/@scope/sub/index.js
echo '{"name":"host"}' > package.json

bun --print 'await Bun.resolve("test-pkg/plain/index.js", process.cwd())'
# /tmp/test/node_modules/test-pkg/dist/packages/plain/index.js  ← OK

bun --print 'await Bun.resolve("test-pkg/@scope/sub/index.js", process.cwd())'
# error: Cannot find module 'test-pkg/@scope/sub/index.js' from '/tmp/test'
What is the expected behavior?
Per the Node.js subpath patterns spec, the wildcard * matches any string and is substituted literally into the target. The @ character has no special meaning inside a wildcard match — it's just a string substitution.
Node.js v22.14 resolves both paths correctly:
$ node -e "console.log(require.resolve('test-pkg/@scope/sub/index.js'))"
/tmp/test/node_modules/test-pkg/dist/packages/@scope/sub/index.js

Bun should match this behaviour.
What do you see instead?
Bun's resolver returns "Cannot find module" for any subpath whose matched substring contains a leading @, even when the resolved file exists on disk. The plain test-pkg/plain/index.js case (no @ in the wildcard match) resolves correctly, confirming the wildcard pattern itself works — it's specifically the @-prefix in the substituted substring that trips the resolver.
Real-world impact
This affects any package that ships submodules under @-prefixed paths via a wildcard exports map. The motivating case for me is ember-source@6.12 (the LTS, released 2026-05-01), whose package.json has:
"exports": { "./*": "./dist/packages/*" }
…with internal subpackages laid out at dist/packages/@ember/renderer/, dist/packages/@ember/template-compiler/, dist/packages/@glimmer/runtime/, dist/packages/@simpl

t: `Bun.file(<fd>).stream()` doesn't drain externally-allocated pipe fds
Windows global install panics when BUN_INSTALL_BIN and global package store are on different drives
b:
How can we reproduce the crash?
On Windows, put the global bin directory on a different real drive from the global package store, then install a package with a bin entry. The package store can be the default under %USERPROFILE%, or an explicit BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR on another drive.
Minimal shape:
$env:BUN_INSTALL_BIN = "E:\Packages\bun\bin"
$env:BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR = "E:\Packages\bun\cache"
Remove-Item Env:BUN_INSTALL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item Env:BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

bun install -g github:b-nnett/codex-plusplus#0.1.4
This uses a real E:/C: split. A subst-mapped drive is not a reliable repro because Bun may canonicalize the mapping enough for the shim target to remain relative.
Observed locally:
Bun v1.3.13 (bf2e2cec) Windows x64
Args: "C:\Users\Claire\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\bun.exe" "install" "-g" "github:b-nnett/codex-plusplus#0.1.4"
Features: binlinks(2) extracted_packages hoisted_bun_install

panic(main thread): Internal assertion failure at install\bin.zig:738:83

This is the same assertion family as #23414 and #29005, but this repro is specifically the supported/intentional split-storage case where the global bin directory is on one drive and the package store is on another.
The local crash above has BUN_INSTALL_BIN and BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR on E: while the default global package store remains under %USERPROFILE% on C:. The same cross-volume assumption also affects the common inverse layout where package storage/caches are intentionally placed on a non-system Dev Drive while launchers or tool shims stay in a separate bin directory on PATH. Microsoft documents Dev Drive as intended for "Source code repositories and project files", "Package caches", and "Build output and intermediate files", and its Dev Drive setup guide gives package-cache examples for npm, NuGet global packages, vcpkg, pip, Cargo, Maven, and Gradle on a Dev Drive. The Windows Developer Blog likewise recommends placing working directories, repositories, and package caches on a Dev Drive.
References:
