t: `bun run` fails with `CouldntReadCurrentDirectory` when ancestor directories are not readable
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.18.18-1-lts x86_64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
bun run fatally errors when it cannot openat ancestor directories (/, /home/), even though getcwd() succeeds. This makes bun unusable in sandboxed environments that restrict filesystem access to the working directory.
Run bun inside any Landlock sandbox that grants full access to the CWD but not to ancestor directories like / or /home/. No project files needed.
I'm using https://github.com/always-further/nono v0.19
# Using nono as an example, but any Landlock sandbox would trigger this
nono run --allow-cwd --allow path/to/bun -- bun eval "console.log('hello')"
What is the expected behavior?
bun eval should print hello. getcwd() succeeds — bun knows the working directory path. It should not need to open ancestor directories to function.
What do you see instead?
error loading current directory
error: An internal error occurred (CouldntReadCurrentDirectory)

Additional information
Root cause (strace)
getcwd("/home/benjabobs/dev/minimal-repro-dir", 4096) = 34          # succeeds
openat(AT_FDCWD, "bunfig.toml", O_RDONLY) = -1 ENOENT           # fine
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES  # fatal
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/home/", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES  # fatal
error loading current directory

bun walks up the directory tree after getcwd() already returned the path. When any ancestor openat fails, bun treats it as a fatal error rather than gracefully continuing.
Why this is an issue
Sandboxed execution is increasingly common (Landlock, containers, CI). Tools like Node.js and tsc work fine in these environments because they don't require openat on ancestor directories. bun's ancestor traversal — likely for config file discovery — should be best-effort, not fatal. If getcwd() succeeds, bun has the information it needs.
Suggested fix
Make the ancestor directory walk non-fatal. If openat on a parent directory fails with EACCES, skip it and continue rather than aborting. Config file discovery (e.g. bunfig.toml) in parent directories can gracefully degrade when access is denied.

t: Programmatic CPU profiler API
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun supports CPU profiling via --cpu-prof flag, which generates a CPU profile to help visualize things happening behind the scene
bun --cpu-prof script.js
It's nice, but it's a bit hard to profile long running process, eg. web server, terminal process or anything that lives longer than a simple script or to scope down to only between a function
Bun also supports a --heap-prof but also supports an API to generate a heap snapshot programmatically via v8.writeHeapSnapshot()
import { writeHeapSnapshot } from 'v8'

writeHeapSnapshot("my-application.heapsnapshot")
This allows us to programmatically detect memory leak as mentioned in "Debugging Memory Leaks"
It would be great if we could somehow measure CPU usage programmatically as well
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I don't know how hard or is it even possible to do the same
Currently, there is a v8-profiler-next that allows us to measure CPU usage between start and end points programmatically
import profiler from 'v8-profiler-next'

profiler.startProfiling('myFunc', true)
yourFunction()
const profile = profiler.stopProfiling('myFunc')
profile.export((err, result) => {
  fs.writeFileSync('myFunc.cpuprofile', result)
  profile.delete()
})
However, this package doesn't work with Bun
Alternatively, it would be great if we Bun does support something similar (although the API doesn't have to be similar to v8-profiler-next)
What alternatives have you considered?
Since v8-profiler-next doesn't work, I'm not sure either

Feature request: streaming / temp-file-backed multipart parsing for Bun.serve uploads
b:
What is the problem?
For server-side multipart/form-data uploads in Bun.serve, the currently documented APIs appear to be eager materializers:

Request.formData()
Bun.readableStreamToFormData(...)

That is useful for small forms, but it leaves a gap for large file uploads. If an app wants to handle large uploads without large RSS spikes, it currently has to parse the multipart stream manually and spool file parts to disk itself.
In PocketBun, we just had to add a custom request-scoped multipart parser for this reason. The main goal was to avoid materializing uploaded files as in-memory blobs and instead expose temp-file-backed uploaded parts.
Why this matters
Large multipart uploads are a common server-side use case. Today there does not seem to be a first-class Bun API for:

iterating multipart parts incrementally
streaming file parts directly from the request body
spooling uploaded files to temp files
setting per-part and per-request multipart limits

Without that, frameworks and apps end up reimplementing multipart parsing themselves, which is:

easy to get wrong
duplicated across the ecosystem
likely less efficient than a native implementation

What I’m requesting
A native Bun API for streaming multipart parsing on the server side.
Any of these shapes would solve the problem:
Option A: async multipart iterator on Request
for await (const part of request.multipart()) {
  part.name;
  part.filename;
  part.contentType;
  part.headers;
  part.body; // ReadableStream<Uint8Array>
}
Option B: parser helper over a ReadableStream
const parts = Bun.readableStreamToMultipartParts(request.body!, boundary, options);
for await (const part of parts) {
  // ...
}
Option C: enhanced formData() with storage options
const form = await request.formData({
  fileStorage: "tempfile", // or "memory"
  maxMemoryFileSize: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
  tempDir: "/tmp",
  limits: {
    maxParts: 1000,
    maxFileSize: ...,
    maxFieldSize: ...,
    maxHeaderBytes: ...,
  },
});
Important capabilities
Whatever API shape Bun prefers, these capabilities would be especially useful:

stream each part incrementally
avoid buffering entire uploaded files in memory
optionally spool file parts to temp files
expose name, filename, content-type, and raw headers
support limits like:

max parts
max file size
max non-file field size
max header bytes


clean up temp files automatically or provide an explicit cleanup hook

bun install hangs indefinitely on Linux after successfully downloading all packages. The hang occurs in the post-install phase (confirmed via --verbose) and appears to be the OSV security scanner hitting the OS ARG_MAX limit.

Environment

OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest)
bun versions tested: 1.3.5, 1.3.10 — all hang
macOS (ARM64): works fine with the same lockfile and packages
Packages: ~1,243 packages in a monorepo

Steps to Reproduce

Create a monorepo with ~1,200+ packages using bun.lock (text lockfile)
Run on a Linux x64 machine with a cold cache:
bun install --frozen-lockfile --verbose


Observe packages downloading normally for ~6 minutes
Observe complete silence for 14+ minutes before the process is killed

Skip installing fsevents - os mismatch   ← last line at T+6min
[14+ minutes of silence]

Without --verbose, there is zero output between bun install vX.X.X and the eventual kill — not even with --verbose (per original report in #23607).
What We Tried
All of the following hang on Linux, all complete successfully on macOS:



Command
Result

❌ hangs

❌ hangs

Actual Behavior

t: Bun.zstdDecompress lacks decompressed size limit
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun.zstdDecompress currently appears to decompress the entire input without allowing callers to specify a maximum decompressed size. When handling untrusted input, this makes applications vulnerable to compression bombs.
This is both a security concern and an API limitation, since most decompression APIs provide a way to bound the output size.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A max output size parameter.
What alternatives have you considered?
Using node:zlib or DecompressionStream and checking its size as it gets streamed and abort after reaching a certain threshold, but those APIs are slower than Bun.zstdDecompress.

bun add -d git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#<hash>

t: jemalloc reserves ~485GB VSZ per process on aarch64 macOS (Apple Silicon, 16KB pages)
b:
Environment

Bun version: 1.3.10
OS: macOS 15.7.4 (24G517)
Hardware: Apple M3 Pro, 36GB RAM, aarch64
Page size: 16KB (Apple Silicon)

Description
Each bun process reserves approximately 485GB of virtual address space at startup on Apple Silicon macOS, before executing any user code. This is visible immediately via ps -o vsz.
  PID    RSS      VSZ COMMAND
63053 229936 485365472 bun run (session 1)
63031 248144 485304096 bun run (session 2)

VSZ ~462GB per process. RSS is only ~230MB — the virtual reservation is ~2000x actual physical usage.
Impact
With multiple long-running bun processes, the combined virtual address space exhausts macOS's ability to handle new mmap requests. macOS begins compressing mapped pages aggressively. Once the compressed pool fills:

New allocations fail silently or get shorted
Process behavior becomes unpredictable
Eventually OOM kill or segfault

On this machine with 2 active bun processes: ~930GB combined VSZ against 36GB physical RAM. macOS is compressing ~100GB of virtual mappings at any given time during interactive use. This manifests as a slow death — the machine appears to be holding 200GB+ in compressed RAM while interactive, with allocations progressively failing.
Root cause hypothesis
jemalloc's arena initialization calls mmap(MAP_ANON) to reserve a large contiguous virtual region upfront. On x86_64 Linux with 4KB pages this is less visible. On aarch64 macOS with 16KB pages, the arena reservation is significantly larger in address space terms, and macOS's VM system does not aggressively reclaim unreferenced anonymous mappings the same way Linux does.
This is compounded by any application that mmaps additional files (e.g. git pack files for snapshot/session storage) on top of the baseline reservation.
Reproduction
# Any bun process on Apple Silicon macOS
bun run some-script.ts &
ps -o pid,rss,vsz,command -p $!
# VSZ will show ~485GB regardless of script complexity
Expected behavior
VSZ should reflect actual heap arena needs, not a pre-reserved maximum. On x86_64 Linux bun processes show VSZ in the low GB range for equivalent workloads.
Notes

Upgrading to 1.3.10 appears to reduce but not eliminate the issue
The jemalloc aarch64/16KB page interaction has been noted in prior issues but the VSZ reservation size at startup may not have been specifically reported
Related: applications using bun as a sidecar (e.g. opencode) see this multiplied by the number of concurrent sessions

t: ASan use-after-poison in WebWorker__notifyNeedTermination when terminate() called from message handler
b:
Seen on debian-13 x64-asan in build #39654 running test/js/web/workers/worker.test.ts.
Stack (abbreviated)
==6014==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison on address 0x105c606215a0
READ of size 1 at 0x105c606215a0 thread T0
    #0 atomic.Value(bun.js.web_worker.Status).load  vendor/zig/lib/std/atomic.zig:14
    #1 WebWorker__notifyNeedTermination            src/bun.js/web_worker.zig:571
    #2 jsWorkerPrototypeFunction_terminateBody     src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/JSWorker.cpp:549
    ...
    #16 EventTarget::innerInvokeEventListeners
    #19 Worker::dispatchEvent                       src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/Worker.cpp:323
    #20 jsFunctionPostMessage::$_0::operator()      src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/Worker.cpp:669  <-- queued task lambda
    #23 EventLoopTask::performTask

Address 0x105c606215a0 is a wild pointer inside of access range of size 0x000000000001.
Shadow byte: f7 (Poisoned by user)

Analysis
Shadow byte f7 is the mimalloc poison marker for freed allocations.
The sequence:

Worker thread calls postMessage → schedules an EventLoopTask on the parent thread via a lambda at Worker.cpp:669 that captures Worker*
Worker exits and the Zig WebWorker struct is freed before the parent processes the queued task
Parent runs the task → dispatches message event → JS event listener calls worker.terminate()
terminate() → WebWorker__notifyNeedTermination → this.status.load(.acquire) on freed memory at web_worker.zig:571

The Worker C++ wrapper (or the task lambda) needs to keep the underlying WebWorker alive while message-dispatch tasks are pending on the parent event loop.
There are existing TODOs from @190n at web_worker.zig:581,584 suggesting this area is already being reworked.

Segfault when native code repeatedly invokes `JSCallback({ threadsafe: true })`
b:
What happens
Hi, I stumbled upon an issue while adding an Electrobun (bun:ffi) backend to my lib, where event streams can fire repeatedly into the same JSCallback. A native library repeatedly calling a Bun JSCallback({ threadsafe: true }) can segfault Bun.
I reduced this to a very small repro:

one JS callback
passed directly to native, which repeatedly invokes the callback from a worker thread
callback body only increments a counter

Minimal repro shape
I've published the repro here:
https://github.com/hsjoberg/bun-ffi-crash
It creates a small Rust lib that we then load in via bun:ffi.
JS side:

create a JSCallback with { threadsafe: true } whose body only increments a counter
pass the callback pointer to native

Native side:

start a worker thread
repeatedly invoke that callback in a loop

The repro is intentionally hammering the FFI path, but I originally hit this in my library with only a small number of stream events.
Setting the worker count to 2+ makes the crash reproduce consistently for me. With 1 worker thread, it is still reproducible, but more intermittent.
To run the reproducer:
bun install
bun run repro
Stack traces
I have confirmed this crash on Windows x64, macOS arm64, and Linux x64 (via WSL2). The exact crash site varies, but on macOS and Linux the stack traces consistently pass through JSFFIFunction.cpp in Bun’s threadsafe FFI callback path.

t: webkit: re-add -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON to Windows prebuilts
b:
Context
bmalloc/libpas causes crashes on Windows under memory pressure during GC. See #28097, #26985, #26982.
The fix requires a coordinated change between oven-sh/WebKit and oven-sh/bun:
Upstream (oven-sh/WebKit)
Re-add -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON to the cmake invocation in windows-release.ps1:
 cmake -S . -B $WebKitBuild `
     -DPORT="JSCOnly" `
     -DENABLE_STATIC_JSC=ON `
+    -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON `
     ...
This was previously added in WebKit PR #97 (July 2025) but was removed in a later update. The current prebuilt WebKit for Windows (commit 00e825523d) does not have this flag.
Downstream (oven-sh/bun) — after prebuilts are rebuilt

Remove bmalloc.lib from Windows link targets in cmake/targets/BuildBun.cmake
Exclude bmallocLib(cfg) on Windows in scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts (TODO comments already added in #28098)
Add CI regression guard (assertNoBmallocOnWindows)

Background

WebKit PR #97: Originally added -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON for Windows
Bun PR #20931: Removed bmalloc.lib from link targets (worked with the WebKit fix)
Bun PR #26381: WebKit update — new version dropped the flag, re-enabling bmalloc in prebuilts

t: pipeReadableStreamToBlob assertion failure on Windows when readStreamIntoSink completes synchronously

t: Bun.secrets: secrets are accessible by any bun script without password prompt
b:
What is the type of issue?
Documentation is confusing
What is the issue?
When one bun script stores a secret via Bun.secrets.set(), any other bun
script can read it silently — no Keychain password prompt, no Touch ID, no user
confirmation.
With compiled binaries (bun build --compile), macOS Keychain correctly
prompts for a password. But with scripts, all access goes through the same
bun binary, so Keychain treats them as the same application.
Reproduction
https://github.com/KarKarbI4/bun-secrets-process-isolation-test
git clone https://github.com/KarKarbI4/bun-secrets-process-isolation-test
cd bun-secrets-process-isolation-test
./run-tests.sh

Three independent scripts: writer.ts stores a secret, reader.ts reads it,
cleanup.ts deletes it. The test also compiles each into a standalone binary and
 runs again.

Results

┌────────┬────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
│        │  Script → Script   │         Binary → Binary          │
├────────┼────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Read   │ no password prompt │ password prompt                  │
├────────┼────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Delete │ no password prompt │ blocked (errSecInvalidOwnerEdit) │
└────────┴────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
Impact
A malicious or compromised dependency running via bun can silently read all
secrets stored by any other bun script — API tokens, database credentials, etc.
No password prompt, no user confirmation.
The documentation states "Process Isolation: Credentials are isolated per user
account" without clarifying that there is no isolation between bun scripts.
Suggestion

Update docs to clarify that any bun script under the same user can read
secrets created by any other bun script without a password prompt
Consider recommending bun build --compile for applications that need real
secret isolation
Investigate whether per-application ACLs (e.g. SecAccessCreate on macOS)
could be applied for interpreted scripts

Environment

Bun: 1.2.22
OS: macOS 15.5 (Darwin 24.6.0)
Arch: arm64

Where did you find it?
https://bun.com/docs/runtime/secrets

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

t: Support bun:ffi on Windows ARM64
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Windows ARM64 support landed in #26215, but bun:ffi is still completely disabled on that target.
Today we explicitly gate it off in:

cmake/Options.cmake (DEFAULT_ENABLE_TINYCC OFF on WIN32 && aarch64)
src/bun.js/api/ffi.zig (cc(), callback(), dlopen(), linkSymbols() all throw when TinyCC is disabled)
test/js/bun/ffi/* (Windows ARM64 is treated as FFI-unavailable)

So native Windows ARM64 Bun exists, but any FFI-backed app/library still fails there.
This seems like the missing follow-up to #9824 / #26215.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Enable bun:ffi on native Windows ARM64.
Concretely, that likely means:

vendor/bump TinyCC to a revision that includes the Windows ARM64 work
get Bun’s FFI path green on real Windows ARM64
unskip/enable the FFI tests on Windows ARM64
flip ENABLE_TINYCC on for that target once stable

Relevant detail: Bun is still pinned to an older TinyCC revision in cmake/targets/BuildTinyCC.cmake, while the Windows ARM64 TinyCC work appears to have landed later upstream.
If the plan is not full TinyCC-backed support, it would still be useful to track whether dlopen() / fixed-symbol calls can be split from the TinyCC dependency.
What alternatives have you considered?

x64/baseline Bun under emulation: works around it, but not a real fix
app-level fallbacks: useful UX-wise, but doesn’t address the platform gap

t: fs.watch() throws unhandled EACCES when a file inside watched directory is not readable
b:
Bun version: 1.3.10 (Linux x64)
Platform: Ubuntu Linux x86_64
Describe the bug
When using fs.watch() on a directory that contains files not readable by the current user, Bun throws an unhandled EACCES error and crashes instead of passing the error to the callback or ignoring it.
Node.js handles the same scenario correctly — it uses inotify purely for change notification and does not attempt to open files inside the watched directory.
Steps to reproduce
# Create a directory with a file readable only by root
mkdir /tmp/test-watch
echo "secret" > /tmp/test-watch/private.txt
chmod 600 /tmp/test-watch/private.txt

# Run as non-root user
bun watch-dir.js /tmp/test-watch
# then trigger any change in the directory
// watch-dir.js
import { watch } from "fs";
watch("/tmp/test-watch", { persistent: true }, (eventType, filename) => {
  console.log(eventType, filename);
});
Expected behavior
fs.watch() should work identically to Node.js: emit events with (eventType, filename) without attempting to open files inside the directory.
Actual behavior
error: EACCES: permission denied, open '/tmp/test-watch/private.txt'
      at emitError (node:events:51:13)
      at #onEvent (node:fs:48:16)

Process crashes.
strace evidence
inotify_add_watch succeeds normally. The crash happens later in #onEvent when a file change is detected — Bun attempts to open() the changed file, which Node.js does not do.
Workaround
Using Node.js instead of Bun for this script works without issues.

t: Support custom dictionaries in "node:zlib" for (RFC 9842 CDT)
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
CDT (Compression Dictionary Transport, spec, datatracker) is a new HTTP protocol
(RFC draft) that allows browsers and servers to compress responses
using a shared pre-negotiated dictionary, achieving dramatically
better compression ratios for repeated content (APIs, HTML pages, etc).
CDT uses two new Content-Encoding values:

dcz dictionary-compressed Zstandard
dcb dictionary-compressed Brotli

To implement a CDT server in Bun today, you need to call
ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary / ZSTD_createCDict from libzstd,
but this is not exposed through node:zlib (bun).
What Node.js already supports
Node.js v22.19+ / v24.6+ added dictionary support to node:zlib (doc):
import { createZstdCompress, constants } from 'node:zlib'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'

const dict = readFileSync('my.dict')

const compress = createZstdCompress({
  params: {
    [constants.ZSTD_c_dict]: dict,
  }
})
What Bun currently does
Bun exposes createZstdCompress / createZstdDecompress and the
ZstdCompress / ZstdDecompress classes, but the params option
does not support ZSTD_c_dict / ZSTD_d_dict. Passing a dictionary
buffer is silently ignored.
Spec

RFC 9842 (Standards Track): https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9842
IETF Datatracker: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpbis-compression-dictionary/

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Proposed solution
In src/node_zlib.zig, expose ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary and
ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary when a dictionary buffer is provided
in the options params, matching the Node.js API surface.
What alternatives have you considered?
No response

Any non-ASCII UTF-8 character: Norwegian (ø, æ, å), Polish (ż, ó, ł, ś, ć, ź, ń), CJK (日本語, 中文, 한국어), French accents (é, è, ê), etc.
Root cause
Bun builds libarchive with ENABLE_ICONV=OFF (see cmake/targets/BuildLibArchive.cmake). The *Utf8 pathname functions (archive_entry_set_pathname_utf8 / archive_entry_pathname_utf8) require iconv for charset conversion. Without iconv:

Non-ASCII bytes are silently dropped from the pathname
archive_write_header returns an error due to the corrupted/empty path

The same issue affects reading: pathnameUtf8() also fails to return non-ASCII characters from archives that do contain them.
Fix
PR #27484:

Sets hdrcharset=BINARY to bypass charset conversion (bytes stored as-is, which is correct since filenames from JS are already valid UTF-8)
Switches to raw setPathname / pathname variants that pass bytes through without iconv conversion
Adds archive.errorString() to all tarball creation error handlers for better diagnostics

bun:sqlite: segfault after SQLiteError on missing virtual table module (vec0)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10 (30e609e)
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 (macOS 15.7.4, Apple M4 Pro)
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install a package that uses sqlite-vec (which registers a vec0 virtual table module via loadExtension)
Run under Bun where bun:sqlite is used instead of better-sqlite3
Since bun:sqlite does not support loadExtension(), the vec0 module is never registered
When code calls db.prepare() with a query referencing vec0, Bun throws SQLiteError: no such module: vec0 — correct behavior
Bun then segfaults during error handling/cleanup

Concrete reproduction with QMD (markdown search engine using sqlite-vec):
bun install -g @tobilu/qmd
qmd query "test" --json -n 1
What is the expected behavior?
The SQLiteError should propagate as a normal JavaScript exception. The process should exit cleanly (or the error should be catchable).
What do you see instead?
SQLiteError: no such module: vec0
      at prepare (bun:sqlite:345:37)
      at searchVec (/Users/gerhard/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/store.js:2047:27)
      ...

panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0xCC
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.

Full crash report: https://bun.report/1.3.10/Ma130e609egjEugggC____ut27nB+gy8nB+z0+nBu1gsCulr2Fuiz1kBu0miFuv0iFutqiF279oF2hrB+giB__A2A4M
Additional information

The SQLiteError is thrown correctly — the bug is that Bun segfaults after throwing it, rather than letting it propagate normally
This is different from #5756 (fixed by PR #5773), which was about calling .loadExtension() directly. Here the crash happens on prepare() when referencing a missing module
bun:sqlite does not support loadExtension() on macOS (Apple's system SQLite has extension loading disabled), so any package relying on native SQLite extensions (sqlite-vec, sqlite-regex, etc.) will hit this path when run under Bun
Bun 1.3.10 on macOS Silicon — not tested on other platforms

Workaround
Run through Node.js instead of Bun. The native addons compiled by Bun are ABI-compatible with Node.js, and better-sqlite3 supports loadExtension() correctly.

t: HTML imports: `Cache-Control` header not set on content-hashed assets despite `development: false`
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11-canary.80+3832c8570
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
index.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head><link rel="stylesheet" href="./style.css" /></head>
<body><script type="module" src="./app.ts"></script></body>
</html>
style.css
body { background: red; }
app.ts
console.log("hello")
server.ts
import index from "./index.html"

const server = Bun.serve({
  development: false,
  port: 4567,
  routes: { "/": index },
})

console.log(`Listening on ${server.url}`)
Then run with any of the three modes:
# Runtime bundling
bun server.ts

# Compiled binary
bun build --compile server.ts --outfile app && ./app

# Ahead-of-time build
bun build server.ts --outdir dist --target bun && cd dist && bun server.js
Check asset headers:
curl -sI http://localhost:4567/chunk-58p6fhtw.css
What is the expected behavior?
Content-hashed assets (/chunk-[hash].css, /chunk-[hash].js) should be served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable when development: false. The docs state that development: false will "Enable Cache-Control headers and ETag headers".
What do you see instead?
No Cache-Control header in any mode. Only ETag and Content-Type are set:
=== Runtime bundling (development: false) ===
CSS /chunk-58p6fhtw.css:
Content-Type: text/css;charset=utf-8
ETag: 5cba11efa65608a5

=== Compiled binary (bun build --compile) ===
CSS /chunk-58p6fhtw.css:
Content-Type: text/css;charset=utf-8
ETag: 5cba11efa65608a5

=== Ahead-of-time build (bun build --target=bun) ===
CSS /chunk-58p6fhtw.css:
Content-Type: text/css;charset=utf-8
ETag: 5cba11efa65608a5

Additional information
Related: #19198, #25513
Source analysis:


Runtime bundling path — HTMLBundle.zig:382 has code to append Cache-Control when !isDevelopment() and output_kind == .chunk, but it never reaches responses.


Compiled binary / AOT path — HTMLImportManifest.zig:writeEntryItem only writes etag and content-type into the manifest JSON. At serve time, server.zig:bundledHTMLManifestItemFromJS reads headers from this manifest, so Cache-Control is never set.


Without Cache-Control, every visitor re-validates every asset on every page load. Since filenames contain content hashes, these assets are immutable and should be cached indefinitely.

b:
Summary
When using bun build --compile --bytecode --format esm, the compiled binary fails at runtime with Cannot find module errors. The bundler appears to correctly bundle all modules into a single file, but the bytecode compilation step for ESM format produces a binary that retains unresolved internal module references.
Exact reproduction steps
mkdir repro && cd repro

# Create package.json
cat > package.json << 'EOF'
{
  "name": "repro",
  "type": "module",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "diff": "^8.0.3"
  }
}
EOF

# Create index.ts
cat > index.ts << 'EOF'
import { createTwoFilesPatch } from 'diff';
const msg = createTwoFilesPatch('a.ts', 'b.ts', 'a', 'b');
console.log(msg);
EOF

# Install dependencies
bun install

# Build and run (THIS FAILS)
bun build --compile --bytecode --format esm --outfile=out index.ts
./out
Expected behavior
The compiled binary runs and outputs a unified diff patch.
Actual behavior
error: Cannot find module './diff/base.js' from '/$bunfs/root/out'

Bun v1.3.10 (Linux arm64)

Systematic flag testing



Flags
Result




--compile --bytecode --format esm --minify
FAIL — Cannot find module './diff/base.js'


--compile --bytecode --format esm
FAIL — Cannot find module './diff/base.js'


--compile --bytecode --minify (no --format esm)
PASS


--compile --bytecode (no --format esm, no --minify)
PASS


--compile --format esm --minify (no --bytecode)
PASS


--compile --format esm (no --bytecode, no --minify)
PASS



Conclusion: The bug requires both --bytecode AND --format esm together. --minify is NOT required.
Workaround
Using a namespace import instead of a named import avoids the issue:

Removing --bytecode or removing --format esm both independently fix the issue.

In monorepos, bun run --filter '*' test runs scripts in all packages, even when only a few files changed. This wastes CI time and resources.
Today, teams must build custom detect-affected scripts (parsing package.json workspaces, running git diff, building a reverse dependency graph, doing BFS) to achieve what Nx provides natively with nx affected.
Bun already has the workspace dependency graph internally (filter_run.zig). The missing piece is connecting it to git changes.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A --affected flag for bun run that only runs scripts in packages affected by git changes:
# Run tests only in packages affected since main
bun run --affected test

# Custom base (CI: last successful SHA)
bun run --affected --base=abc123 test

# Custom base + head (PR diff)
bun run --affected --base=main --head=feature-branch test

# Include uncommitted/untracked changes (default when no --base)
bun run --affected --uncommitted test

# Combine with --concurrency (#27855)
bun run --affected --concurrency 4 typecheck

# Just list affected packages (no execution)
bun run --affected --list
Algorithm (4 phases)


Determine changed files — git diff --name-only between --base (default: main) and --head (default: HEAD + uncommitted + untracked). Uses git merge-base to handle diverged branches correctly.


Map files → packages — Walk up directory tree from each changed file to find the owning workspace package (longest prefix match on package roots). Root-level changes (bun.lock, tsconfig.json) → all packages affected.


Build reverse dependency graph — Invert the workspace dependency graph (already available in Bun internals). If A depends on B, reversed: B → A.


Traverse transitively — DFS/BFS from each directly-changed package on the reversed graph → collect all transitively affected packages.


Behavior



Scenario
Result




src/packages/auth/entity.ts changed
auth + all packages depending on auth


bun.lock changed
All packages (conservative)


Root tsconfig.json changed
All packages


No changes
No packages, exit 0


--base SHA not in history
Error with clear message



Flags



Flag
Default
Description




--affected
—
Enable affected detection


--base
main
Base ref for git diff


--head
HEAD
Head ref for git diff


--uncommitted
true (no --base)
Include uncommitted changes


--untracked
true (no --base)
Include untracked files


--list
false
Print affected package names, don't run

t: Nested workspace package patchedDependencies break root install
b:
This looks like a separate patchedDependencies bug from the already-filed local path / workspace patch issues.
A package can be installed successfully as its own Bun root when it has top-level patchedDependencies, and a consuming workspace root can also install successfully when only the root carries the patch metadata.
But the same consuming workspace root fails as soon as the nested workspace package also carries its own top-level patchedDependencies:
error: Couldn't find patch file: 'patches/effect-distributed-lock@0.0.11.patch'
The practical problem is that the same package needs contradictory static manifest shapes:

when it is the install root, it needs top-level patchedDependencies
when it is a nested workspace member under another Bun root, that same field breaks the install

Reproduction
https://github.com/schickling-repros/2026-03-bun-nested-workspace-patches
cd fail/packages/lib
bun install --linker isolated

cd ../../pass/packages/app
bun install --linker isolated

cd ../../fail/packages/app
bun install --linker isolated
Expected
Bun should honor the install root's patch metadata and ignore nested workspace package patchedDependencies, or otherwise support this shape consistently.
Actual
The nested workspace package's top-level patchedDependencies is read and Bun fails to find the nested package-local patch path while installing the app root.
Versions

t: Add --concurrency flag for `bun run --filter`
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
When running scripts across many workspace packages with bun run --filter '*' <script>, all matching packages start simultaneously with no way to limit parallelism.
In large monorepos (60+ packages), this causes OOM kills for memory-intensive scripts like tsc --noEmit (~500MB each). Example: 68 packages × 500MB = ~34GB peak RAM.
Currently the only workaround is a custom batching script wrapping bun run --filter.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add a --concurrency <N> flag to bun run that limits how many scripts run in parallel when used with --filter:
# Run typecheck across all workspaces, max 4 at a time
bun run --filter '*' --concurrency 4 typecheck

# Sequential execution
bun run --filter '*' --concurrency 1 build

# Works with --parallel mode too
bun run --parallel --filter '*' --concurrency 2 build
Behavior:

--concurrency 0 or non-numeric → error with clear message
Without --concurrency → current behavior (unlimited, all in parallel)
Respects existing dependency ordering from filter_run.zig

Implementation: PR #27855
What alternatives have you considered?

External batching script — works but loses dependency graph awareness and requires per-project maintenance
OS-level ulimit — too coarse, affects all processes
GNU parallel / xargs -P — loses bun's workspace resolution and dependency ordering

t: process.env is empty (0 keys) when bun runs inside macOS Seatbelt sandbox
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.6.0 (macOS Sequoia, arm64)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Run bun inside a macOS Seatbelt sandbox (e.g., using nono v0.9.0):
# Install nono
brew tap always-further/nono && brew install nono

# Run bun inside sandbox — process.env is completely empty
nono run --allow-cwd -- bun -e "console.log('keys:', Object.keys(process.env).length)"
# Output: keys: 0

# Compare with python3 in the exact same sandbox — sees 44+ env vars
nono run --allow-cwd -- python3 -c "import os; print('keys:', len(os.environ))"
# Output: keys: 44

# Compare with printenv — sees HOME and other vars
nono run --allow-cwd -- printenv HOME
# Output: /Users/<username>
nono uses macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) for kernel-level sandboxing. The sandbox does NOT strip environment variables — other runtimes (Python, printenv, bash) all see the full environment.
What is the expected behavior?
process.env should contain the same environment variables that the parent process provides. Python, Node.js, and C programs all see the full environment inside the same Seatbelt sandbox.
What do you see instead?
process.env is completely empty — Object.keys(process.env).length === 0.
Impact on spawnSync
Because process.env is empty, spawnSync cannot resolve executables via PATH:
nono run --allow-cwd -- bun -e "
  // Even after setting process.env.PATH programmatically:
  process.env.PATH = '/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin';
  
  const { spawnSync } = require('bun');
  const r = spawnSync(['ls']); // ENOENT — 'ls' not found
  console.log(r.exitCode); // null
"
Setting process.env.PATH in JavaScript does NOT fix spawnSync — it appears bun's spawn uses the C-level environ (which is empty) rather than the JavaScript-level process.env.
Workaround
The only working workaround is passing env explicitly to every spawn call:
const env = { HOME: "/Users/me", PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin" };
spawnSync(["ls"], { env }); // Works
spawnSync(["ls"]);          // ENOENT
Additional context

This affects any tool that runs bun inside a macOS sandbox (nono, sandbox-exec, App Sandbox)
Related: #15661 (bun exits with code 5 in App Sandbox) and PR #27041
The issue appears to be in how bun reads/initializes the process environment at startup — it may be using a mechanism that Seatbelt intercepts, unlike the standard environ pointer that other runtimes use

      bun/src/install/yarn.zig
    
    
        Lines 237 to 241
      in
      2dc1533
    
  
  
    

        
          
           if (last_slash < dash_idx and url[last_slash + 1] == '@') { 
        

        
          
               return url[second_last_slash + 1 .. dash_idx]; 
        

        
          
           } else { 
        

        
          
               return url[last_slash + 1 .. dash_idx]; 
        

        
          
           } 
        
    
  


In getPackageNameFromResolvedUrl, it walks backward from /-/ counting slashes. For scoped packages the URL is:
https://registry.yarnpkg.com/@codingame/monaco-editor-treemended/-/...
                            ^          ^last_slash              ^dash_idx
                            |
                            second_last_slash

The check url[last_slash + 1] == '@' is false (it's 'm'), so it returns monaco-editor-treemended instead of @codingame/monaco-editor-treemended. The @ is after second_last_slash, not last_slash.
Fix: change the condition to url[second_last_slash + 1] == '@'.
Version
bun 1.3.10

b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10+30e609e08
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Put bun into a known location and create a minimal package:
mkdir stomp && cd stomp
wget https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.10/bun-darwin-aarch64.zip
unzip bun-darwin-aarch64.zip
echo '{"scripts": {"cowsay": "cowsay"}}' > package.json
./bun-darwin-aarch64/bun add cowsay  

Now run the script. It creates a dir in /private/tmp:
./bun-darwin-aarch64/bun run cowsay moo

Output:
$ cowsay moo
 _____
< moo >
 -----
        \   ^__^
         \  (oo)\_______
            (__)\       )\/\
                ||----w |
                ||     ||

Created files:
/private/tmp/bun-node-30e609e08/ 
total 0
lrwxr-xr-x 1 misha wheel 51 Mar  3 17:10 bun -> /Users/misha/Downloads/stomp/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun*
lrwxr-xr-x 1 misha wheel 51 Mar  3 17:10 node -> /Users/misha/Downloads/stomp/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun*

Now let's move Bun somewhere else, clean up node_modules and run the script again::
rm -rf node_modules
mv bun-darwin-aarch64 bun-darwin-aarch64-2
./bun-darwin-aarch64-2/bun run cowsay moo 

The output:
$ cowsay moo
env: node: No such file or directory
error: script "cowsay" exited with code 127```

Why? Because the file in /private/tmp hasn't been updated:
/private/tmp/bun-node-30e609e08/
total 0
lrwxr-xr-x 1 misha wheel 51 Mar  3 17:10 bun -> /Users/misha/Downloads/stomp/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun
lrwxr-xr-x 1 misha wheel 51 Mar  3 17:10 node -> /Users/misha/Downloads/stomp/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun

What is the expected behavior?
I expected that the second run cowsay invocation will work.
What do you see instead?
Second invocation failed because it didn't find working node symlink.
Additional information
The problem is that Bun creates a single directory under /private/tmp keyed by the commit ID of Bun. If the interpreter is later moved, or made inaccessible due to a sandbox (that's how I found this issue) the node symlink trick stops working.
Moreover, this path is hardcoded in run_command.zig, so it cannot be overridden. Cleaning up this directory every time Bun is run is not advisable, as it creates TOCTOU races.
Any one of the following solutions would help:

Mix into the directory path the path to Bun executable, so that several Bun executables don't stomp on each other's directories.
Make this path overridable using TMPDIR (this is the last temporary dir Bun uses that's not overridable using TMPDIR).

t: Bun SQL treats Postgres URL path as Unix socket path, causing FailedToOpenSocket on any URL with a database name
b:
Root cause found — Bun SQL treats the Postgres URL path component as a Unix domain socket path
After extensive debugging in a Docker devcontainer (Bun 1.3.10, Debian/Linux), the exact root cause has been identified. It is not network configuration, firewall, DNS, or io_uring. It is a bug in how createPostgresConnection handles the path argument when a URL is involved.

How the bug triggers
There are two independent ways to hit this:
Trigger 1: passing url: to new SQL({})
const db = new SQL({
  url: "postgres://user:pass@my-postgres:5432/mydb",
});
When Bun SQL parses this URL, the path component /mydb (the database name, as encoded in standard Postgres URLs) is extracted and passed as the path argument to the native createPostgresConnection. The native code interprets a non-empty path as a Unix domain socket path and ignores hostname/port entirely.
Trigger 2: individual options + DATABASE_URL in the environment
// DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@my-postgres:5432/mydb is set in the environment

const db = new SQL({
  hostname: "my-postgres",
  port: 5432,
  username: "user",
  password: "pass",
  database: "mydb",
});
If DATABASE_URL is set in the environment, Bun SQL reads and parses it even when all connection options are provided explicitly. The same path extraction happens: path = "/mydb".
Only working combination: individual options with no DATABASE_URL in the environment.

Evidence: strace
strace -e trace=socket,connect -f bun script.ts proves the issue conclusively.
With either trigger active, Bun SQL never makes a TCP connection. Instead it creates a Unix socket and attempts to connect to the database-name path:
# Bun.connect() to the same host:port — works fine:
socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK, IPPROTO_IP) = 11
connect(11, {sa_family=AF_INET, sin_port=htons(5432), sin_addr=inet_addr("10.0.0.5")}, 16) = -1 EINPROGRESS

# Bun SQL — Unix socket, wrong path, ECONNREFUSED:
socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK, IPPROTO_IP) = 11
connect(11, {sa_family=AF_UNIX, sun_path="/mydb"}, 110) = -1 ECONNREFUSED
connect(11, {sa_family=AF_UNIX, sun_path="/mydb"}, 110) = -1 ECONNREFUSED
... (retries)

/mydb is the path component of the Postgres URL — the database name. It is not a valid Unix socket path, so every attempt gets ECONNREFUSED, which surfaces as FailedToOpenSocket.

Source location
The bug is visible in the stack trace at internal:sql/postgres:318:
return createPostgresConnection(
  hostname, Number(port),
  usern

t: File Watcher thread eats 100% CPU
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.9+cf6cdbbba
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.8.0-79-generic x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Unable to reproduce it, was just able to do some debugging by attaching GDB to a bun process where the issue has occurred. I see the Bun File Watcher thread is stuck in a hot loop:

Watcher.watchLoop calls INotifyWatcher.watchLoopCycle
INotifyWatcher.watchLoopCycle calls INotifyWatcher.read to get the events
INotifyWatcher.read returns the same 72 events every time, causing it to never progress
Go to 1

What is the expected behavior?
INotify events are cleared after processing so Watcher.watchLoop does not turn into a hot loop.
What do you see instead?
The same INotify events are returned by INotifyWatcher.read every time, causing a 100% CPU loop.
Additional information
By stepping through INotifyWatcher.read I noticed that it is hitting the this.read_ptr != null case every time. So my guess would be that the update of this.read_ptr at the end of INotifyWatcher.watchLoopCycle is the culprit. This bug happens fairly regularly for us, so I'm able to run GDB commands and provide the output here if it aids debugging.

t: My Thoughts on the Current State (Especially Quality Issues) and Future Development of Bun
b:
Based on my experience with Bun recently, I really have a lot to say. Although I am just an ordinary developer, I feel it is necessary to express my views regarding Bun's future development.
I scrolled through Bun's official X account as well as the author's personal X account, and I found that even after being acquired by Anthropic, most of the official marketing is still obsessed with the "performance" narrative, namely, repeatedly emphasizing how much processing time a new feature cuts down compared to competitors or older features.
Then there are the new features.
Regarding the new features, the ones that left a deep impression on me are native support for Markdown and Stage 3 Decorators.
Stage 3 Decorators are certainly a great feature, but as for Markdown, I truly cannot understand: is rendering Markdown really the proper job of a JavaScript Runtime?
From what I knew about Bun previously, it can do almost anything, from a bundler to built-in database support — I could understand those previous features as Bun's "All-in-One" strategy. But I really cannot understand the Markdown support. I feel this is no longer "All-in-One"; this is "All-in-Everything." Doing this will truly cause maintenance costs to skyrocket.
Granted, Bun is now under Anthropic (acquired in December 2025), and Anthropic has a lot of money, but no amount of money can allow a team to add features limitlessly while also guaranteeing quality. That is extremely difficult.
Speaking of quality. I have expressed similar views in the comment sections of some issues(Issue 26660 and Issue 26625) before, but I assumed my views wouldn't get enough attention, which is why I opened this issue.
I think it was around 2023 when I first learned about Bun. At that time, star number and open issues weren't that high. Back then, I thought Bun was pretty good; although there were some minor bugs, it was generally acceptable.
But now, in March 2026, although Bun's star count has reached nearing 100k, the number of open issues has also hit a staggering 4.9k (Now it has dropped to 4.8k again and is now stably maintained at this level long-term) , and this is even with a bot automatically closing duplicate issues.
JavaScriptCore comes from Apple, and getting it to run on Windows indeed requires some adaptation work. I am also aware that in production environments, Bun mostly runs on GNU/Linux (especially backend web apps). From this perspective, it's understandable that Bun focuses more on POSIX-compliant op

t: `String.raw` corrupts null bytes in template literals
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10+30e609e08
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Create test.js with a literal null byte (0x00) between the backticks:
const s = String.raw``;
console.log("length:", s.length);
console.log("charCode[0]:", s.charCodeAt(0));
Run with bun test.js and node test.js.
What is the expected behavior?
length: 1
charCode[0]: 0

A null byte in a template literal should be preserved as-is, matching Node v22.22.0 behavior.
What do you see instead?
length: 6
charCode[0]: 92

Bun outputs the 6-character literal string \uFFFD (\, u, F, F, F, D) instead of a single null byte.
Additional information
Bun version: 1.3.10+30e609e08
Node version: v22.22.0 (reference)
Ran into this with wasm-audio-decoders, which uses simple-yenc to embed WASM binaries as yEncoded strings in template literals, decoded at runtime via String.raw. Every decoder (mpg123-decoder, flac, ogg-vorbis) failed with a CRC mismatch because null bytes in the payload were being corrupted by the transpiler.
Workaround was applied in simple-yenc (escape null bytes on encode, treat 0xFFFD as 0x00 on decode) but the root cause is in Bun.

What steps can reproduce the bug?
We run Bun HTTP servers inside Docker containers on AWS Lambda using Lambda Web Adapter (LWA), which forwards Lambda invocations as HTTP requests to a local server. The server uses:

Effect TS for composition
@libsql/client (Turso) which uses WebSockets internally
OpenAuth for OAuth2 token issuance

WORKDIR /app

t: Feature request: built-in VCR (record/replay) testing
b:
Feature request: built-in VCR (record/replay) testing
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Testing code that performs I/O (API calls, database queries, filesystem operations) currently requires either manual mocking or hitting real services in CI. Manual mocking is verbose, brittle, and requires knowing internal implementation details. Hitting real services is slow, flaky, and expensive.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
VCR testing — recording real I/O during an initial test run, then replaying it deterministically on subsequent runs. It's a well-established pattern (Ruby's VCR gem, Python's vcrpy, Go's go-vcr), but the JavaScript ecosystem has no great answer — existing options are userland libraries limited to HTTP interception.
Interface
A test.recorded qualifier, following the same pattern as test.skip, test.only, test.concurrent, etc.

First run: executes all I/O normally and saves a recording.
Subsequent runs: replays recorded I/O. Asserts that the sequence of calls and their arguments match the recording exactly. Fails if the code makes different I/O calls than what was recorded.

test.recorded chains with other qualifiers naturally: test.recorded.only(...), test.recorded.concurrent(...), etc. describe.recorded works too — all tests in the block are recorded.
CLI
Following the conventions established by snapshot testing:

bun test --update-recordings — re-record all recordings (parallel to --update-snapshots)
bun test --update-failing-recordings — re-record only tests whose replay assertions failed. This is especially valuable for VCR because re-recording means hitting real services, which is slow and potentially costly. This lets you run your full suite, see what's stale, then selectively re-record just the broken ones.

When a replay assertion fails, the error message could show what changed and suggest the fix:
Recording mismatch in "user service" at call 3:

  Expected: fetch("https://api.example.com/users")
  Received: fetch("https://api.example.com/users/active")

Re-record with: bun test -t "user service" --update-failing-recordings

Similar messages would appear for extra calls (test makes more calls than recorded) or missing calls (test finishes with unplayed recording entries). Note that recordings are orthogonal to snapshots — --update-snapshots and --update-recordings are independent flags.
Recording storage
Recordings live alongside tests, parallel to __snapshots__/:
tests/
├── api.test.ts
├── __recor

t: Severe Memory Retention (RSS) / OOMKilled in Next.js SSR with Bun, despite low JS Heap
b:
We are experiencing a critical issue with memory retention (RSS) when running a Next.js application (standalone mode, SSR/AMP pages) using Bun. Under production load, the RSS memory grows continuously until it hits the container's memory limits, resulting in an OOMKilled crash.
The JS Garbage Collector successfully cleans up the heap, but the underlying allocator (mimalloc) or JavaScriptCore fails to release the memory pages back to the OS.
Environment & Setup
Runtime: Bun 1.3.10+30e609e08

Framework: Next.js (Standalone build, Pages Router, dynamic AMP pages)
Deployment: Docker / Kubernetes
Container Limits:
requests: { memory: "1024Mi" }
limits: { memory: "1230Mi" }

Steps to Reproduce / Architecture Context
It is difficult to provide a minimal reproduction repository because the issue occurs under concurrent production traffic, but the pattern is consistent:

The server receives concurrent requests for hundreds of unique SSR/AMP pages.
The RSS spikes as expected during rendering.
When the load drops, the RSS does not drop.
With the next wave of traffic, RSS grows further until it hits 1230Mi, and Linux kills the process (OOMKilled - Code 137).

Proof that there is NO JavaScript Memory Leak
To isolate the issue, we manually triggered Bun.gc(true) and logged process.memoryUsage().
The logs clearly show that JS objects are successfully collected, and the heap shrinks significantly, but RSS remains locked:

t: .env not loaded in git worktrees — Bun resolves from cwd, not repo root
b:
Bun's automatic .env loading resolves relative to the current working directory. When running scripts in a git worktree, the working directory is a separate checkout that does not contain .env (since .env is typically gitignored), so environment variables silently fail to load.
Steps to reproduce
# Set up a repo with a .env file
mkdir test-repo && cd test-repo && git init
echo 'MY_VAR=hello' > .env
echo '{"name":"test","scripts":{"check":"bun run index.ts"}}' > package.json
echo 'console.log("MY_VAR:", process.env.MY_VAR)' > index.ts
git add -A && git commit -m "init"

# Works from repo root
bun run check
# Output: MY_VAR: hello

# Create a worktree and run from there
git worktree add ./wt -b test-branch
cd wt
bun run check
# Output: MY_VAR: undefined
Expected
Bun finds and loads .env from the git repo root (discoverable via git rev-parse --git-common-dir), even when cwd is a worktree.
Actual
.env is not loaded because it does not exist in the worktree directory.
Why this matters now
Tools like Claude Code use git worktrees to give AI agents isolated working copies of a repository. Since .env files are gitignored, they are never present in the worktree, and any Bun script that relies on automatic .env loading silently breaks. As AI-assisted development tools adopt worktrees more broadly, this will affect more users.
Related

#11190 (same root cause in monorepo context — .env at repo root not found from subdirectories)

t: bmalloc SYSCALL macro spins at 100% CPU on madvise EAGAIN — zero-delay retry loop
b:
Summary
bmalloc's SYSCALL and PAS_SYSCALL macros (from bundled WebKit) retry syscalls on EAGAIN in a zero-delay tight loop with no backoff. When madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP) returns EAGAIN under kernel mmap_write_lock contention, this causes 100% CPU usage across GC threads, effectively freezing the application.
Fix submitted: oven-sh/WebKit#169
Root Cause
Heavy allocation workload (e.g. LLM token streaming)
  → JSC allocation-triggered GC fires
  → GC sweep calls bmalloc vmDeallocatePhysicalPages() thousands of times
  → Each call does TWO madvise syscalls: MADV_DONTNEED + MADV_DONTDUMP
  → MADV_DONTDUMP requires kernel mmap_write_lock
     (unlike MADV_DONTNEED which only needs read lock)
  → Multiple GC threads contend on single process-wide mmap_write_lock
  → Kernel returns EAGAIN (VMA split/merge allocation failure under memory pressure)
  → SYSCALL macro retries in ZERO-DELAY infinite loop:
     while((x)==-1 && errno==EAGAIN){}
  → 250K+ madvise calls/sec/thread, 100% CPU, application frozen

The Bug (BSyscall.h line 30-32)
#define SYSCALL(x) do { \
    while ((x) == -1 && errno == EAGAIN) { } \
} while (0);
Zero backoff. No retry cap. Windows already has Sleep(50ms) + 10 max retries in virtual_alloc_with_retry() — POSIX has neither.
Evidence
Reproduced via strace -f -e trace=madvise:

250K+ madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP) calls per second per GC thread
All returning EAGAIN
3 threads spinning simultaneously on the same kernel lock
Application completely frozen during spin

BUN_GC_TIMER_INTERVAL is irrelevant — GC is allocation-triggered, not timer-triggered.
Proposed Fix
Add usleep(1000) backoff (1ms) and cap retries at 100 (100ms total). Submitted as draft PR on oven-sh/WebKit: oven-sh/WebKit#169
This matches:

Existing Windows precedent in virtual_alloc_with_retry() (same codebase)
Google tcmalloc's bounded retry pattern for expensive madvise operations
Red Hat's recommendation against sched_yield() for this use case

Likely Related Issues
These issues likely share this root cause or are exacerbated by it:

#17723 — Moving from Node to Bun spikes container CPU and memory usage (41 👍)
#27371 — OOM on trivial scripts
#27196 — OOMKilled on Prisma migrations (1.3.9 regression)
#26982 — Crash in bmalloc after ~73 minutes

Cross-Project References

google/tcmalloc#247 — madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) causing kernel interrupt storms (same kernel lock contention)
golang/go#61718 — MADV_HUGEPAGE causes 100+ ms stalls (same mmap_write_lock)
WebKit Bug #177839 — bmalloc mutex con

t: [Windows] N-API vtable corruption causes segfault, TUI escape, and orphaned processes in Bun v1.3.10
b:
Summary
Bun v1.3.10 (bundled with Claude Code / Anthropic CLI) has a critical N-API race condition on Windows that causes:

Segfaults at addresses 0x18, 0x7, 0x113, 0xFFFF (vtable corruption pattern)
TUI escape — terminal state machine dumps raw CSI focus reporting codes ([I[O[) and internal message buffers into the host shell as executable commands
Orphaned processes — crashed Bun processes stay alive, leak memory (1GB+ each), accumulate until system runs out of RAM
Full computer lockups — 5 hard reboots in 8 days from orphaned process memory exhaustion
Config file corruption — non-atomic writes during crash leave truncated JSON (280+ corruption events in one day)

Reproduction

Application: Claude Code (Anthropic CLI), which bundles Bun v1.3.10
Platform: Windows 11, x86_64 (MSYS2/Git Bash terminal)
Trigger: Extended sessions (30min+) with sub-agent spawning (multiple concurrent Bun child processes). Also occurs in single-process sessions after ~4-5 hours.
Frequency: 42 crashes in 33 days. 22+ crashes in a single day (Feb 25-26, 2026).

Steps to Reproduce

Run Claude Code on Windows with multiple concurrent sub-agent tasks
Wait 30-90 minutes
TUI escape occurs: [I[O[I[O[ dumped to terminal, session dies
Bun process stays alive with no window handle, consuming 400MB-1GB+ RAM
Repeat until system runs out of memory

Crash Variants Observed

panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x18 — most common
panic: switch on corrupt value — vtable corruption
SIGILL — illegal instruction (less common)
Silent TUI escape with no panic output (most frequent on Windows)

Root Cause Analysis
WinDbg analysis (posted on anthropics/claude-code#21875) points to N-API callback vtable corruption during concurrent TUI rendering + child process I/O. The crash site is in the N-API bridge between Bun's native runtime and the JavaScript TUI layer.
Community member @balandari identified the pattern: the vtable pointer is corrupted to point at an invalid address, causing the "switch on corrupt value" panic when the runtime tries to dispatch through it. This is consistent with a use-after-free or double-free in the N-API reference tracking.
Terminal State Corruption
When Bun crashes, it does NOT:

Exit the alternate screen buffer
Disable focus reporting (CSI ?1004l)
Restore terminal raw mode to cooked mode
Kill child processes / process group
Clean up ConPTY handles (Windows)

This means:

Focus reporting events ([I / [O) continue being sent to the dead terminal
Internal message

t: crypto.createPrivateKey(encrypted legacy RSA PEM) error poisons later Ed25519 private key parsing in same process
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10-debug+84e4a5ce9
Originally observed on Bun 1.3.9; still reproducible on a current local debug build.
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
I found this while debugging dotenc SSH key loading. A failed crypto.createPrivateKey() call on a legacy encrypted RSA PEM appears to poison later Ed25519 parsing in the same Bun process.
Standalone repro docs (permalink):

Repro write-up
Standalone repro script

Run:
bun /path/to/repro-bun-encrypted-rsa-poisons-ed25519.ts
In my local Bun repo debug build I ran:
bun bd /Users/ivanfilho/Projetos/dotenc/docs/bun-crypto-encrypted-rsa-poisons-ed25519/repro-bun-encrypted-rsa-poisons-ed25519.ts
What the script does:

Generates an unencrypted OpenSSH Ed25519 key (ssh-keygen).
Generates a legacy encrypted RSA PEM key (ssh-keygen -m PEM -N pass123).
Parses the Ed25519 key via a custom OpenSSH parser that reconstructs PKCS#8 DER and calls crypto.createPrivateKey({ key: der, format: "der", type: "pkcs8" }).
Calls crypto.createPrivateKey(encryptedLegacyRsaPem) and expects a passphrase-required error.
Parses the same Ed25519 key again in the same process.

The script exits 1 if the bug reproduces, 0 otherwise.
What is the expected behavior?
Step 4 should still throw a passphrase-required error for the encrypted RSA PEM, but step 5 should continue to succeed.
A failed crypto.createPrivateKey() on an encrypted legacy RSA PEM should not affect later key imports/parsing in the same process.
What do you see instead?
After the encrypted RSA PEM import throws, the second Ed25519 parse fails unexpectedly — and it fails with the same passphrase error message, which is itself a strong signal that the OpenSSL error queue is not being cleared after the encrypted-PEM error path.
Observed output on 1.3.10-debug:
runtime: bun 1.3.10-debug
sequence: parse OpenSSH ed25519 -> crypto.createPrivateKey(encrypted legacy RSA PEM) throws -> parse OpenSSH ed25519 again
parse before encrypted RSA error: {
  ok: true,
  type: "ed25519",
}
encrypted RSA import error: Passphrase required for encrypted key
parse after encrypted RSA error: {
  ok: false,
  error: "Passphrase required for encrypted key",
}
BUG REPRODUCED: Bun failed to parse the same OpenSSH ed25519 key after a thrown crypto.createPrivateKey(encrypted RSA PEM) call.

The repro script exits with code 1.
Additional information
This affects dotenc because it scans multiple keys in ~/.ssh and may encounter legac

t: Ability to change proxy settings from typescript
Replace master/slave terminology in PTY code with inclusive alternatives
b:
Summary
Bun's PTY/Terminal implementation uses master/slave terminology extensively. The industry-standard inclusive alternatives are host/client, primary/replica, or controller/worker (POSIX itself is moving toward ptm/pts or simply avoiding the terms). This issue proposes updating the terminology in Bun-authored code to use inclusive alternatives.
Locations
PTY / Terminal code (master/slave)
src/bun.js/api/bun/Terminal.zig (~20 instances)

Field names: master_fd, slave_fd
Struct field: PtyResult.master, PtyResult.slave
Functions: getSlaveFd(), closeSlaveFd()
Comments: "PTY master/slave pair", "The master side of the PTY", "The slave side of the PTY", "Close slave fd", "EOF from master"

src/bun.js/api/bun/process.zig

Comment: "PTY slave fd for controlling terminal setup"
Comment: "Pass PTY slave fd to attr for controlling terminal setup"

src/bun.js/bindings/bun-spawn.cpp

Variable: pty_slave_fd
Comments: "slave fd to set as controlling terminal", "Set PTY slave as controlling terminal"

src/bun.js/api/bun/js_bun_spawn_bindings.zig

User-facing error message: "terminal slave fd is no longer valid"

test/js/bun/terminal/terminal.test.ts

Comment: "each terminal uses ~4 fds: master, read, write, slave"

packages/bun-uws/misc/READMORE.md

Documentation: "master/slave set-ups"

Whitelist/blacklist (minor)
docs/runtime/archive.mdx

Code comment: "Whitelist specific directories" — could be "Allowlist specific directories"

Suggested replacements



Current
Suggested




master_fd
host_fd


slave_fd
child_fd or client_fd


getSlaveFd()
getChildFd()


closeSlaveFd()
closeChildFd()


PtyResult.master
PtyResult.host


PtyResult.slave
PtyResult.child


"PTY master/slave pair"
"PTY host/child pair" or "pseudo-terminal pair"


pty_slave_fd
pty_child_fd


"Whitelist"
"Allowlist"



The host/child pairing works particularly well for PTY since the "slave" side is literally used by the child process.

What steps can reproduce the bug?
Minimal reproduction repo - https://github.com/DashwoodIce9/bun-bug-bundle
When installing a dependency (PackageA) that includes bundled dependencies (PackageB via bundleDependencies field in PackageA's package.json), Bun fetches the package manifest of the bundled dependencies (PackageB) from NPM registry.
$> bun install --verbose --no-cache --dry-run PackageA
.

Enqueue package manifest for download: PackageB
[fetch] > HTTP/1.1 GET https://registry.npmjs.org/PackageB
.
.
.
[fetch] < 404 Not Found

This behavior differs from npm which doesn't contact the NPM registry for bundled dependencies.
This causes issues in an edge case wherein bundled dependency (PackageB) was present in the NPM registry used by the author of PackageA but isn't present in the registry configured for use in my package. Bun would try to fetch PackageB's manifest from the NPM registry configured for my package, fail to find PackageB there, and fail the install.
npm install does not have this issue.
You can see the difference in install behaviors of bun and npm in the README of the reproduction repo.
My workplace uses custom internal NPM registries so this prevents me from using Bun there.

Don't contact NPM registry for bundled dependencies.

Bun attempts to fetch the package manifest of bundled dependencies from the configured NPM registry.

This is intermittent (same command may succeed or fail on the same machine).
Environment:

macOS 26.2 (25C56) Apple Silicon
Node v22.20.0
Bun 1.2.23 (this is the initial version, also tested on latest 1.3.9 — no change in behavior)

Steps:


bun install


Run Convex dev (any of these):
bunx convex@1.32.0 dev --once --verbose --typecheck disable --codegen disable --tail-logs disable
bunx convex@1.32.0 dev --run-sh "bunx --bun next dev"


When it fails, macOS writes crash reports for esbuild under:

~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/esbuild-*.ips



Excerpt from one report:
procName : "esbuild"
parentProc : "node"
exception : ... "signal":"SIGKILL (Code Signature Invalid)"
os_version : "macOS 26.2 (25C56)"

Notes about the esbuild binary in node_modules:

node_modules/@esbuild/darwin-arm64/bin/esbuild and node_modules/esbuild/bin/esbuild are hardlinked (links=2)
xattr shows com.apple.provenance present
codesign -vvv --verify .../esbuild reports valid on disk even when runtime kill occurs

Workaround that makes it reliable:
cp node_modules/@esbuild/darwin-arm64/bin/esbuild /tmp/convex-esbuild
chmod 755 /tmp/convex-esbuild
ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH=/tmp/convex-esbuild bunx convex@1.32.0 dev --once --typecheck disable --codegen disable --tail-logs disable
What is the expected behavior?
convex dev reliably starts and reaches "Convex functions ready!" every run.
What do you see instead?
Intermittently:

convex dev hangs at "Preparing Convex functions...", or
✖ esbuild failed: Error: The service was stopped: write EPIPE

And macOS crash reports show esbuild was killed: SIGKILL (Code Signature Invalid).
Additional information
I tried to reproduce outside Convex with standalone esbuild API loops and direct esbuild CLI loops and could not trigger the crash. It seems specific to the Convex dev invocation path, but the OS crash report is for esbuild itself.
This might be:

a macOS 26.x code signing/provenance interaction with binaries under node_modules, or
something about Bun’s install/linking strategy for native executables (hardlink/clonefile) that can result in runtime “Code Signature Invalid” kills.

t: [Feature Request] Support configuring test runner `bail` option in bunfig.toml
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, the --bail flag (which makes the test runner stop after a set number of test failures) cannot be configured in bunfig.toml. This means users always have to specify --bail on the CLI and cannot centrally manage this setting in their configuration like they can with other test options (randomize, retry, rerunEach, etc.). For teams relying on bunfig.toml for CI consistency and easy onboarding, this is a limitation.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Allow the bail (or equivalent) option to be set in bunfig.toml under the [test] section, so test runner bail behavior can be configured centrally and shared across environments. Ideally, both the number of allowed failures before bailing and whether bailing is on/off can be set with bail = N (matching the CLI flag).
What alternatives have you considered?

Manually passing --bail on the CLI for every run (easy to forget)
Using standalone wrapper scripts or package.json scripts (does not scale well for large teams or CI/CD)
Documenting the flag in team README (not as robust or enforceable as configuration)

t: Bun SQL: Sequential `await sql.unsafe()` calls hang forever on remote TCP connections
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.9
What platform is your computer?
windows 11
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Bun version: (fill in your version)
OS: Windows / Linux (reproducible on both)
Database: Remote MySQL over TCP (does NOT reproduce with localhost/Unix socket)

Problem
When making sequential await sql.unsafe() calls against a remote MySQL server (real TCP latency), a later call in the sequence hangs forever — the Promise never resolves and never rejects. No error is thrown, no timeout fires. The process simply freezes silently.
This does not happen with a local MySQL server (127.0.0.1 or Unix socket).

Minimal Reproduction
const sql = new SQL({
  adapter: "mysql",
  hostname: "remote-host",  // ← must be remote, non-localhost
  port: 3306,
  database: "mydb",
  username: "root",
  password: "password",
  max: 10
});

await sql`SELECT 1`; // warmup / connection

// These calls are sequential (not concurrent)
await sql.unsafe("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM table_a");  // ✅ resolves
await sql.unsafe("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM table_a");  // ✅ resolves
await sql.unsafe("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM table_b");  // ❌ hangs forever
The hang consistently occurs around the 3rd–4th sequential call, always on a remote TCP connection. The exact call that hangs may vary but is always reproducible.

Investigation
Through extensive binary search debugging, we ruled out:

❌ Redis (removing all Redis calls did not fix it)
❌ Table locks (confirmed via information_schema.INNODB_TRX)
❌ Data issues (hardcoded queries to the same tables worked fine)
❌ Connection pool size (max: 10 is set, confirmed in config)
❌ setImmediate after each query (no effect)
❌ await Promise.resolve() after each query (no effect)
❌ .then(r => r) chaining (no effect)
❌ new Promise((resolve, reject) => nativePromise.then(resolve, reject)) (no effect)
❌ await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0)) after the query (no effect)

Only one thing fixes it: having a setTimeout registered in the event loop before the sql.unsafe() call is made:
// ✅ Works — timer registered BEFORE the query
const timer = setTimeout(() => {}, 999999);
try {
  result = await sql.unsafe(sql_string);
} finally {
  clearTimeout(timer);
}
Key observations:

The setTimeout duration is irrelevant (1ms, 15000ms, 999999ms all work equally)
The timer never fires — the query always completes well within the timeout
The timer must be registered before sql.unsafe() is called, not after
All microtask-based workarounds (Promise.resolve(), .then(), new Promis

t: Memory leak in fetch() with TLS client certificates (mTLS)
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.9

What platform is your computer?
Linux x86_64 (Docker: oven/bun:1.3.9)

What steps can reproduce the bug?
git clone https://github.com/slucascosta/bun-mtls-memory-leak.git
cd bun-mtls-memory-leak
docker compose up --build
3 tests run against a local HTTPS server:

test-http -- HTTPS fetch without client cert (control)
test-mtls -- HTTPS fetch with client cert via tls option (leaks)
test-node-mtls -- Same as 2 but in Node.js 24 (control)

Each test: 3 rounds x 10,000 requests @ 100 req/s, with Bun.gc(true) + 5s pause between rounds.
Minimal reproduction
import fs from "fs";

const cert = fs.readFileSync("data/certs/server.crt", "utf-8");
const key = fs.readFileSync("data/certs/server.key", "utf-8");

for (let round = 1; round <= 3; round++) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 10_000; i++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch("https://localhost:8443/", {
        tls: { cert, key, rejectUnauthorized: false },
      });
      await res.text();
    } catch {}
  }
  Bun.gc(true);
  await Bun.sleep(5000);
  const m = process.memoryUsage();
  console.log(`Round ${round}: RSS=${Math.round(m.rss / 1024 / 1024)}MB`);
}
// RSS grows ~35MB per round and is never reclaimed.
What is the expected behavior?
RSS should remain stable across rounds. Certificates are loaded once, response bodies are fully consumed, and GC is explicitly called between rounds.
What do you see instead?
RSS grows linearly with each fetch() that uses the tls option and is never reclaimed.



Test
Runtime
Requests
RSS growth
Leak?




HTTPS (no client cert)
Bun 1.3.9
30,000
+20MB
No


HTTPS + client cert (tls)
Bun 1.3.9

+109MB
Yes


HTTPS + client cert
Node.js 24.13.1
30,000
+22MB
No




The only difference between test-http and test-mtls is { tls: { cert, key } } in fetch options
Heap stays at 1MB -- the leak is in native memory, not JS heap
The leak is linear: ~3.6KB/request (~36MB per 10k requests)
Node.js with the same workload does not leak

Suspected root cause
Each fetch() call with a tls option appears to allocate a new native SSL context that is never freed. Consistent with unreleased BoringSSL SSL_CTX or SSL objects.

t: fetch() hangs indefinitely on HTTPS connections in Docker on VM with VXLAN
b:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.9+cf6cdbbba
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.12.68 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run a Bun process inside a Docker container using bridge networking (default compose setup)
The container's network path has an effective MTU < 1500 (PMTUD blackhole — ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages are not forwarded into the container namespace)
Make an HTTPS fetch() to any server that sends a TLS Certificate larger than the path MTU

fetch('https://any-internal-server.example.com', {
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30000)
})
Ubuntu on Proxmox VM, VXLAN SDN, effective path MTU = 1450
What is the expected behavior?

Detect the interface MTU and set a max accordingly before initiating connections, so the remote server's response segments stay within the path MTU
Or implement tcp_mtu_probing-style fallback: after a connection stalls mid-handshake, retry with progressively smaller MSS values

What do you see instead?
fetch() hangs indefinitely. TCP connects, TLS ClientHello is sent, server Certificate is sent back in segments that exceed the path MTU, segments are silently dropped, connection stalls. No error, no timeout (unless AbortSignal is set manually).
Additional information
Temp fixes that work:

Set docker network MTU to 1450
MSS clamping on host: sudo iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
Increase MTU across the network and allow jumbo frames

t: Flaky SIGILL crash in JSC garbage collector during `bun test` on Linux x64 (1.3.7 and 1.3.9)
b:
How can we reproduce the crash?
This crash is intermittent and non-deterministic. It occurs during bun test on GitHub Actions (ubuntu-latest) with roughly 60–65% frequency across 30+ observed CI runs. The same commit passes on retry without any changes.
Environment:

Runner: ubuntu-latest (Linux Kernel 6.11.0, glibc 2.39)
CPU: sse42 popcnt avx avx2
Machine memory: 16.77 GB
Bun versions tested: v1.3.7 (ba426210) and v1.3.9 (cf6cdbbb) — same crash on both

Setup:

Monorepo with 22 TypeScript packages, using Turborepo for orchestration
CI runs bun run verify:ci which builds, typechecks, lints, and tests all packages via Turbo
The crash always occurs in the same package's test suite (the CLI app, which has the heaviest tests)
All tests pass before the crash — the panic happens during process cleanup/GC, not during test execution

CI workflow (minimal):
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
    with:
      bun-version-file: .bun-version
  - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
  - run: bun run verify:ci
Test characteristics of the crashing suite (~8 tests):

Creates temp directories with mkdtempSync, writes TypeScript files, runs analysis, cleans up with rmSync
Patches process.stdout.write / process.stderr.write for output capture (restored in finally)
Uses spyOn(Bun, "spawn").mockImplementation(...) in one test
Total elapsed time: ~5–6s for the suite
Peak RSS at crash: 0.40–0.43 GB (well within 16 GB machine)

Frequency data from 30 consecutive CI runs on main (all running the same code):

19 failures (63%), 11 successes (37%)
Failures and successes are interleaved — the same commit hash appears in both pass and fail runs
Retrying a failed run succeeds without any code changes

Why this is not our code:

All tests pass before the crash — Bun reports "N pass, 0 fail" then panics
The crash is in JSC's garbage collector (SlotVisitor::drain), not in user code
Same commit passes on retry
Crash occurs on both Bun 1.3.7 and 1.3.9 with identical stack traces
No floating point operations in our test code — this is purely string/JSON/filesystem work
Bun's own crash message says "This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code"

Minimal reproduction is difficult because the crash is non-deterministic and may depend on GC timing, heap layout, or Turbo's parallel scheduling. We can provide access to the repository if that would help the Bun team investigate.

t: Detect and optionally remove unused package.json dependencies from source imports
b:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun does not currently provide a built-in way to keep package.json dependencies aligned with what is actually imported in source code. In practice, dependencies accumulate over time and become stale, especially in monorepos and fast-moving apps.
We currently need third-party tools like Knip/depcheck plus manual bun remove, which adds complexity and inconsistency to Bun-first workflows.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Go, being an example for great tooling ecosystem (IMHO) has a go mod tidy command, which makes sure go.mod is aligned with what's actually in the code. I wish Bun had the same feature.
What alternatives have you considered?
Using Knip/depcheck + manual bun remove works, but it is extra tooling and less integrated with Bun’s own resolver and workspace model. Also these tools can produce a lot of false-positives.

What platform is your computer?
